# analog-guest

This is the messaging engine for Analog — a guest recognition platform for independent cafes, bakeries, and restaurants. This repo handles inbound and outbound messages between venues and their guests, plus the AI generation, classification, and routing logic. It also hosts the internal Command Center (`app/admin/*`) — the Analog-staff debugging surface served on `admin.theanalog.company`. A separate venue-operator dashboard (`analog-operator`) is planned but not yet built; bearer-token auth scaffolding for that future repo lives in `lib/auth/` (see "Auth boundary" below).

---

## Keeping this file current

This file is the source of truth for how the codebase works. When shipping a new script, migration, schema convention, file-naming convention, library pattern, or workflow rule, update this file in the same commit. If a future-you (or a future Claude Code session) would have to rediscover the convention, document it here.

---

## Product principles (do not violate)

- **Recognition, not loyalty.** Guests do not "earn" things — they get recognized. Avoid loyalty-program language ("points," "rewards," "tier," "earn") in any guest-facing output, system prompts, or operator-facing UI copy.
- **Speaker framing is per-venue.** Messages to guests can come from a few different framings depending on what the venue approves: from the venue itself (default), from a named person at the venue ("[Name] from [Venue]"), or from the owner directly when the owner approves that framing. The default is venue-level until told otherwise per venue.
- **Every venue is its own isolated block.** Own messaging number, own voice corpus, own config, own data. Cross-venue queries are Analog-internal only and never exposed to operators.
- **The product is messaging-only.** There is no guest app. Do not assume a frontend for guests. The guest's only surface is the iMessage/SMS conversation with the venue.
- **Voice is the product.** The agent's response style, register, and judgment are what we sell. Treat voice quality as a first-class concern, not a polish-later detail.

---

## Tech stack

- **Language:** TypeScript, strict mode
- **App framework:** Next.js (App Router) deployed on Vercel
- **Database:** Postgres with pgvector, plus Auth and Storage (Supabase as the current provider)
- **Messaging:** iMessage + SMS fallback (Sendblue as the current provider). One dedicated number per venue. Inbound webhook: `webhooks.theanalog.company/api/webhooks/sendblue` (configured Sendblue-side; route handler at `app/api/webhooks/sendblue/route.ts`). Future webhook integrations (Square, Stripe, Toast) inherit this subdomain convention. **Instagram DM is a second inbound channel as of TAC-445** (Meta app, Instagram Login path — `graph.instagram.com` and an Instagram User token, never `graph.facebook.com` or a Page token), handler at `app/api/webhooks/instagram/route.ts`, callback `webhooks.theanalog.company/api/webhooks/instagram`. **Since TAC-468 it saves what arrives**, into the schema TAC-467 added (migration 048): a guest message or icebreaker postback becomes an inbound row, and the venue account's echo an outbound row, all with `channel: 'instagram'` set explicitly; the guest is found or created by `(venue_id, instagram_scoped_id)`; the venue comes from `venues.instagram_account_id`, which has **no write path and is set by hand in Studio**. Until it is set, every delivery is skipped as `venue_not_found`, so the feature saves nothing. The value is the webhook's `entry.id`, which no log line carries (TAC-458): get it with the venue's Instagram User token from `GET https://graph.instagram.com/me?fields=user_id,username`, taking `user_id`, NOT `id` (which is app-scoped). Confirm the mapping by the logs: `instagram_event_skipped` stops and `instagram_event_persisted` appears. A read receipt is matched to its row and logged, never written, because no column holds read state. It has the Sendblue route's shape (save, answer 200, hand a new guest message to the agent via `waitUntil`), and **since TAC-469's PR C (2026-09-20) the agent RUNS for Instagram guests**: `INSTAGRAM_AGENT_REPLIES_ENABLED` in `lib/messaging/instagram/agent-gate.ts` is `true`. Outbound is "Instagram outbound (TAC-469)" under the runtime contract; the flip was made alone and last so a rollback is a one-line revert of that constant and nothing else, and `agent-gate.test.ts` pins it at true while keeping the shut behaviour covered through the `enabled` parameter, because that is what a rollback restores. **STOP is handled only by the classifier inside that agent run**, which the flip turns on — so an Instagram guest's opt-out is now classified, but it is still not RECORDED anywhere (TAC-475 has no writer for `guests.opted_out_at`, verified 2026-09-20: the one row fleet-wide carrying it was set by hand in Studio), so PR B still records a follow-up task for a guest who has said stop. Every Instagram inbound row was read before the flip and none was an opt-out; a STOP sent as a voice note or sticker would have been invisible to that read, since those are logged and not saved. **The daily webhook-silence alarm (`app/api/cron/webhook-silence`) counts `channel = 'text'` inbound only since TAC-468**, so it watches Sendblue alone; without that filter one Instagram DM a day would hide a complete Sendblue outage. Instagram has no silence check of its own. **The `x-hub-signature-256` signature is ENFORCED as of TAC-458**: a delivery that fails it, and every delivery while `INSTAGRAM_APP_SECRET` is unset or empty, gets 403 with nothing from its body logged. That is the route's only non-2xx. A verified delivery gets 200 on every path including a parse failure and an unhandled throw (so does a throw while reading the body, which logs nothing from it), where Sendblue and Square reserve 5xx so the provider retries. **Since TAC-468 that includes a failed save, which loses that event** (ruled 2026-09-18): Meta disables a subscription after repeated non-2xx, and a failure that isn't transient would keep failing until the channel switched off with no alert. Sendblue loses messages the same way in practice, because supabase-js returns a network failure as `{ error }` rather than throwing, so its route 200s on a failed insert too. The same fact cuts the other way for the 403: **if GENUINE deliveries start getting it, Meta will eventually disable the subscription and nothing here alerts** (see the env-var entry). A rotated or cleared secret is the likely cause; fix the secret or revert rather than debug in place. **Since TAC-479 every saved Instagram row carries `provider_sent_at`** (migration 049): Instagram's own time for the event, from the `messaging[]` item's `timestamp`, never `entry.time`, which is when Meta sent the delivery. TAC-469's window gate and TAC-486's countdown read it; nothing that reads `created_at` switched, because history sorts on one clock across both channels. **The guest's handle and display name are fetched after the 200** (`guests.instagram_username` / `instagram_name`, `lib/messaging/instagram/refresh-profile.ts`) with `INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN`, the one theanalog.company token until per-venue tokens exist (Phase 3, TAC-460). **So when a second venue connects, every message from its guests logs `instagram_profile_wrong_account` until tokens are per venue.** That is deliberate: the refresh compares the token's own account with the venue's before fetching, so the failure is never mistaken for Meta or a guest's privacy.
- **LLM:** Anthropic API via the Vercel AI SDK abstraction layer (model-agnostic from day one)
- **Embeddings:** Voyage
- **Drive integration:** Google Drive + Sheets API for the venue onboarding artifact pipeline (06-09 files described below)
- **Analytics:** PostHog for product/event analytics, Slack for operational alerts

Treat the database, messaging, and LLM providers as swappable. Code should depend on internal interfaces (e.g., `lib/messaging/send.ts`), not on vendor names.

## Brand & design

The Analog visual language is documented in `docs/brand/style-guide-v01.html`. Open in a browser to view rendered. It defines:

- Color tokens (clay, paper, parchment, ink variants, stone variants) with hex values in the `:root` CSS block
- Typography stack: **Fraunces** (variable serif — display + italic-display, with brand-default `opsz/SOFT/WONK` variation settings in `--fraunces` and `--fraunces-text`) and **Inter Tight** (variable sans — body, UI, eyebrows with `letter-spacing: 0.22em`, captions). No script face — every italic-display moment resolves through Fraunces.
- Voice register guidance ("Tone continuum" section — Composed / Direct / Quiet, with surface-by-surface mapping)
- Layout primitives (eyebrows, section headers, hairline borders, tabular nums for receipt-shaped data)

The file is reference material, not code. Do not modify it. Brand updates land as a new versioned file (v02, v03, etc.) so the canonical reference for any given moment is pinned.

Token extraction into runtime code happens in `app/globals.css` under `@theme inline` (Tailwind v4 — no separate config file) — set up during THE-198 (Command Center scaffold).

## Folder layout

### App and library code

- `app/api/` — route handlers (webhooks, internal API for operator)
- `lib/db/` — database clients and queries (currently backed by Supabase). `lib/db/admin.ts` exports `createAdminClient` for service-role access in scripts and crons.
- `lib/messaging/` — message send + receive + webhook verification (currently backed by Sendblue). `instagram/` (TAC-445) holds the Meta half, in a provider subfolder mirroring `lib/pos/square/` and imported BY PATH, since sub-barrels are not the convention here and a barrel is what lets a future `vi.mock` hand a test a stubbed verifier it needed for real. `verify-webhook.ts` is pure (secret passed in, never read from env) so it is testable with known vectors — **note it does NOT reuse `lib/messaging/verify-webhook.ts`, which is Sendblue's and is not HMAC at all**: Sendblue echoes its secret in plaintext in an `sb-signing-secret` header, so the reusable precedent is Square's. `verifyInstagramSignature` returns ok or a rejection reason and NEVER the computed digest, and refuses an empty secret itself rather than relying on the route (see the signing-oracle gotcha). `summarize-payload.ts` is the non-PII shape summary; since TAC-458 removed the raw-body capture it and `logInstagramOutcome` (below) are the only things the route logs about a payload, so they are what hold "no guest content in logs". **TAC-468 added the handler, in three files.** `parse-events.ts` is pure: a verified delivery becomes typed events in delivery order (Meta batches `entry[] × messaging[]`), told apart by the item's own keys (`message` with or without `is_echo`, `postback`, `read`), with the guest taken from the RECIPIENT on an echo. Everything else (comments and other `changes[]` fields, `standby`, reactions, edits, handover, unsends, unsupported or empty messages, a standalone `referral` whose ref is therefore lost, and any entry key besides `id`/`time`/`messaging`/`changes`/`standby`) becomes an `unhandled` event carrying key names, never values, and is logged and acknowledged, never dropped silently. `handle-events.ts` saves them, one at a time and each in its own try/catch, following the Sendblue order (venue, guest, duplicate check on `provider_message_id` = the `mid`, insert). Only a guest's own message or postback creates a guest; an echo or a read for an unknown IGSID is skipped (ruled 2026-09-18), so staff messaging a supplier from the venue account creates no "guest". **A new guest is `created_via: 'qr_scan'` when the event creating them carries a referral whose `source` is `SHORTLINK`, and `'inbound_message'` otherwise (TAC-492, ruled 2026-09-18).** SHORTLINK is Meta's own statement that the thread was opened from an ig.me link, which is what the venue's QR code is, and it is the whole signal: the icebreaker `payload` is never read (a label we chose, which can drift, TAC-455), `ref` isn't required, and a typed first message carrying the referral counts like a postback (never observed; device QA). `created_via` is the carrier because the opener (`computeFirstTouchAfterQrScan`) and `understand_order`'s arming already read it, so an Instagram QR guest gets exactly what a Sendblue QR guest gets and only the detection differs. Sendblue's `resolveCreatedVia` is separate and stays so; `app/api/webhooks/sendblue/route.test.ts` pins it. Only creation sets it, as on Sendblue. Any ig.me link counts, including one shared online. A staff reply typed in the Instagram app before the agent reads the thread turns the opener off, and that is intended, not a gap: a person already greeted the guest. **The icebreaker titles are the one input nothing can test**: a title naming a menu item drops `understand_order`'s line on the opener turn and sends the turn to the order extractor, and a question-shaped title gives the model two instructions that disagree (the opener says answer instead of asking what they got; the block's first natural opening allows one question after an answer), so what it does has to be measured. Checking them is a named TAC-469 pre-flight item, listed in `agent-gate.ts`, and it recurs whenever the copy or the menu changes. Since TAC-495 an Instagram guest gets the opener's Instagram variant, which drops "on this number" and says "messaging" for "texting"; "at pickup" and the rest of its presence language are shared with Sendblue, by ruling (see *Channel copy* under the runtime contract). A postback is saved even without a title, because TAC-469 computes the 24-hour reply window from the newest inbound Instagram row and a postback opens it (the row is legal only through the TAC-309 NULL quirk in `messages_has_content`). A guest message with nothing to show (unsupported, or no text and no attachment URL) is logged, not saved, as approved: it creates no guest and doesn't count toward the window, which TAC-469 should revisit if that refuses replies it could send. `created_at` is our receipt time, not Meta's `timestamp`, so the window computation needs a margin. A racing guest insert re-reads the winner on 23505, and a racing message insert reads as a duplicate. Echo rows are shaped like `sendReaction`'s outbound insert (status `sent`, no `review_state`, no `generated_by`). `logInstagramOutcome` logs our row IDs, flags and names, plus a failed save's PostgREST message and code; never its `details`, which carry the failing row's values. `agent-gate.ts` holds `INSTAGRAM_AGENT_REPLIES_ENABLED` and, since TAC-523, `resolveAgentHandoff` — which REPLACED `agentMessageIdFor`'s `string | null`, because the null was the whole problem: the route discarded it, so a delivery the agent never saw left nothing behind. It returns `run` / `record` / `not_a_turn`, total over `InstagramEventOutcome`'s six statuses, and `record-turn.ts` writes the row. **The echo check runs BEFORE the gate check**: reversed, a shut gate would report the venue's own messages as dropped guest turns and the incident count would be nonsense. The route's `waitUntil(runInboundAgent(...))` call sits behind it, and since TAC-469's PR C the constant is `true`. **`unhandled` is split by reason**: `message_unsupported` and `message_no_content` are guest messages saved nowhere, so they record as `message_unrenderable`; reactions, edits, handover, comments, standalone referrals and a message the guest unsent are not turns. Its kind check is NOT part of the gate and stays: an echo, a read, or a duplicate is never handed to the agent, or the agent would answer its own replies once they echo back. **Echoes race TAC-469's own sends, and nothing orders the two.** The send path learns the `mid` only from the Send API's response, and Meta can deliver the echo first. When it does, this handler saves the echo as an outbound row with no agent metadata, and the send path's own write of that `mid` then hits 23505 on `provider_message_id`. TAC-469 handles it rather than assuming an order: an agent send whose insert collides fills in that echo row, and an operator send folds the echo into the card (see "Instagram outbound (TAC-469)"). What the shut gate hid, and where each item stands (the titleless postback now skips the agent; unsent messages accepted; STOPs and the live icebreaker titles are manual checks before the flip), is in `agent-gate.ts`'s header. `testing/db-fake.ts` is the in-memory store both test files use; like `lib/agent/testing/pending-rows-fake.ts` it answers only the query shapes the handler sends, so an update (say, on a read receipt) throws. `fixtures/` holds real Meta deliveries captured on 2026-09-17 (a guest message, an echo, a read receipt, and an icebreaker postback carrying an `ig.me` referral), with IDs, `mid`s and text replaced because the repo is public. Its README and `fixtures.test.ts` record what they show, and each point is a test: **a reply typed by hand in the Instagram app arrives as an echo** (`is_echo: true` inside `message`, sender and recipient reversed), so a handler will see venue staff's own messages. `is_echo` marks the venue's side, not staff: the agent's own API sends most likely arrive as echoes too (uncaptured; verify when the real handler lands); **a read receipt's key is `read`** (`messaging_seen` is only the subscription field name) and it names one `mid`, so read state is per message; the two guest IGSIDs seen were 16 digits where the account ID is 17, so the two kinds of ID don't share a length; a `mid` encodes the account, conversation and message IDs; **an icebreaker tap after an `ig.me` link is a `postback` carrying the referral**, with the link's `ref` unchanged in the one sample and the `mid` inside `postback` (a hand transcription put it outside; copy fixtures from the logs by script, never by hand); and **a thread the guest deleted on their side and reopened through the link got a referral but kept its thread ID** (expected: Instagram deletes a chat only for the side that deletes it, so the venue still had it), so on that path the referral, not a new thread, is what signals a returning guest (other re-entry paths weren't captured). Never commit a delivery's signature beside its body. **TAC-469 added the outbound half here**: `send.ts` (the Send API, `POST /{instagram_account_id}/messages`, with the 1000-byte cap), `window.ts` (the 24-hour window on Meta's clock and `INSTAGRAM_WINDOW_MARGIN_MS`), `reply-check.ts` (has this guest message already been answered), `send-target.ts` (account, IGSID and token, never `messaging_phone_number`) and `graph.ts` (the Graph request path, moved out of `fetch-profile.ts`, which re-exports its old names). Only the two Instagram arms may import them, `lib/agent/dispatch-instagram-reply.ts` and `lib/operator/dispatch-instagram-outbound.ts`; `window-import-guard.test.ts` enforces it. `testing/query-recorder.ts` records every query-builder call so their tests can assert on the filters, not on a mock's opinion of them. **TAC-473 added `resolve-external.ts`**: a reply staff typed in the Instagram app clears the card it answered. `externalResolutionTargetFor` is the pure selector (only a NEWLY PERSISTED echo — a `duplicate` is a redelivery or one of our own sends being reconciled), and the route hands `resolveCardAnsweredExternally` to `waitUntil` beside the agent hand-off and the profile refresh. **THE STRUCTURAL GUARD, which is the whole mechanism: an echo arriving while the window is EXPIRED cannot be one of our own sends**, because every send we make is gated on the window being OPEN (`prepareInstagramOperatorSend` and the agent arm both refuse a closed one). Nothing in an echo itself distinguishes ours from staff's — an agent send racing its own echo has not written its `mid` yet — so relaxing this into "an echo arrived, clear a card" would let the agent silently close its own cards. It uses Meta's TRUE deadline with no margin: subtracting the margin makes the expired set LARGER, and the margin window is exactly where one of our sends could still be in flight. **Several cards resolve exactly ONE, the OLDEST** (FIFO, the order the queue shows them): one send, one card, and resolving too few leaves a stale card an operator can skip while resolving too many silently drops a question the guest asked. Instagram cards only, since a reply typed in Instagram does not answer a card queued for SMS. Known hole, stated not fixed: `prepareInstagramOperatorSend` does not refuse when the window READ fails, so a send could go out with the window actually closed and its echo could resolve another expired card. **TAC-479 added the profile refresh, in two files.** `fetch-profile.ts` is the Graph client: `GET /{igsid}?fields=username,name` and `GET /me?fields=user_id`. The fetch and the token are passed in. The token goes in the `Authorization` header, never the URL, and a failure carries Meta's error code, subcode, type and `fbtrace_id` but NEVER its message, which quotes the scoped ID. `refresh-profile.ts` is handed to `waitUntil` by the route, once per guest with a saved message or postback in a delivery, and never awaited. A refresh is due when the profile was never fetched or is over 24 hours old, and nothing was tried in the last hour (both placeholders). It then checks the token's own account (`/me`) against `venues.instagram_account_id`, claims by setting `instagram_profile_attempted_at` only if it still holds the value it read, fetches, and writes only `instagram_username`, `instagram_name` and `instagram_profile_fetched_at`. **The display name never goes into `first_name`** (ruled 2026-09-18): the agent would greet the guest by a name they never gave the venue, and `learn_name` would close on it. A failed fetch keeps the stored handle. Four failures have their own events so none reads as another: `instagram_profile_token_missing`, `instagram_profile_token_rejected` (Meta code 190) and `instagram_profile_wrong_account`, all error level; and `instagram_profile_fetch_failed` (warn: a privacy refusal, a block, a timeout, a bad response). The three configuration failures are found before the claim, so each repeats on every message until fixed; the one exception is a 190 on the profile call itself, which comes after the claim and so waits the hour like any other failed fetch. A failed `/me` call is also before the claim and is NOT throttled: it is retried on every message, which at a wrong-account venue is what keeps it loud. `testing/db-fake.ts` answers `update` only on the tables a test names in `updatable`, so the handler's own tests still throw on any update. The Command Center shows `@handle` where it showed `NO_PHONE_LABEL`, and nowhere else (`app/admin/(authed)/_lib/guest-name.ts`); `GuestLikeRow.instagramUsername` is required so `tsc` names every loader that has to select it. The operator API reads none of these columns: exposing them is TAC-473's, and the non-blank CHECKs mean an absent handle is always NULL, never `''`.
- `lib/ai/` — AI SDK setup, prompts, classification, generation. Contains `classify-message.ts`, `generate-message.ts`, the `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE`, and the universal voice rules R1-R22. `extract-reported-order.ts` (TAC-323) is a standalone Haiku call mirroring `classify-message.ts`'s shape exactly (`generateObject`, `AIResult`, no `.min()/.max()` on the `quantity` number field per THE-157) — given an inbound body + the venue's menu item names, returns the items a guest is reporting having already ordered, or none. Deliberately carries its own `EXTRACT_REPORTED_ORDER_PROMPT_VERSION`, independent of `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE`'s `PROMPT_VERSION` — it never touches the classify/generate contract. `classify-intention-prompts.ts` (TAC-324) is the same shape again for a different question: given a message the venue just SENT plus the caller's currently-open intentions as self-contained `{key, description}` pairs (never a bare key list this module would need its own description lookup for — that lookup lives once, on `IntentionDefinition` in `lib/agent/intentions/definitions.ts`), returns which of those the sent text actually raised. `raisedKeys` is constrained via a `z.enum` built from the caller's open-key list PER CALL (not a bare `z.string()`) — the same structural-constraint fix a prior code review forced onto `extract-reported-order.ts`, applied from the start here. Own `CLASSIFY_INTENTION_PROMPTS_PROMPT_VERSION`, same independence rationale. `verify-grounding.ts` (TAC-350) is the same shape once more, for the knowledge-gap fabrication problem: given the guest's inbound, the generated reply body, and the SAME `venueInfo` + `knowledgeChunks` the generator saw (rendered via the same `venueInfoToProse`/`knowledgeChunksToProse` serializers `compose-prompt.ts` uses — never a separately re-derived summary), returns whether the reply states a specific factual claim not supported by that source material. Own `VERIFY_GROUNDING_PROMPT_VERSION` (v1.6.0 as of TAC-502), same independence rationale. **TAC-409 added two bullets to the prompt's `Do not flag:` list, and the framing matters: the verifier was UNSTABLE and is now LESS so — not "too strict and now calibrated."** (1) **Abridgement.** A reply that omits detail the source contains, while contradicting nothing in it, is grounded. The bullet names its own DIRECTION against rule 3 deliberately: rule 3's three worked examples are all a reply asserting MORE than the source, and this is the reverse case. The two never conflicted logically and the model conflated them anyway, twice, three days apart, drawing a different line each time. (2) **Identity.** Who the assistant is — the name it speaks under, and that it works at this venue — is configured, not asserted. **Deliberately NOT "the role it claims": nothing configures a role.** `speakerFramingProse`'s `named_person` branch renders only "staff at the venue" and `venue_info.staff` is `z.array(z.string())` of free-form lines, so a reply claiming a specific job title, shift or responsibility is an ordinary unsupported claim and stays checked — an earlier draft of this bullet exempted it, caught in code review. Scoped to identity ONLY so it cannot be read against the assistant's-own-text rule, which must survive intact. **On whether context parity would have fixed this instead: on these drafts, no — but do not generalise that.** The name the verifier objected to was already in `venue_info.staff`, which it receives, and on one draft in the guest's own inbound, so context was not the constraint there. The persona block is a separate matter: `personaToProse` renders into the generator's SYSTEM prompt and `verifyGroundingStage` passes only the USER prompt, so `speakerName`/`speakerFraming` never reach the verifier at all. At a venue whose `speakerName` is NOT on the staff roster — a configuration the product allows — an identity flag would be a genuine context gap. The exemption is what covers that case, not TAC-422. Measured by a verifier-only replay, both arms against fixed bodies: 39 promise bodies (19 recovered + 20 fresh, reported as two populations and never combined) held at OLD and still held at NEW, zero regressions, so the rules do not widen TAC-401's prose-promise leak. Both identity drafts went 5/5 and 4/5 held to 0/5. See the gotcha on single-verdict sampling below before reading any of those numbers as deterministic. **TAC-367 added `VERIFY_GROUNDING_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (2000, was an inline 500) and `VERIFY_GROUNDING_TRUNCATED_ERROR_CODE`** — the catch block now reads `NoObjectGeneratedError.isInstance(e) && e.finishReason === 'length'` off the SDK's own error rather than inferring truncation from provider-formatted message text, and reports it as a distinct `errorCode` so the caller can fail CLOSED on that one cause. That constant is imported BY PATH in `lib/agent/stages.ts`, never via the `@/lib/ai` barrel, because `stages.test.ts` `vi.mock`s the barrel and a bare constant arriving `undefined` would make the fail-closed branch silently unreachable in every test — same reasoning as `emoji-cadence.ts`'s deliberate exclusion. **TAC-502 (v1.6.0) made it channel-aware, and the fix is one required field plus one bullet.** `VerifyGroundingInput.conversationChannel: MessageChannel | null` is the same value `RuntimeContext.conversationChannel` holds, handed over unchanged and never re-resolved; `buildSourceMaterial` renders it as a `## Conversation channel` section from `CONVERSATION_CHANNEL_FACT`, a total `satisfies Record<MessageChannel, string>` map so a third channel fails `tsc` rather than silently losing the exemption on it. **The defect: `venue_info.contact` at Le Mil's is `{website, publicEmail}` — correctly, the venue has no PUBLIC phone number — so a reply saying "just text here, this is the number" read as a claim about a contact method the venue does not list, and the draft queued while the guest was mid-text-conversation.** The conversation was the dispositive evidence and was the one thing the verifier never saw. `venueInfo` and the knowledge chunks state no channel at all, and the lines that DO state one — `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE`'s opening, R5, R32, the register line, the persona, `unknown`'s category copy (all TAC-495) — live in the SYSTEM prompt, which this check is never given. **One narrow exception, which is real and does not rescue the general case**: the QR-scan first-touch opener renders through `runtimeToProse` into the USER prompt and says "first message on this number ... who they're texting", so on that one turn per guest the verifier does hold a channel claim. Every other turn it holds none, which is every turn the defect was measured on. **Not the knowledge entry**, measured: with the venue's own "no public phone number" entry removed from the source material entirely, 5 of 6 suspect bodies still flagged 5/5 and the sixth still flagged 1/5. **Scoped to PRESENT-TENSE self-reference only** (ruled 2026-09-21): a promise to use the channel again later is a future commitment and stays checked, and a number, account or channel named for any OTHER purpose — one to call, one for a friend who is not in the conversation — stays an ordinary claim, which is what keeps TAC-501's fabricated number catchable. Both exclusions are written into the bullet, not left as a boundary nobody wrote down. **The bullet's HEAD PARAGRAPH is pinned by one exact contiguous literal, and that is not belt-and-braces.** A first version pinned three fragments of it, and code review ran three mutants that all passed 36/36: the operative clause inverted from "is supported by it, and is never flagged" to "is NOT supported ... must be flagged"; the sentence scoping the bullet to the current exchange deleted; and "describing that medium in the present tense" widened to "naming any way to reach the venue, at any time", which reverses the ruling outright and is the tidy a future reader is likeliest to attempt. The TAC-409 lesson is that a sentence can be reversed while every asserted fragment survives, and it landed here on the very entry that cites it. **The section is withheld on a PROACTIVE turn** (followups and the holding message, which have reached this check since TAC-376): the guest is not messaging anyone when a cron fires, so rendering "the guest is texting RIGHT NOW" would hand the verifier a false statement labelled as a fact, and would cut against `PROACTIVE_ADDENDUM`'s own rule. That path behaves exactly as it did before this ticket. **The section renders BEFORE the runtime context**, because that block is the generator's whole user prompt appended verbatim with no terminator, and a `##` section after it reads as though it were inside it — which the system prompt tells the verifier is "not your concern and not grounding rules". **`null` gets NO exemption**: the section does not render and a channel claim is checked exactly as before, because generation already renders channel-neutral copy on an unresolved channel, so there is no channel-specific claim to protect. The field is REQUIRED rather than optional for the reason `runtimeContext` and `isProactive` are, sharpened by this seam's one recorded drift: TAC-350 shipped the retrieval relevance floor to `stages.ts` and the Voices regen kept the old semantics until TAC-366 made the two share a helper. (TAC-350's VERIFIER half was mirrored correctly at the time — see "Regen helper coupling" below, which is the authority on that history; an earlier draft of this entry cited TAC-350 and TAC-366 as two separate failures of the mirror, which is wrong in both directions and is the sort of stale justification this file keeps warning about.) `tsc` is what stops the next one. All three call sites move together — `verifyGroundingStage`, the Voices regen, and `scripts/measure-order-attribution.ts`. Deliberately excludes voice-corpus (`ragChunks`) from what it checks against — voice is how the venue talks, not what's true about it. See "AI agent runtime contract → Per-message emoji cadence" for the measured basis. `self-talk-detector.ts` (TAC-355) is a pure, dependency-free deterministic module — no AI call, no independence-rationale prompt version — exporting `SELF_TALK_PATTERNS` + `matchSelfTalk(body)`, same shape as `lib/agent/comp-backstop.ts`'s `matchComp`. Catches the agent showing its own reasoning in a guest-facing body (a dash self-correction: "...dandelion root — actually wait, no dashes"). Wired into `generateMessage`'s existing per-attempt regen loop alongside `DASH_REGEX`, sharing its attempt budget (the two failures are correlated — the motivating incident WAS dash avoidance) and composing regen feedback when both fire on the same attempt. Patterns requiring a self-referential subject (`my`/`our`/`I'm`/`I was` + instructions/rules/programming/guidelines) deliberately exclude bare "the rules"/"instructions" so ordinary venue copy ("per house rules") can't trip it; "actually wait"/"let me rephrase" are deliberately left loose (a false positive there costs one harmless regen, not a queue) — see the module's own header for the full false-positive analysis. `verify-mechanic-offer.ts` (TAC-355) is the same `verify-grounding.ts`-shaped independent backstop again, for the mechanic-approval self-flag: given the drafted reply plus this turn's `requires_operator_approval: true` eligible mechanics (name/reward/qualification — the exact bullets `formatMechanicEligibility` renders), returns whether the reply offers one of them. `mechanicId` is a per-call `z.enum` built from the actual eligible-gated-id set (never a bare `z.string()`), same discipline as `extract-reported-order.ts`/`classify-intention-prompts.ts`.   **THE CARVE-OUT RENDERS ONLY WHEN A GUEST MESSAGE IS SUPPLIED, and that conditionality is a MEASURED fix, not tidiness.** Shipped unconditionally, it moved TAC-401's recorded apology-idiom rate from **0/20 to 8/20 (40%)** on the 220-body replay (1100 calls, zero failed; the other three categories unmoved at 0/30, 0/25, 0/1005). Both offending bodies were **A4 engine followups** — "sorry again about the cortado the other day, that's on us." 5/5 and "still thinking about that cortado, that one was on us to get right." 3/5 — i.e. the PROACTIVE path, which passes `null` in production, where the rule's own condition has no referent and the model applied its spirit instead. Rendering it conditionally makes the no-inbound system prompt **byte-identical to v1.0.0's, verified at 2464 characters and pinned by a test** that transcribes the whole v1.0.0 string, so TAC-401's baseline holds by construction and every proactive path behaves exactly as before. Post-fix the rate is **1/20 (5%)**, which is sampling noise on a provably identical prompt at temperature 0.2, not a residual — do not read it as a partial fix.
  **Measured by `scripts/measurement/prose-promise-elliptical.ts`, two arms, 280 calls, zero failed.** The incident body goes **0/10 in the control to 10/10 with the inbound**, naming `comp / "a replacement gulab jamun"`; a second elliptical row 2/10 to 10/10; three plain-promise rows hold 10/10 in BOTH arms, so the widening broke no existing catch; and every must-stay-clean row is 0/10 in both, including one that was 9/10 body-only before the conditional fix. **TWO cells breach and both are recorded rather than smoothed over.** (1) `ell-04`, "same for that one" against "the second drink was wrong as well", scored 5/10, 2/10 and 4/10 across three runs — no stable verdict at all, which is the finding rather than the number; that shape is too thin for this check even with the inbound. (2) `ell-11`, **a genuine false positive**: "that's on us for not checking the case this morning" after "the gulab jamun was stale" mints a comp for the gulab jamun 8-10/10, where the reply accepts FAULT and offers nothing. That is exactly the case the measurement was asked to cover, its cost is bounded (the regex holds the draft either way, the card names what approving creates, and skipping creates nothing), and whether to tighten the rule is Jaipal's call rather than a thing to quietly adjust. `reasoning` is declared FIRST in its schema for TAC-301 part 1.5's reason, and `VERIFY_PROSE_PROMISE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` is 1000 rather than the mechanic checker's 300 because that unbounded field sits ahead of a description as well as a verdict. `VERIFY_PROSE_PROMISE_TRUNCATED_ERROR_CODE` is imported BY PATH in `lib/agent/stages.ts`, never via the barrel, for the same reason `VERIFY_GROUNDING_TRUNCATED_ERROR_CODE` is — it decides the no-retry branch. Body-only input like its TAC-401 sibling, `reasoning` first, own `VERIFY_CANCELLATION_CLAIM_PROMPT_VERSION`, `VERIFY_CANCELLATION_CLAIM_TRUNCATED_ERROR_CODE` imported BY PATH in `stages.ts`, fails CLOSED after one retry. **A SEPARATE check rather than a second question on `verify-prose-promise.ts`, and the first reason is mechanical**: the two have different SKIP conditions, so one call cannot serve both — `verifyProsePromiseStage` skips on `isCommitmentTypeGated`, this one skips on a RESOLVED cancellation carrier and must RUN on a carried-obligation draft, because a reply can offer one thing and falsely claim to cancel another. The second reason is the safety one: TAC-401's check PRODUCES a carrier, this one must never produce one, because minting an obligation from a second reading of prose is protective while minting a cancellation is destructive. It returns a boolean and nothing actionable, pinned as an exact key set. Folding them would also reset TAC-401's baseline (measured over 220 replies at its v1.0.0) and make the two rates inseparable.

Required rather than optional-with-a-default on purpose: a new caller on a path with no inbound has to DECIDE its query rather than inherit a wrong one by saying nothing. `''` is the legitimate "do not retrieve" answer and short-circuits to `[]`.
- `lib/agent/` — orchestration layer. `build-runtime-context.ts` (assembles RuntimeContext for a single agent run), `stages.ts` (classify → retrieve → generate stage functions), `handle-inbound.ts`, `handle-followup.ts`. `dispatch-arrival-capture.ts` (TAC-297) is the shared helper called from all three handlers to transition a guest's open obligations to `pending_ack` (imminent) or stamp `expected_arrival` for cron (scheduled) — never throws, RAGResult-shaped. **TAC-363 changed which rows it touches, twice over.** It consults the venue's hours and records NOTHING for an `imminent` signal while the venue is closed (ruling 1(a)); and it no longer reads `arrivalCapture.referencesCommitmentId` to choose a row, sweeping every `status='open'` obligation on `ctx.activeCommitments` instead, because that field is a single id and the prompt tells the model to pick one — so a guest owed two comps had one surfaced when they walked in. The id still GATES the emission via `isEmptyArrivalCapture` (it is the evidence the model read the `## Active commitments` block) and a model-supplied id now never reaches the database at all. `venue-open-state.ts` (TAC-363) is the single derivation site for the open/closed verdict, shared by this, the approval gate and `buildAiRuntime`; `isVenueClosed` is true only for a POSITIVE closed verdict, which is how ruling 2(a) ("unknown hours behave as open") holds by construction rather than by each caller remembering. **`handle-operator-decline.ts` (TAC-299)** is a third orchestrator parallel to inbound + followup, fired from `/api/operator/commitments/[id]/draft-decline` when an operator swipes left on a heads-up commitment card. Calls `persistOrRegenQueuedDraft` with `primaryTrigger='operator_decline_initiated'` (an operator-initiated `messages.review_reason` distinct from the `APPROVAL_TRIGGERS` auto-policy set — see `lib/operator/queue.ts` `ExtraReviewReason`). **TAC-527 found a gap here and deliberately did NOT fix it — see TAC-531.** Skipping the gate (deviation 2) also skips the prose-promise check, because that check is called from the gate's CALLERS rather than the gate, so a decline draft promising a comp in prose ("sorry, we're out of those, next one's on us") persists `pending_commitment: null` and creates nothing when the operator approves it. That is TAC-527's incident on a different route. **It was built and then reverted (ruled 2026-09-23), because the fix cannot be carrier-only.** Routing the carrier in requires `resolveDraftCarrierIdentity` — the slot decided against and the carrier persisted must be the same thing, or a flagged draft 23505s into a card the slot decision left alone, which is TAC-401's own blocker — and that changes the SLOT, which has two consequences neither this ticket nor TAC-299 has ruled on: with the obligation slot empty the draft inserts there and stops superseding the pending conversation card (TAC-299 decision #2), and with a different comp there it drops, which the route maps to 502 **without cancelling the commitment**, losing the operator's swipe-left. A swipe-left that errors and loses the cancellation is worse than the defect, so the second decision was split out rather than bundled. **Do not "fix" this by passing the carrier while leaving the slot on `draftCommitmentIdentity`**: migration 041's index predicate reads `pending_commitment->>'type'`, so the row lands in the obligation index whatever the app decided, and the divergence is the unsafe half. Returns the standard `AgentResult` discriminated union. The agent module owns the per-request lifecycle. **TAC-308 adds a fourth orchestrator plus the timer it serves.** `handle-holding-message.ts` generates and SENDS the holding message for one knowledge-gap card — the only outbound in this repo with no operator and no gate behind it, acceptable only because the message is content-free by construction (asserts nothing, commits to no time, names no fact). It runs the real gates and treats a `queue` verdict as a FAILURE, because the card already owns one of this guest's pending slots: generate, retry once, then send `FALLBACK_HOLDING_BODY`. **TAC-424 makes that ladder reachable by one more cause, with two consequences worth knowing.** A grounding check that faults twice now returns `degraded` and queues, so on this path it drives the attempt to failure exactly as a truncated one already did — meaning a guest waiting on a card gets the fixed line instead of a generated holding message for as long as the verifier is faulting. That is acceptable (the fallback asserts nothing by construction) and it is tested. The second is a genuine gap in ruling 2's "distinguishable by SQL alone": `sendFallback` goes through `scheduleAndSend`, which writes neither `review_triggers` nor `ungrounded_claims`, so **on this one path a degraded grounding check leaves no row-level record at all** — only the PostHog event and the fallback's red alert. There is no queue slot to carry it, so this was accepted rather than solved; stated here so it is not discovered later as a hole in the query. **TAC-367: it retrieves NO knowledge corpus at all** — `ctx.knowledgeCorpus = []`, unconditionally, like `handle-operator-decline.ts`. Measured against Le Mil's live corpus that returns a FULL slate every time (4/4 above the floor on every variant); two of the four chunks were `mechanic` entries. **On when this exposure existed — the obvious reading is wrong, and a first version of this entry got it backwards.** The highest score across EVERY measured variant is **0.4977** (`Followup manual for guest`), the rest 0.31–0.38; all are BELOW 0.5 and `filterByRelevance` is `>=`, so at the old floor this path retrieved **zero** — and `manual` has no `CATEGORY_TO_PRIMARY_TAG_PREFERENCE` entry, so no untagged-retry branch rescues them. The real history is three-step: the exposure predates TAC-350 (before it there was no relevance floor at all, only `lib/rag`'s `SIMILARITY_FLOOR` of 0.3, which every one of these clears), **TAC-350's 0.5 floor closed it by accident, and TAC-358's drop to 0.30 reopened it** — so TAC-358 is the proximate cause of the live exposure even though the underlying synthetic-query defect is older than both. `[]` not `null` is deliberate: an empty array renders TAC-242's explicit "No specific venue knowledge matched this query… do not invent specifics" framing, while `null` omits the block — for a message whose whole guarantee is that it asserts nothing, being told it has no venue knowledge beats being told nothing. It suppresses on `guests.opted_out_at` (read fresh, fails CLOSED), on `venues.hold_all_outbound` (a venue that reviews everything can't be handed an ungated send), and — TAC-307 — when `approval_policy` holds its category (`'manual'`) or everything. **That third check MUST live at the suppression point, not at the gate**, and the reason is the trap: `tryGenerateHolding` DOES call `applyApprovalPolicyStage`, but it treats a `queue` verdict as a FAILURE, and the failure ladder ends in `sendFallback`, which bypasses generation and the gate entirely. A policy hold enforced at the gate would be converted into an ungated send one line later. `knowledge-gap-timeout.ts` is the processor — third sibling of `commitments-due.ts` and `followups/engine.ts`, still concrete-not-generic — doing scan → CAS claim → send → regenerate-card. **`pending-slots.ts` (TAC-394, extended by TAC-397)** owns the two-slot rule: `pendingSlotOf`, `loadPendingRowsBySlot` (the only per-guest pending-draft read, DESC-windowed since TAC-397), `decideSlotAction` (the one decision table shared by the gate, persist race recovery, the crash card and the decline), and the knowledge-gap card predicate, moved out of `stages.ts` (which re-exports it) because `schedule-and-send.ts` cannot import `stages.ts` without loading Voyage. **TAC-397 adds the routing half here**: `ConversationDisposition` and `resolveConversationDisposition` (the three cases, pure), `silencesConversationTurn` (shared by the gate and `decideSlotAction`, because the gate must ask BEFORE its `triggers.length === 0 → send` return and `decideSlotAction` asks again for the queue path and 23505 recovery), `mostRecentlyOpenedConversationCard` (the single implementation of ruling Q2), and `occupantOfSlot`. `PendingRowsBySlot.conversation` is an ARRAY, oldest first; `otherSlotOccupant` became the boolean `otherSlotOccupied`; and `PendingSlotRow` gained `reply_to_message_id`, which is what lets recovery tell a duplicate delivery from a different message. It imports `looksLikeQuestion` (pure, dependency-free) and `MessageCategory` as `import type` only, so the module stays loadable from `schedule-and-send.ts`, which cannot pull in `lib/ai`. `testing/pending-rows-fake.ts` is its in-memory `messages` table, with index modes `'020'`, `'041'`, `'054'` and `'none'`; its 054 key writes migration 054's sentinel out longhand rather than importing it, because a fake that reused the code under test would agree with it by construction. `pending-question.ts` loads the outstanding question for the `## Unanswered question` prompt block and exports `loadInboundQuestion`, shared with the processor so the two can't disagree about whether a question is readable. **`extract-reported-order.ts` (TAC-323)** is a fire-and-forget side effect fired from `handle-inbound.ts` via `waitUntil` right after classification succeeds — a slow or failed call can never delay or block the reply, at the accepted cost that the extracted order is NOT available to `generateStage` (the reply can't reference it). Gate is three conditions, ANDed: prefilter hit, zero existing `guest_reported` transactions for the guest (once one exists, permanently disarmed for that guest — Command Center's delete action on the row is the only re-arm path), and within 7 days of `guests.created_at`. Never throws; every branch (including DB/LLM failures) returns a typed outcome and is logged, matching the `updateGuestContext` failure-handling posture already in the same file — no red alert, since this isn't part of the voice/reply contract. **TAC-325 adds ONGOING order capture alongside this, not on top of it**: enrollment's gate 2 (zero existing rows) and gate 3 (within 7 days) no longer terminate the run on a miss — either failing falls through to a second write path, `source='guest_reported_ongoing'` (migration 047), which enrollment's own index and gate never see. Ongoing capture collapses to one row per guest per venue-local calendar day: a later same-day report merges its new items into the most recent ongoing row (name-only dedupe against that row's existing `raw_data.line_items` — deliberately not "is this a re-order," so "got another cortado" reads the same as "that cortado was cold," a known simplification costing item/spend attribution, never visit count) unless the model's `continuesRecentVisit` flag says this is a separate trip. `reportTiming` widens from `'present' | 'past'` to `'present' | 'specific_past_day' | 'vague_past'` — a specific relative day ("yesterday", a named weekday) now resolves to a real `occurredOnDate` via `venueLocalInstant` (venue-local noon as a synthetic anchor, always `approximate` precision), while a genuinely vague reference ("last week") writes nothing at all rather than falsely dating itself to the message's own timestamp. `advanceLastVisit` is the one shared `last_visit_at`/`last_visit_precision` advance helper used by both paths — forward-only as before, plus a new guard: an `approximate` write never displaces a `pinned` value anchored to the SAME venue-local day. **`lib/agent/intentions/` (TAC-324)** is the first-touch-intentions mechanism: `definitions.ts` holds the closed `IntentionKey` union (`learn_first_order`, `invite_contact_save`) plus `INTENTION_DEFINITIONS` (each with a `promptLine`, a `classifierDescription` — what the post-send classifier is told this intention means, added on code review so `lib/ai` never carries its own independently-maintained copy of the same fact — an `expiresAfterMs`, an `isSatisfied` predicate, and — TAC-379 — a `satisfactionLabel`, plain-English prose stating how the intention closes. Display-only and structurally unable to reach the prompt — `OpenIntention` carries `key` and `promptLine` only — TAC-380 added `eligibleAt`) — the sole extension point for future intent sets, so adding one never touches `derive.ts` or `lib/ai/classify-intention-prompts.ts`. `derive.ts` is deliberately PURE (no DB access, unlike the ticket's own suggested signature) — `deriveOpenIntentions` takes already-loaded facts and applies one uniform rule (open until satisfied, prompted, or expired) with zero per-key branching, mirroring `filterEligibleMechanics`'s pure-filter-fed-by-caller-loaded-data shape; `applyCurrentTurnSuppression` drops `learn_first_order` for the current turn only when `bodyMentionsMenuItem` (imported from `extract-reported-order.ts` above, not reimplemented) hits the inbound body, so the reply answering an order question never gets rendered next to "you haven't heard what this guest ordered yet." `record.ts` is the post-send counterpart — fired from `handle-inbound.ts` via `waitUntil` after `scheduleAndSend` succeeds, using the SENT body (never a queued/dropped/refused draft, since those never reached the guest): classifies which open intentions the send raised via `lib/ai/classify-intention-prompts.ts`, then upserts one `guest_intention_prompts` row per raised key with `ignoreDuplicates: true` (independent per-`(guest_id, intention_key)` writes, unlike `claimFollowupLogRows`'s deliberately-`onConflict`-free multi-row claim, which needs atomic all-or-nothing rollback for a different reason — see that file's own header). Gated to `created_via: 'qr_scan'` guests and to inbound runs only; `build-runtime-context.ts` sets `openIntentions: []` unconditionally on the followup path, because recording never fires there and rendering the block would raise an intention with no row ever capping it. **TAC-380 supersedes the specifics above — see "Intentions, redefined (TAC-380)" under the runtime contract:** seven keys, not two; `load.ts` (new) owns the reads; `derive.ts` gains arming, re-arming, gating, the brake, `deriveIntentionState` and `renderableIntentions`; `record.ts` gains `recordIntentionEligibility` (inserts and re-arms) and retry-then-close-pessimistically; the `qr_scan`-only origin gate is gone. **TAC-385 PR 1 adds `rendered.ts`**, a NEW sibling rather than an addition to `derive.ts` / `definitions.ts` / `record.ts` — those three stay untouched, which is PR 1's structural guarantee that it changes no file deciding when an intention CLOSES. It owns both ends of the `messages.rendered_intentions` carrier: `buildRenderedIntentionsPayload` (write) and `parseRenderedIntentionsForRecording` (read, dropping a retired key or an unparseable anchor rather than throwing, because it runs inside the operator's approve tap). **`crisis-safety.ts` (TAC-348)** is a pure, dependency-light module (`CRISIS_SAFETY_REPLY_BODY`, `CRISIS_SAFETY_REVIEW_REASON`, `buildCrisisSafetyResult()`) consumed identically from two call sites — `handle-inbound.ts` (right after `classifyStage` succeeds, before any retrieval) and `scripts/onboarding/run-test-scenarios.ts` (the TAC-347 harness, same position) — so the harness grades the actual shipped mechanism rather than a full-pipeline generation the code never runs on this turn. See "AI agent runtime contract → Crisis-safety short circuit" below for the full design rationale. **`dispatch-reply.ts` (TAC-469)** is the one place an agent reply picks its transport, with `dispatch-instagram-reply.ts` as its Instagram arm and `last-inbound-channel.ts` as the read behind the both-identifiers rule; see "Instagram outbound (TAC-469)". **`conversation-channel.ts` (TAC-495)** is the pure rule that picks a conversation's channel for prompt copy; see "AI agent runtime contract → Channel copy". **`coalesce-turn.ts` (TAC-526)** owns the inbound-burst claim — the settle, the `(venue_id, guest_id)` claim against `inbound_turn_claims` (migration 057), the lease takeover CAS, `pickNewer`'s `(created_at, id)` comparison, and the four constants `INBOUND_COALESCING_ENABLED` / `COALESCE_SETTLE_MS` / `CLAIM_LEASE_MS` / `MAX_TURN_EXTENSIONS`. `RAGResult`-shaped, genuinely never throws (see the runtime-contract entry for why that claim was FALSE until the flag was flipped), injected `{ store, now, sleep }` so no test waits 8 real seconds (the `dispatch-instagram-reply.ts` precedent). `testing/turn-claims-fake.ts` is its in-memory table: it enforces the primary key and YIELDS BEFORE IT CHECKS, so two claims started together really interleave — without the yield the runtime serialises them by luck and the concurrency test would pass against a claim with no atomicity in it. See "AI agent runtime contract → A guest's burst is one turn". **`instagram-window-warning.ts` (TAC-473)** is the FOURTH concrete cron-processor sibling, run from `/api/cron/pending-timeout` beside `processDueKnowledgeGaps`: it warns an operator when a held Instagram draft has `INSTAGRAM_WINDOW_WARNING_MS` (one hour) or less left in Meta's window. **Idempotency is a COLUMN, not an interval** — the tick is every minute against an hour-long window, so without `messages.window_warning_pushed_at` one card pushes sixty times (migration 038's escalation lesson). CAS-claim before the push, like its siblings. It reads the anchor through `loadLastGuestActionAt` rather than a second copy of that query, because that function is what the SEND GATE consults and a different answer would warn about a deadline the server would not honour; a failed read is an error for that draft, never a null, since null means "no guest action" and a read that failed has not established that. The anchor is cached per GUEST, not per card. **`record-inbound-turn-outcome.ts` (TAC-523)** writes the ledger row for an agent run. `handleInbound` is now a thin wrapper around the orchestrator, renamed `runInboundTurn`: the wrapper records the `AgentResult` at ONE exit, so all thirteen agent-layer paths are covered without touching any of the orchestrator's ~20 return sites — which is what makes "no path's decision changed" a property of the diff (52 insertions, 0 deletions — an earlier draft of this line said 24, estimated rather than measured, which code review caught) rather than a claim in a review. **The record call is guarded SEPARATELY from the run, and the structure is load-bearing**: inside the same `try`, a throwing recorder would be caught, recorded a second time and rethrown, converting a reply that reached the guest into a failed request. Which outcomes write what is a mapped-type total over `AgentResult['status']`, verified by adding an eighth member and watching `tsc` fail (TS2741 names the missing key) rather than by a comment claiming a guard — TAC-424's lesson, on this exact shape. It resolves `venue_id`/`guest_id`/`channel` from the inbound row itself rather than threading them out, one cheap read, so the orchestrator body stays untouched.
- `lib/auth/` — auth helpers. `verifyAnalogAdminAccess(authUserId)` gates `/admin/*` access via cookie-session (THE-198) — admin layout (`app/admin/(authed)/layout.tsx`) is the primary caller. The bearer-token path — `verifyOperatorRequest(request)` (returns `{ operatorId, allowedVenueIds }` or throws `AuthError`), `getCurrentOperator(request)` (Response-returning wrapper), `verifyAnalogAdminRequest(request)` (bearer + `is_analog_admin = true`), and `withOperatorAuth(handler)` (HOF for `app/api/operator/*` route handlers, TAC-258) — went live with the operator API endpoints. `verifyAnalogAdminRequest` remains forward-scaffolding for the future `analog-operator` repo; the others are active. **TAC-272 split `operators.auth_user_id` into `auth_user_id_phone` and `auth_user_id_email`** so an operator can sign in via phone OTP OR email magic link and resolve to the same row — both `verifyOperatorRequest` and `verifyAnalogAdminAccess` do an OR-match across the two columns and lazy-link via `linkOperatorByAuthUser` (`lib/auth/link-operator.ts`) on the miss path. The admin magic-link callback at `app/admin/auth/callback/route.ts` eager-links right after `exchangeCodeForSession`; lazy-link still fires for any session that pre-dates that wiring. `authUserPhoneToE164` (`lib/auth/normalize-phone.ts`) bridges Supabase's `auth.users.phone` (no `+` prefix) and `operators.phone_number` (with `+`) at match time. Server-only; uses the admin DB client.
- `lib/operator/` — Operator API building blocks (TAC-258, TAC-277, TAC-297). `dispatchOperatorOutbound({messageId, operatorId, allowedVenueIds, action, editedBody?})` is the shared "send the pending draft via Sendblue and update the existing row" helper for approve + edit; optimistic UPDATE flips `review_state` pending→target, then Sendblue, then second UPDATE for `status='sent'` / `sent_at` / `provider_message_id`. Returns `originalBody` (pre-UPDATE) so the edit route can stamp `response_review.originalAiBody`. **TAC-297 extends this** with a post-dispatch read of `messages.pending_commitment` and a call to `createCommitmentFromPending` to materialize the `guest_commitments` row from the carrier; failures log + don't roll back the dispatch. `listPendingQueue(allowedVenueIds)` wraps the `list_operator_queue` RPC and normalizes the jsonb recent_context into `QueueDraft.recentContext[]` (entries typed as the canonical `ThreadMessage` from `@/lib/schemas`). **TAC-364 added four Contract-locked fields to `QueueDraft`, all ALWAYS PRESENT (empty array / empty string, never undefined, so the client never branches on presence): `reviewReasonCode` (the RAW primary trigger code — colour keys on this, never on the prose label, because shipping only the label is what left analog-operator's `queue-tone.ts` joining on three English strings this server has never emitted, so every production card fell to its default and two of its three colours were dead), `reviewTriggers` (the full set as RAW CODES, **primary included and never deduped server-side** — the field means "everything that fired", and the client renders secondaries as `reviewTriggers` minus `reviewReasonCode`, a subtraction that is only well defined because both sides are codes), `reviewTriggerLabels` (display text, PARALLEL to `reviewTriggers`: same length, same order, index-aligned, with the same `'Needs review'` fallback `reviewReason` uses) and `ungroundedClaims`. Note the wire DELIBERATELY collapses `ungrounded_claims`' three-state column to `[]` — see migration 039: the never-ran-vs-found-nothing distinction is a property of the row for SQL to ask, not a UI state, and neither value renders anything on a card.** **TAC-397 added a sixth, `replacedDraft: { body, replacedAt } | null`** (always present, non-null only on a card a CORRECTION regenerated in place), projected from migration 054's two columns by `normalizeReplacedDraft`, which requires BOTH — the persist layer pairs them, but that guarantee lives in another file and a half-written pair would break a Contract promising a string. TAC-397 also unbounded `otherPendingDraftsForGuest`: no code changed, but the comment claiming the server produces 0 or 1 did, because a client could read it as a guarantee. **TAC-394 added a fifth, `otherPendingDraftsForGuest`** (always present, 0 when none): how many other pending cards the same guest holds, 0 or 1 under migration 041, from migration 042's `other_pending_for_guest` and normalized to 0 unless it is a positive finite number. Client half: TAC-402. **No card-facing string contains an em dash (ruled 2026-09-14).** `REVIEW_REASON_LABELS` values, and anything else that reaches the operator card, are read fast on a phone mid-shift, where an em dash is a pause the reader has to parse and a full stop or comma is not. Enforced by a test in `queue.test.ts` that runs EVERY key of the label map (plus the `'Needs review'` fallback) through `listPendingQueue` and checks both `reviewReason` and `reviewTriggerLabels`, so a new trigger's copy cannot reintroduce one; a review-only rule would not have survived the next trigger added. Comments and ticket prose may keep em dashes; only strings that reach the card may not. **TAC-527 makes two labels DYNAMIC, and that changes what the em-dash invariant covers.** `labelForTrigger(code, carrier)` is the one resolver behind both `reviewReason` and `reviewTriggerLabels`, so a card's primary line and its secondary chips cannot disagree about what is being offered. `prose_promise_backstop` with a resolved carrier names what approving creates (`Approving this comps {description}. Your call.`, and for the other two types `sets aside {description} for them` / `promises a discount on {description}` — **both wordings carry a constraint from Jaipal's 2026-09-23 approval and must survive any rewrite: "holds" read as the SYSTEM holding the item rather than the venue setting one aside, and "discounts" implies we know the amount, which we do not**); without one it keeps its TAC-401 wording. `comp_regex_backstop` with NO carrier gains `Approving won't create anything.`, which is the residual case where the regex held a reply and nothing is minted from it; with a carrier it keeps its plain wording, because the suffix would be false. **`commitment_type_gated` is deliberately excluded and that boundary needed a TEST, not a comment**: a mutant widening the dynamic sentence to it passed all 71 tests in `queue.test.ts`, because the copy table renders that trigger with no carrier and the dynamic branch was unreachable for it. **The description is the first card string built from MODEL-WRITTEN text**, so it is stripped of em and en dashes and capped at a word boundary before interpolation — the no-em-dash invariant runs the STATIC map and cannot see a dash arriving that way. The carrier comes from a second batched `SELECT id, pending_commitment` keyed on the ids the RPC just returned (the TAC-299 precedent), which is what keeps this free of a migration and of a DROP/CREATE on `list_operator_queue`; it **FAILS SOFT**, because losing the specific sentence costs a worse card while failing the queue costs every operator at that venue every card, and the cards are the things with clocks on them. `listHeadsUpQueue(allowedVenueIds)` (TAC-297) is the sibling for the new `commitments` field on the queue response — Contract-locked payload `{ id, venueId, guestId, type, guest: {name}, description, code, expected_arrival, created_at, recognitionState, sourceMessageId }` (TAC-299 added the last two, TAC-364 `venueId`/`guestId`), FIFO via `ORDER BY created_at ASC`. `loadGuestThread({messageId, allowedVenueIds})` (TAC-277; since TAC-395 it returns only messages that reached the guest) is the full-thread-fetch helper behind the operator-app edit screen: two-step lookup (resolve `(venue_id, guest_id)` from `messageId`, then membership check + most-recent-200 select with `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 200` reversed in JS to oldest→newest per the Contract — CC's `loadConversationData` used ASC LIMIT 200 until TAC-316, which kept the OLDEST 200 rows and went live as a truncation bug the night Mock Sextant crossed the cap; both now use the DESC-window pattern). Failure modes distinguished as `message_not_found | out_of_allowlist | db_error` so future logging/alerting can tell them apart even though the route flattens the first two to a uniform 404. All four helpers are RAGResult-shaped (`{ok: true, ...} | {ok: false, error}`) and consumed by the routes under `app/api/operator/*`. **TAC-473 added three more Contract-locked fields to BOTH `QueueDraft` and `ConversationSummary`, all ALWAYS PRESENT**: `guestChannel` (`'text' | 'instagram'`, never null), `replyWindowExpiresAt` (ISO 8601 or null) and `instagramUsername` (handle without the `@`, or null). `instagram-fields.ts` is the shared projection. **`guestChannel` is derived DIFFERENTLY on the two surfaces, and that is deliberate**: on a queue draft it is the DRAFT ROW's own `messages.channel`, because `dispatchOperatorOutbound` routes on the card's channel and the field must mean "what approving this card will do" — a value re-derived from the guest could disagree with the routing and mislead the operator about their own tap. On a conversation summary there is no draft, so it defers to `resolveConversationChannel` (TAC-495) rather than restating that rule. Both degrade an unresolvable channel to `'text'` with an error log rather than sending a null the client cannot parse. **`replyWindowExpiresAt` is Meta's own clock plus `INSTAGRAM_WINDOW_MS`, the TRUE deadline with NO margin subtracted** — the client applies its own, and the server's send gate closes `INSTAGRAM_WINDOW_MARGIN_MS` (5 min) earlier, so a client rendering it raw shows a few minutes this server would already refuse. **Its null is two-valued and `guestChannel` separates them**: a text conversation has no window, while an Instagram conversation with a null here has an UNKNOWN window, not an expired one. A value in the past means expired and is not clamped. **`phoneFallback` / `guestPhoneFallback` stay non-nullable `''` for a phoneless guest (ruled 2026-09-23)**: `analog-operator` parses both lists all-or-nothing and neither field carries a `.catch()`, so a null empties the queue and the conversations tab for every operator at that venue, with a TestFlight-length recovery. The sentinel stops being load-bearing in the same ticket anyway, because the client now branches on `guestChannel` and never tests `phoneFallback === ''`. **`queue.test.ts` had NO exact field-set assertion before TAC-473**, so a Contract field dropped from the projection would have failed nothing; it has one now, transcribed from the ticket's Contract rather than read back out of the implementation.

Sourced from the brand language at `docs/brand/style-guide-v01.html` — do not introduce decorative variants without updating the style guide first. **`<Card>` was removed here in TAC-306** — the single Card now lives at `@/components/ui/card` (shadcn). The remaining primitives stay because shadcn has no equivalent.
