That last one lived at `venues/[slug]/_components/section-shell.tsx` until the intentions page (TAC-379) grew an identical local `Section` and TAC-381's venue sections would have made a third copy; it is now imported as `@/app/admin/_components/section-shell` from 17 call sites. **Put a new section's chrome here, never a local re-declaration** — the promotion reconciled one divergence already (the intentions copy used `CardContent py-5` where the other 14 used `py-4`; unified on `py-4`), and a fourth copy would reintroduce exactly that drift.
- `lib/schemas/` — Zod schemas for venue-shaped JSONB fields. `BrandPersonaSchema` (handles dual-shape `voiceAntiPatterns`, see gotchas), `MessageReviewSchema` (the `response_review` shape from migration 014), `VenueInfoSchema` (with `filterActiveContext` per THE-150, and `classifyContextEntry` — extracted from it in TAC-343 so the admin venue page's expiry queue and the agent's own active-context filter share one per-entry active/expired/malformed classification instead of two), `GuestContextSchema` + `GuestContextPatchSchema` (the persisted shape and the agent-emitted patch shape for `guests.context` per TAC-296, plus `filterActiveLifeContext` mirroring the venue-info expires_at filter, and `toParsedGuestContext` for the runtime-ready projection with expired entries dropped + observations truncated to `OBSERVATION_RENDER_LIMIT`=10). `approval-policy.ts` (v1.24.0) owns `venue_configs.approval_policy` — `parseApprovalPolicy` (fail-OPEN to defaults) + `resolveCategoryPolicy` (stored `perCategory` merged ON TOP of the code default, so an empty stored object can't erase the `comp_complaint` route). **TAC-307 adds three things**: `POLICY_EXEMPT_CATEGORIES` / `isPolicyExemptCategory` (categories that can never be held — `opt_out`, for TCPA; the one named place, consumed by the resolver, the admin UI, and the write route alike), and `resolvePolicyDecision`, which returns `{disposition, source}` where source is `'exempt' | 'stored' | 'code_default' | 'policy_default'`. `resolveCategoryPolicy` is now a thin wrapper over it. **The source is what makes a hold absolute or not** — see trigger 8 under *Approval policy gates*. Note the resolver reads the stored entry off the CALLER'S policy, never off the `?? APPROVAL_POLICY_DEFAULT` fallback: indexing the fallback would report the fleet-wide default as source `'stored'` and silently make every degraded context absolute (caught in TAC-307's own tests; there's a named regression test for it). `guest-commitment.ts` (TAC-297) covers `CommitmentEmissionSchema` + `ArrivalCaptureEmissionSchema` (what the LLM emits — all inner optional, no-op shape `{}`), `PendingCommitmentSchema` (the stricter jsonb carrier shape on `messages.pending_commitment`), `GuestCommitmentRowSchema` (full DB row), helpers `isEmptyCommitmentEmission` / `isEmptyArrivalCapture` / `pendingFromEmission` (generates a 4-char verification code for comp/hold/discount when the agent didn't emit one), and `toActiveCommitment` (runtime projection used by the `## Active commitments` prompt block). `VenueServicesSchema` (TAC-301 part 2) is the structured statement of what a venue does and doesn't do for a guest — `aheadOrdering` / `holds` / `reservations` / `delivery` / `catering` as **optional booleans**, plus free-form `alsoOffers` / `alsoDoesNotOffer`. **Three-state, and the distinction is the design: `true` renders a positive, `false` renders an explicit negative, ABSENT renders nothing.** Absent must never read as a denial — the block's closing line says unlisted services "have not been stated either way" precisely because an earlier wording ("unknown, not available") re-read every unstated service as unavailable the moment a venue filled in ONE field, which is the same failure narrowed to partially-configured venues. Named fields rather than `Record<string, boolean>` so `services.holds === false` is compile-checked the day commitment vocabulary is conditioned on capability; `SERVICE_LABELS` in the serializer is a total map, so adding a service fails `tsc` until it gets a label. Parsed `.optional().catch(undefined)` — permissive at the LIVE boundary because the field is Studio-only today and `buildRuntimeContext` throws on a venue_info parse failure, so a typo would otherwise take down every agent run for that venue. `rendered-intentions.ts` (TAC-385 PR 1) owns the shape of `messages.rendered_intentions` — `RenderedIntentionsSchema` plus `parseRenderedIntentions`, permissive at the live boundary (a malformed entry is dropped on its own, keeping its siblings). Deliberately DOMAIN-FREE: resolving a key to a live definition needs `lib/agent/intentions/definitions.ts`, and `lib/schemas` must not depend on `lib/agent`, so that half lives in `lib/agent/intentions/rendered.ts`. `visit-precision.ts` (TAC-377) owns `VisitTimePrecision` (`pinned` | `approximate`) plus `parseVisitPrecision` — the shape behind `transactions.occurred_at_precision` and `guests.last_visit_precision`; permissive at the live boundary (an unrecognized value degrades to null, the "nobody recorded this" state) with migration 036's CHECK as the strict half. `venue-hours.ts` (TAC-301) is the pure interpreter of `venue_info.hours` — `parseDayRange` (one day's free-text range to minutes, tolerating the canonical en dash the venue-spec parser writes plus the hyphen/em-dash/`7am-3pm`/24h variants the admin page permits) and `resolveOpenState(hours, timezone, now)` returning `open | closed | unknown`. **Its governing rule: never claim OPEN or CLOSED on input it did not positively understand.** Every ambiguous branch resolves to `unknown`, which renders no line at all — a wrong verdict fires on every turn at that venue, where the bug it fixes needs a specific arrival phrasing to surface. Three consequences, each caught in code review after a first version got them wrong: (1) **a DESCENDING pair needs explicit half-of-day evidence** (a meridiem on both sides, or unambiguous 24-hour values) before it's read as crossing midnight — `"5:00 PM – 2:00 AM"` is a bar, but `"7-3"` is a cafe writing 7am-3pm in shorthand, and reading the second as overnight reports OPEN at 7:57pm, the exact minute of the incident, now asserted confidently rather than merely unstated. (2) **Absence is never a closure.** `parse-venue-spec.ts` silently drops table rows whose label isn't in `DAY_KEY_MAP` (`Sat & Sun`, `Weekends`) and the admin venue page writes `undefined` for a cleared field, so a missing key means "nobody said" at least as often as "shut" — an earlier version read it as a closure and would have emitted CLOSED all day at an open venue. A real closure arrives through `classifyDay`'s word-like `CLOSED_MARKER` instead, which matches the pipeline's own `"Closed – Closed"` shape, not just a hand-typed bare `"Closed"`. A bare dash is a placeholder, not a closure, and stays `unknown`. (3) **A substituted timezone suppresses the verdict** — `buildAiRuntime` tracks whether `isValidTimezone` fell back to `FALLBACK_TIMEZONE` and passes `{state:'unknown'}` when it did, since a venue resolved against the wrong zone is input nobody positively understood either. Watch the related hazard the code can't see: `parse-venue-spec.ts` and migration 001 BOTH default `timezone` to `America/Los_Angeles`, which `isValidTimezone` passes silently — a venue whose spec omitted the key is confidently Pacific, and that default is now guest-facing rather than cosmetic. `referral-source.ts` (TAC-518) owns `SCAN_REFERRAL_SOURCE` and `isScanReferral` — what `messages.referral_source` holds and what counts as a guest arriving through the venue's ig.me link. Domain-free on the `message-channel.ts` model, because it has TWO callers that must agree and must not import each other: TAC-492's guest creation (`lib/messaging/instagram/handle-events.ts`) and TAC-518's per-turn read (`build-runtime-context.ts`). Exact match, no trim and no case fold — Meta sends an uppercase constant, and every widening anyone proposes admits a value Meta has never sent on a signal that decides whether the agent treats a guest as standing in the shop. A source-level test holds both callers to it, because a local `=== 'SHORTLINK'` behaves identically until the day one of them changes. `review-state.ts` (TAC-473) owns `RESOLVED_EXTERNALLY_REVIEW_STATE`, the sixth `messages.review_state` value, set when a card was answered outside the operator app. Domain-free on the `referral-source.ts` model and for the same reason: THREE callers must agree and two of them must not import each other — the Instagram echo resolver writes it, `POST /api/operator/messages/:id/resolve-external` writes it (and that route is deliberately NOT Instagram-specific, so importing the value out of a provider folder was backwards), and `deriveDelivery` reads it. `review-state.test.ts` reads migration 056 and binds the constant to the CHECK that is the only thing able to reject a wrong value, since SQL cannot import it. `message-channel.ts` (TAC-495) owns `MESSAGE_CHANNELS` (`text`, `instagram`, bound by a test to migration 048's `messages_channel_check`) and `parseMessageChannel`, which degrades an unknown value to null, never to `text`. `inbound-turn-outcome.ts` (TAC-523) owns the vocabulary of `inbound_turn_outcomes` (migration 054) — `INBOUND_TURN_OUTCOMES`, `INBOUND_TURN_REASONS`, `INBOUND_TURN_LAYERS`, each mirrored by a CHECK and bound to migration 054 by a test that reads the file. **Deliberately NOT exported from `lib/schemas/index.ts`**: every consumer imports it by path, a barrel entry would add a second route for no gain, and `dispatch-operator-outbound.test.ts` mocks that barrel — the shape `emoji-cadence.ts` is kept out of `lib/ai/index.ts` to avoid. **No Zod parse schema and no reader**, because nothing reads the table yet (surfacing it is a later ticket) and a parser with no caller is this repo's recurring dead layer. Read JSONB fields through these — never directly via SQL paths.
- `lib/guests/` — Per-guest helpers consumed by the agent runtime (TAC-296, TAC-297). `context.ts` exposes `getGuestContext(guestId)` (parsed JSONB read, fail-OPEN on malformed payload → empty context), `updateGuestContext({guestId, update, now})` (deep-merge patch + observation append + identity-column sync in a single multi-SET UPDATE), `deepMergeContext(existing, patch, now)` (pure), and `isEmptyContextUpdate(update)` (short-circuit predicate for the no-op emission shape). `commitments.ts` (TAC-297) exposes `createCommitmentFromPending` (INSERT from the jsonb carrier), `transitionToPendingAck` / `scheduleArrival` / `markAcknowledged` / **`markCancelled` (TAC-299)** (all CAS-gated on prior status — the rowcount=1 result anchors push idempotency per TAC-297 design call #4; **the first two are also gated on `venue_id` AND `guest_id` since TAC-363**, because they were gated on `id` and `status` alone and the id on the agent path comes from the MODEL, copied out of the `## Active commitments` prompt block: a hallucinated or stale one transitioned whatever row it named, including another guest's or another venue's, and the caller got back what looked like a clean CAS win. Both were scoped rather than only the one named in the ruling, since they are called from the same function on the same id. Their tests APPLY the recorded predicate to a row set rather than checking the query mentions the right columns, which is what catches a filter built with the wrong VALUE; `markCancelled` is CAS-gated on `status='pending_ack'` and shaped like `markAcknowledged` for caller parity, but writes NO `cancelled_at` / `cancelled_by` columns because TAC-299 was scoped to no-migration — operator audit lives on the `operator_draft_decline_initiated` PostHog event), **`cancelCommitmentForGuest` (TAC-513)** (CAS-gated on `status IN ('open','pending_ack')` AND `venue_id` AND `guest_id` — it exists BESIDE `markCancelled` rather than widening it, because that one gates on `pending_ack` ALONE and the comp TAC-513 was filed for was `open` with no arrival signal, so it could not have been touched; widening it would change TAC-389's decline path. Two cancel helpers with different gates is real duplication, each carries a comment pointing at the other, and they fold under TAC-389's own follow-up. The `guest_id` in the predicate is the SECOND layer of the cross-guest guard: `resolveCancellation` already makes a foreign id unreachable, but that is application code and can be refactored away, where a WHERE clause is enforced by Postgres. Terminal states are excluded deliberately — flipping a redeemed row to `cancelled` would erase the record that the venue honoured it), `findActiveCommitmentsForGuest` (loaded by `build-runtime-context.ts` for the `## Active commitments` prompt block), **`findEarliestAcknowledgedArrival` (TAC-436)** returns the earliest `acknowledged_at` for a guest, or null — the arrival half of "a visit is confirmed", and the ONE arrival signal that creates no transaction row, which is what makes it usable for arming an intention any transaction closes. Earliest, not latest, because `understand_order` never re-arms and its window runs from its anchor. Reads the column directly rather than through `GuestCommitmentRowSchema`, so an unrecognized `type` on some other row can't drop a genuine arrival. `findScheduledOpenCommitments()` (no time arg — returns ALL `status='open' AND arrival_signal='scheduled'` rows; the per-venue morning-hour + date filter lives in the processor, not the query). **`commitment-expiry.ts` (TAC-341)** is the pure, single derivation site for every commitment horizon — `OBLIGATION_TYPES` (comp/hold/discount, an ALLOWLIST so a fifth type defaults to being left alone rather than inheriting a negation), `deriveExpiresAt`, `escalationDueAt`, and `venueLocalInstant`. That last one is genuinely new logic: venue-local wall clock → UTC, DST-aware, **two-pass** because the offset has to be sampled at an instant that is itself what you are solving for — a single pass is silently an hour wrong for any local time on the far side of a DST transition from the naive guess (mutation-verified against a Pacific/Auckland case; `venueLocalNow` in `venue-hours.ts` goes the OTHER direction and is private, so nothing existing covered this). `commitment-lifecycle-due.ts` (TAC-341) is the processor — **fourth** concrete sibling to `commitments-due.ts` / `followups/engine.ts` / `knowledge-gap-timeout.ts`, still concrete-not-generic. `commitments-due.ts` (TAC-297) is the cron processor — `processDueCommitments(now)` is the single named function for the commitments consumer; **the TAC-123 follow-up engine landed its sibling `processDueFollowups(now)` in `lib/followups/engine.ts` — the two are deliberately concrete-not-generic per design call #3; the shared "find-eligible → side-effect" seam stays unextracted until both processors' shapes have stabilized enough for the seam to fall out cleanly.** All `RAGResult`-shaped — never throws into the agent loop. Last-write-wins concurrency for `guests.context` v1, see "Common gotchas." The orchestrator dispatches `updateGuestContext` from `handle-inbound.ts` + `handle-followup.ts` **between `generateStage` success and `applyApprovalPolicyStage`** so context capture reflects what the agent UNDERSTOOD from the inbound regardless of whether the draft ships, queues, or refuses. The TAC-297 arrival-capture dispatch (`dispatchArrivalCapture` in `lib/agent/`) sits in the same window for the same reason.
- `lib/followups/` — TAC-123 follow-up engine (concrete sibling to `lib/guests/commitments-due.ts`). `engine.ts` exposes `processDueFollowups(now): Promise<ProcessDueFollowupsResult>` — top-level processor called from `/api/cron/followups-due`. Per-venue → per-enrolled-guest scan that runs detectors → Gate 1 (`canSendFollowup`) → claim-before-dispatch → `handleFollowup` → finalize/release. Per-venue local-hour filter against `followup_rules.cron_hour_local` lives in the processor. **Since TAC-428 the trigger is an hourly external cron on cron-job.org and the filter is `hour >= cron_hour_local`, not `===`** — see "Cron timing" below; the GH Actions workflow stays as a redundant net, and Vercel Hobby still caps its own cron at daily. **TAC-367: `handle-followup.ts` retrieves knowledge ONLY against the operator's own note.** The original defect was never "followups retrieve" — it was retrieving against `Followup {reason} for {name}`, a template with no referent in any corpus that still returned a full 4/4 slate on every measured variant at Le Mil's, because cosine always ranks something highest. Every chunk it produced was coincidence. An operator note ("tell her about the new Panama lot") is real content about a real topic, so `operatorInstructionQuery(trigger)` — **shared with `buildAiRuntime`, never reimplemented, so the text the model is instructed with and the text it is grounded against cannot diverge** — is the query. No note, or any engine reason (`day_*`, `cold_lapsed`, `perk_unlock`), means no query and no retrieval: those runs have no free text at all, and their content is structured (visit history, guest context, the perk's own `reward_description`) and already in the prompt. **Keeping `[]` for a hinted note was considered and rejected**: a note asking the model to be specific, with nothing behind it, removes the grounding while leaving the pressure — on a path that, at the time, had no grounding backstop. `verifyGroundingStage` used to return early when `currentMessage === null`, so no followup had one; the approval gate ran but no trigger keyed on fabrication for an outbound, so at a venue with no hold configured a fabricated fact auto-sent. **Closed by TAC-376**: per the 2026-09-17 ruling, `verifyGroundingStage` now runs on every followup (engine and manual) and the knowledge-gap holding message too — same verifier, same `knowledge_gap_backstop`/`grounding_check_failed` triggers, same failure posture as inbound, no new trigger or parallel check. (That posture was fail-open-on-transient/fail-closed-on-truncation until **TAC-424**, which made a transient fault fail closed too after one retry. The "same as inbound" half is what matters and is unchanged: there has never been a second policy for proactive turns.) The one deliberate divergence from inbound: a claim about the GUEST'S OWN actions ("brought a friend in") is in the verifier's remit on a followup — on inbound the guest made the claim, on a followup the venue does, and a followup must never assert something the guest did that isn't recorded (a fact stated in the operator's own note still counts as supported). `detectors.ts` is pure (`detectPostVisitReason`, `detectColdLapsedReason`, `detectPerkUnlockReason`, `dedupKeyForReason`) — detectors answer "did the calendar/state condition trip?" and never consult the DB; intent-bound dedup lives at the claim layer via the dedup_key UNIQUE constraint. `log.ts` is the `followup_log` interface: `claimFollowupLogRows` (atomic INSERT — 23505 conflict means another run is handling at least one reason, engine skips), `finalizeFollowupLogClaim` (UPDATE message_id post-dispatch), `releaseFollowupLogClaim` (DELETE on refusal/failure so dedup isn't burned), `loadFollowupSnapshotsForVenue` (batched per-venue read of the rolling-7d count + per-reason history + announced-mechanic set). The companion Gate 1 implementation lives at `lib/agent/followup-rules.ts` (`canSendFollowup` pure function — opt-out / quiet hours / recent conversation / weekly cap / time-bound cold dedup; per-reason intent-bound dedup is NOT here, that's the claim layer). Manual followups (TAC-249 Command Center button) bypass this engine entirely — they call `handleFollowup` with `trigger.reason='manual'`, don't write `followup_log` rows, and don't count toward weekly_cap. They do NOT bypass the approval gate (TAC-307). The render-side multi-reason intake landed in the same ticket at `deriveFollowupContext` (`lib/agent/stages.ts`) which now consumes `[primary, ...trigger.additionalReasons]` and `buildAiRuntime` now populates `perkBeingUnlocked` from `FollowupTrigger.perkMechanic` (first production wiring of that AI-runtime field).
  **TAC-313 adds two pure, dependency-light modules here.** `split-message.ts` is the surviving DEFENSIVE half of message splitting (`BUBBLE_DELIMITER` = `[[BREAK]]`, `MAX_BUBBLES_PER_RESPONSE` = 3, `INTER_BUBBLE_GAP_MS` = 1500, `collapseToSingleMessage`; `splitIntoBubbles` was retired by TAC-319 when the model's delimiter role ended) — deliberately import-free so it loads in vitest with no SDK init. Its sibling `sentence-split.ts` (TAC-319) is the DECIDING half: `splitIntoSentences`, `stripTerminalPeriod`, `resolveDispatchBubbles`, `SPLIT_PROBABILITY` — pure, imports only `split-message.ts`. `group-responses.ts` is the READ-side inverse (`groupIntoResponses`), folding a response's bubble rows back into one `RecentMessage` so `build-runtime-context` caps on responses and BOTH prompt serializers are fixed at a single site — `formatRecentConversation` and `formatClassifierRecentConversation` are independent one-line-per-element renderers over the same `ctx.recentMessages` array, so fixing either alone would leave the classifier reading rows.
- `lib/analytics/` — PostHog event emission helpers (events fire and forget; failures must not crash the agent path)
- `lib/observability/` — Langfuse SDK wrapper (THE-200). `startAgentTrace(opts)` returns an `AgentTrace` with `span() / update() / flushAsync()`; spans expose `span()`, `generation()`, `update()`, `end()`. No-op when env vars missing or `NODE_ENV=test`. Wrapper never throws — SDK errors are swallowed with `console.warn`. Use this from `lib/agent/` only; never import `langfuse` directly from app code.
- `lib/voice-training/` — Shared voice-data write helpers used by the 08-flow onboarding script (`scripts/ingest-response-review.ts`), the cc-review live-edit API route, and the Voices command-center rail (THE-237). Channels: `upsertCorpusEdit({...}, 'skip-existing' \| 'replace')` for source-ref-keyed cc-review/08-review/voices-commit writes (anti-corpus-poisoning rule applies — only the operator-edited message text is embedded). `addCorpusEntry({venueId, content, sourceType, tags, addedByOperatorId?})` for ad-hoc rail additions (`source_type` ∈ `manual_entry` \| `sample_text` \| `past_message`). `editCorpusEntry({corpusId, content?, tags?})` re-embeds only on content change. `removeCorpusEntry(corpusId)` straight delete + FK cascade on voice_embeddings. `dedupeAndAppendAntiPatterns(venueId, rules, { source, authorOperatorId? })` does read-modify-write on `venue_configs.brand_persona.voiceAntiPatterns` with case + whitespace normalization. `removeAntiPattern(venueId, ruleText)` removes by exact text match (operators delete what they see). THE-236 reshaped the persisted anti-pattern entries from `string[]` to `Array<{ text, source: 'auto' \| 'manual', authorOperatorId?, addedAt? }>`; `BrandPersonaSchema` accepts both legacy strings and the struct shape and normalizes string entries to `{text, source: 'manual'}` on parse. **Asymmetry to know about (TODO):** the cc-review path doesn't currently populate `voice_corpus.added_by_operator_id`; only `addCorpusEntry` does. Track for backfill in a future ticket.
- `lib/voices/` — Critique → regen → commit loop helpers that drive the live half of the Voices command-center playground (THE-238). Distinct from `lib/voice-training/` which owns CRUD: this folder owns inference + persistence around critiques. `regenerateWithCritique({venueId, originalMessageId, critique})` rebuilds runtime context with history pinned to the moment of the original outbound's triggering inbound, classifies + retrieves + generates a fresh response with the operator's critique injected, and returns a single attempt (multi-attempt state lives client-side). **Coupling: this helper deliberately mirrors the wiring in `lib/agent/stages.ts` — if retrieval thresholds, knowledge gating, or post-generation logic change there, mirror them here.** `classifyCritique({critique, badResponse, goodResponse})` is the commit-modal Sonnet call deciding edit_only vs edit_and_rule + synthesizing a candidate ruleText (operator overrides both before commit fires). `persistCritique({...})` embeds + inserts a `voice_critiques` row. `findPatternClusterForCritique({...})` and `findActiveClusters(venueId)` run cosine-search → verification per the cluster-detection pipeline. Pure helpers (`-pure.ts`) split the prompt builders + threshold logic out so module-load SDK init doesn't trip vitest.
- `lib/tunables/` — Hand-maintained manifest of operational tunables (TAC-183). `manifest.ts` re-exports agent / recognition / retrieval / timing constants from their source files with display metadata, consumed by the read-only Command Center viewer at `/admin/tunables`. No registration primitive, no module-load side effects — purely a data file. Read-only by design; editable overrides are Phase 2. Vitest module-load: the manifest test mocks `voyageai` (the only SDK module that trips vitest's ESM directory-import resolver) — adding a tunable that pulls in another heavy SDK at module load may require extending that mock.
- `lib/notifications/` — APNs push pipeline for the operator approval queue (TAC-207) and the commitment-arrival heads-up surface (TAC-297). `apns/jwt.ts` signs the ES256 bearer token using `jose` (5 env vars: `APNS_AUTH_KEY` PEM, `APNS_KEY_ID`, `APNS_TEAM_ID`, `APNS_BUNDLE_ID`, `APNS_ENV`); cached at module scope with a 50-minute refresh window and an explicit invalidation on key-id / team-id rotation. `apns/client.ts` wraps `node:http2` (new pattern — no prior http2 use in the repo) with one-shot `sendApnsRequest(deviceToken, payload)` returning a `RAGResult`-shaped result; one session per request, no pooling at pilot scale. `env.ts` is the pure shape validator for the five `APNS_*` vars (`checkApnsEnv`, layer-scoped via `JWT_APNS_VARS` / `TRANSPORT_APNS_VARS`; never returns key material) — consumed first-call by `client.ts` + `jwt.ts` and ambiently by `/admin/health`. `push-policy.ts` owns the fire/skip decision as a TOTAL `satisfies Record<ApprovalTrigger, PushDecision>` map (deny-list: everything pushes except `previous_pending_held`) — deliberately separate from the context-label map so the two can't drift into one constant again. `send.ts` is the draft-flagged orchestrator: `shouldSendDraftFlaggedPush(primaryTrigger)` (re-exported from `push-policy.ts`) skips only `previous_pending_held` and fails OPEN on unknown triggers; `sendDraftFlaggedPush({agentRunId, venueId, guestId, guestFirstName, draftId, primaryTrigger})` fans out to every operator whose allowlist covers the venue, computes the badge using the same predicate as `list_operator_queue`, POSTs to APNs, handles 410 Gone / 400 BadDeviceToken by nulling the token columns. **`send-commitment-push.ts` (TAC-297)** is the sibling for the commitment-arrival surface — `sendCommitmentArrivalPush({commitmentId, venueId, guestId, guestFirstName, type, code, expectedArrival, arrivalSignal, venueTimezone, agentRunId?})` fired from `handle-inbound.ts` (imminent CAS win) and the `/api/cron/commitments-due` processor (scheduled fires). Same `loadRecipients` + token-invalid handling, but the badge predicate combines pending drafts + pending_ack commitments across the operator's allowed venues — single source of truth across both push surfaces. Payload `{ aps: {alert: {title, body}, badge, sound: "default"}, commitmentId, guestId, operatorId }` — content-free (no commitment description, no inbound text). Body `"{firstName} arriving {context} — {typeLabel}{ code}"`. PostHog discriminator: `surface: 'commitment_arrival'`. Both surfaces never throw. **`recipients.ts` (TAC-473) is the shared half, and the duplication caveat that stood here is RESOLVED.** `loadPushRecipients`, `countPendingDraftsForOperator`, `countOperatorBadge` and `clearOperatorPushToken` were copied between `send.ts` and `send-commitment-push.ts` from TAC-297 until a third surface arrived. Pure extraction: every query, guard and log line byte-identical, the log prefix passed in as a parameter so neither caller's output moved, and the 80 existing tests across `lib/notifications` unchanged as the evidence. **What the extraction made VISIBLE rather than fixed: the two badge counts genuinely disagree.** `countPendingDraftsForOperator` counts pending drafts; `countOperatorBadge` counts drafts PLUS pending_ack commitments, under a docstring that called itself the single source of truth for both surfaces — which it never was. `send.ts` still uses the first and `send-commitment-push.ts` the second, so the same operator's badge is one number when a draft queues and another when a commitment arrives. Both kept with their existing callers, because making them agree changes what an operator sees and is a product decision, not a refactor; they now sit in one file where the disagreement can be read. **A new surface should use `countOperatorBadge`** — a badge that ignores commitments under-reports what is waiting. **`send-instagram-window-push.ts` (TAC-473)** is the third surface: `sendInstagramWindowWarningPush({draftId, venueId, guestId, guestFirstName, remainingMs})`, fired from the cron processor below when a held Instagram draft has an hour left. Body `"{firstName} has {N}m left to reply on Instagram"`, minutes rounded DOWN so the number never promises more time than there is, and no em dash (the `REVIEW_REASON_LABELS` rule — read fast on a phone mid-shift). Content-free like its siblings: no message body, no guest handle. PostHog discriminator `surface: 'instagram_window_warning'`. **The caller must already have won the CAS claim** on `messages.window_warning_pushed_at`; this does not re-check it, exactly as `sendCommitmentArrivalPush` trusts `transitionToPendingAck`'s rowcount.

### Scripts

- `scripts/` — top-level CLI entry points. Each is a thin orchestrator that reads args, sets up clients, calls helpers, logs progress.
- `scripts/onboarding/` — helpers used by the onboarding pipeline scripts. One helper module per pipeline step. Helpers may be split into `<name>-pure.ts` (no `@/*` imports, vitest-loadable) and `<name>.ts` (DB-touching wrapper) when tests need to load the pure logic — see "Module split for testability" below. Modules: `airtable.ts` (transcript fetch), `menu-csv.ts` (CSV parser), `parse-venue-spec.ts` (Zod-strict venue-spec parser; the offline boundary referenced in the permissive-schema gotcha; **TAC-343 Phase 0** stops silently dropping `staff[].notes` on the way to the flattened `venue_info.staff` roster string — any non-empty `notes` is routed into a synthesized `staff_<slug(name)>` `knowledge_corpus` entry, appended alongside whatever the extraction itself wrote, so the content survives whether or not extraction independently covered it), `seed-supabase.ts` (helper imported by `scripts/seed-venue.ts`; **TAC-343 Phase 0b** adds a `force?: boolean` option to `seedVenue()` — the already-exists guard still hard-refuses by default; `force: true` deletes and rewrites CONFIG STORES ONLY (`venue_configs`, `mechanics`, `voice_corpus`+embeddings, `knowledge_corpus`+embeddings), never the `venues` row itself and never any guest-relationship table, and refuses outright — even with the flag — if the venue has any `guests` or `messages` rows, so it can never erase real guest history; nothing in this repo passes it yet), `extract.ts` (LLM-extraction orchestrator; exports `buildExtractionSystemPrompt` (TAC-331) as a same-file pure split — no `@/*` imports to strip here, just a network call to keep out of the unit-testable prompt-content path — so the extraction routing/mood rules are covered by `extract.test.ts` without hitting Anthropic; **TAC-343 Phase 0** adds a knowledge_corpus GRANULARITY rule — one entry per self-contained claim, never several combined, each entry must name its own subject since `chunkText()`'s character-count splitting downstream has no idea where one item ends and the next begins; **TAC-346** tightens the voice/knowledge/persona/mechanics/staff placement rules described under "Extraction hardening" below and imports `MECHANIC_TRIGGER_TYPES` from `lib/schemas/mechanic.ts` rather than hand-copying it), `verify.ts` (TAC-346, NEW — the post-extraction verification pass; `runVerification` via `generateObject`, `VerifyResultSchema`, `countVoiceCorpusEntries` (pure, mechanical — never delegated to the model), `formatNeedsConfirmationSection` (pure renderer for the `## Needs confirmation` markdown); own `VERIFY_PROMPT_VERSION`, independent of `extract.ts`'s contract, same independence rationale as `EXTRACT_REPORTED_ORDER_PROMPT_VERSION`), `extract-venue-spec-args.ts` (TAC-346, NEW — `parseArgs` + the pure `shouldRefuseOverwrite` guard decision for `scripts/extract-venue-spec.ts`, split out specifically so they're importable from a test without importing the entry script itself: the entry script's unconditional top-level `main()` call means importing it directly would trigger a real run, and a `import.meta.url === file://${process.argv[1]}` main-module guard is NOT a safe fix — that comparison silently never matches on a path containing characters `import.meta.url` percent-encodes, such as spaces or a curly apostrophe, which this repo's own path has), plus `extract-test-scenarios.ts`, `run-test-scenarios.ts`, and `ingest-response-review-pure.ts`. `run-sheet.ts` (NEW, post-TAC-347) is the pure serializer for the 07-sheet's **`Run` tab** — one row per scenario (`sample_id`, `topic`, `category`, `scenario_source`, `mode`, `guest_state`, `inbound_message`, `outcome`, `route`, `primary_trigger`, `all_triggers`, `voice_fidelity`, `reply`, and all three grades — knowledge/voice/routing, each with verdict + reason — plus `expected_behavior_verdict`/`expected_behavior_reason`, and — TAC-358 — the trailing `retrieved_chunk_ids`/`retrieved_chunk_scores` pair). **Those last two are deliberately two columns rather than one `id@score` column**: ids are stable across runs and are what a run-to-run diff by `sample_id` compares, while scores move on every embed and would make that diff noisy; they stay index-aligned, the nth id being the nth score. `retrieved_chunk_ids` carries the `knowledge_corpus` row id, NOT the `knowledge_embeddings` chunk id — 1:1 on today's data, but the corpus id is the one a human can act on (it's what the admin venues page shows and what a retag targets), and a corpus row chunked into several embeddings correctly repeats its id. **Two limits on how far these columns can be read, both load-bearing for anyone recalibrating retrieval.** (1) They are **post-floor SURVIVORS ONLY** — `retrieveKnowledgeStage` returns `filterByRelevance(...)`, so the smallest score that can ever appear is `KNOWLEDGE_RELEVANCE_FLOOR` itself and a near miss (0.4971 against a 0.5 floor) is invisible here. That is precisely the number a floor recalibration needs, so calibration evidence has to come from a direct probe against the corpus, not from this tab; capturing pre-filter scores would mean changing agent-runtime code. (2) An empty pair has SEVERAL causes and they are not equally diagnosable. The crisis-safety short circuit and a throw predating retrieval are identifiable from `outcome`/`primary_trigger`; but every-chunk-below-the-relevance-floor, zero-rows-clearing-the-confidence-floor, and a knowledge-retrieval **degrade** (an RPC or query-embed failure, which only `console.warn`s and returns `[]`) all render identically on an otherwise-normal `sent` row. **Do not read an empty pair as proof the floor is too high.** What the columns do buy, and what was un-observable before they existed, is the distinction between a reply grounded in retrieved `knowledge_corpus` chunks and one grounded only in `venue_info` — which reads identically in the generated text, and is why the TAC-358 floor miscalibration went unnoticed. Sibling to `report-sheet.ts`'s `Report` tab, different shape: `Report` is aggregates/samples/a capped review list, `Run` is the full uncapped per-scenario detail a run-to-run diff by `sample_id` needs. `scripts/run-test-scenarios.ts` (the CLI) writes it automatically on every run via `ensureTabExists` + `writeTabValues`, same overwrite-wholesale pattern as `Report` — it's a snapshot of the latest run, not an accumulating history across runs.
- `scripts/onboarding/fixtures/` — repo-resident input fixtures consumed by extraction scripts (e.g., `venue-spec-example.md`, `test-scenarios-example.md`)
- `scripts/onboarding/drive.ts` — shared Drive integration. Exports `getDrive`, `findVenueFolder`, `listVenueFiles`, `findByPrefix`, `readDriveFileAsText`, `writeMarkdownFile`, `writeJsonFile`, `writeSheetFile`. Use these instead of inlining Drive calls.
- `scripts/measurement/run-log.ts` (TAC-426) — the shared helper behind the "Measurement harness convention" below. `createRunLog({ name, outputPath?, force?, meta, now?, gitSha? })` returns a `RunLog` whose `appendUnit(unit)` flushes one JSON-Lines line per call — the checkpoint itself, not a buffer flushed at the end. No `outputPath` → a timestamped default (`${name}-<ISO>.jsonl`, numeric-suffixed if the exact millisecond collides) that can never overwrite a prior run; an explicit `outputPath` that already exists throws unless `force: true`, mirroring `seed-venue`'s hard-refuse-then-`--force` shape. The first line written is a header (`{__meta__: true, ...meta, generatedAt, gitSha}`) — `meta.arm` plus whatever the caller wants frozen (prompt version, the constant under test) — so a `.jsonl` file states what produced it without the script that wrote it; `gitSha` defaults to `git rev-parse HEAD`, `null` outside a repo. `readRunLog(path)` is the paired reader. Colocated `run-log.test.ts` runs against a real `fs.mkdtempSync` temp dir, not a mocked `fs` — same reasoning CLAUDE.md gives for `run-report.mjs`'s real-git-repo test: a fake answers only the arguments it was written for. Importable from any throwaway `scripts/sandbox/*.ts` harness (gitignored) at zero extra cost; this module itself is not a runnable script.
- `scripts/measurement/first-touch-question.ts` + `first-touch-question-detector.ts` + `first-touch-question-score.ts` (TAC-423, extended by TAC-519) — **the harness for the `## What you're hoping to get to` block, and the thing to re-run before changing it.** Two modes: `--mode first-touch` synthesises the QR opener turn (TAC-423's subject); `--mode ordinary` replays the real production turns that actually rendered intentions (TAC-519's subject, and **the only mode the block's POSITION is measurable in** — on a first-touch turn every block between its old slot and its new one is empty, so the two prompts are byte-identical and the arms cannot differ). Arms are string transformations of one composed prompt per rep, each guarded to match exactly once or the unit is INVALID. The judge is production's own `classifyIntentionPrompts` rather than a regex, because the detector-asymmetry trap under "Measurement harness convention" bit this harness twice and no regex here has a name-question pattern. `first-touch-question-score.ts` re-scores a finished run log, so a detector fix costs no new model calls.
- `scripts/measurement/intention-block-move.ts` (TAC-519) — the pure transformation behind the `position` arm: lifts the intentions block out of a composed user prompt and reinserts it before the emoji directive, so the move was MEASURED before any shipped code changed. Refuses rather than guesses on any prompt shape it does not recognise, because an arm that quietly differs in more than one variable is worse than a missing one. **Two things in it are derived rather than written out, each after a wrong version shipped past its own tests**: the whole-line header match is built from `INTENTIONS_HEADER` (a re-typed regex silently matches nothing after a rename), and the block/tail boundary is the SECOND-TO-LAST blank line of the final element, which follows from `runtimeToProse`'s structure (the tail always contributes the last one) rather than from a heuristic about the first or last blank line — both were tried and both were wrong, the second caught by the test written for the first.
- `scripts/measurement/ordinary-turn-selection.ts` (TAC-519) — selects the replay set: every outbound row with a non-empty `messages.rendered_intentions`, resolved back through `reply_to_message_id` to the inbound it answered. Read-only, `SELECT`s only. Each turn replays on ITS OWN guest and takes `openIntentions` from that turn's own stored set (through production's `parseRenderedIntentionsForRecording`) rather than re-deriving, so arming, gating, the brake and expiry cannot drift between the arms and the turn replayed. Every candidate is either used or recorded with a skip reason. **`buildRuntimeContext` can still persist a `guest_states` row on a recognition-band change; nothing automates that check** and the 2026-09-23 run was verified by hand (25 rows before and after).
- `scripts/measurement/instagram-channel-copy.ts` + `channel-language.ts` (TAC-469 pre-flight) — the first checked-in user of `createRunLog`, and the answer to the one pre-flight item no test can settle: **does a reply generated for an Instagram conversation still talk like SMS?** `compose-prompt.test.ts` proves TAC-495's phrase swaps are in the PROMPT; a prompt is an instruction, and only generation shows whether the model obeys it. Generate-only — nothing is sent and nothing is written. **The two arms differ in exactly one variable**: the context is built once per scenario from a real venue, guest and corpus, then `conversationChannel` is overridden per arm. Resolving the channel honestly instead would mean an Instagram guest in one arm and a phone guest in the other, varying the guest, their history, their name and their recognition state alongside the channel, so no difference in the output could be attributed to the copy. The eight scenarios PULL FOR channel language rather than sample typical traffic (each carries its own `why`), because a run of hours questions reports clean and proves very little. `channel-language.ts` is the pure detector, and it separates **`phone_claim`** (false on Instagram: "text us", "this number", "SMS", "give us a call") from **`instagram_idiom`** (true but off-copy: "DM us", "our stories") — the Instagram copy deliberately says "message", never "DM", so a run must never report an idiom as a false claim. It reports the matched phrase with surrounding text rather than a score, because the verdict on a borderline line is a judgement someone makes by reading it. Run with `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` and `SLACK_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL` unset so the stages' telemetry goes inert.
- `scripts/measurement/date-phrasing.ts` + `date-language.ts` (TAC-520) — does the agent state a date the way a person would, or the way a system would? Generate-only; nothing sent, nothing written. **Its two arms are two RUNS of the file, not two passes inside one**, and that is forced by what is under test: the Instagram harness can flip `conversationChannel` per arm because the channel is a runtime field, but here the variable is the SYSTEM PROMPT, so the arms are `--arm before` on a worktree at `origin/main` and `--arm after` with the rule applied. `createRunLog` stamps the prompt version and git sha into each file's header, which is what tells them apart; compare by `scenarioId`. **The injected `currentContext` entries are computed from today, never hardcoded** — a harness measuring "the agent says dates like a system" that itself went stale next month would be absurd, and the incident entry ("planned for <this month> <this year>") only reproduces if it tracks the clock. **`--reps` defaults to 5 because generation is temperature 0.7, and 5 IS NOT ENOUGH** — one body is a draw, not a property (the TAC-409 lesson), and on TAC-520 two runs of identical code gave 4/5 and 1/5 on the same metric. The default is a smoke-test size. Use `--only <scenarioId> --reps 20` for anything a decision rests on; that flag exists because a six-scenario run cannot afford the reps it needs. It runs the real grounding backstop in the loop, because in production the incident draft was HELD rather than sent, so a run measuring generation alone measures something other than what ships; it also answers whether a prompt change makes the model hold more drafts, which is how TAC-520 found its wide version pushing 4 of 5 onto an operator card. `date-language.ts` is the pure detector and **three of its four kinds are not defects on their own**: `year_stated`, `numeric_date`, `month_named` (correct for something genuinely months out, so a flag to READ), and `person_shaped` as the positive counter, without which a reply that dodges the question entirely scores like one that answers it well. Its guards run in the direction that matters where they run at all: a slash-only date pattern (a dot separator fires on every price), `24/7` excluded, full weekday names only (bare `sat`/`sun` are an ordinary verb and noun), and "may" matched only where it reads as a month rather than as a modal verb. **But `person_shaped` is ADVISORY, not a verdict, and it does have false positives in the flattering direction**: it matches a temporal word, not a statement about the thing asked about, so "we get busy on the weekend", "we're closed Monday" and R2's own prescribed "10pm tonight" all score a win while saying nothing about when the event is. Four such cases are pinned as known non-goals in its test file. Never read a `person_shaped` count as evidence an arm answered better. **What it cannot do is judge truth** — the wide TAC-520 rule scored better on every count while saying "This Thursday" about a Friday, so a run of this harness is read by reading the bodies, not the table. Run with `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` and `SLACK_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL` unset.
- `scripts/measurement/coalesce-window.ts` (TAC-526) — what would the settle window actually have caught? The ticket said of the number *"propose a number with reasoning; we will measure rather than argue about it"*, so `COALESCE_SETTLE_MS = 8_000` is the proposal and this is what moves it on evidence. **Read-only**: it SELECTs `messages` and writes nothing — no sends, no claims, no ledger rows, no model calls — so it is safe against production, which is the only place the data exists. For every inbound it computes the gap to that guest's previous inbound and replays a range of candidate windows over the same data, so the cost of moving the constant is a table rather than a guess. **Three things it cannot tell you, stated because the table looks more authoritative than it is:** it counts gaps between INBOUND rows and cannot see whether the agent replied in between, so `repliedBetween` is reported per pair and that population has to be excluded by whoever reads it; it is blind to the EXTENSION, which catches a mid-generation fragment whatever the window is, so the settle's true marginal value is SMALLER than the burst count suggests; and gaps are computed on `created_at` for both channels, because Instagram rows carry Meta's clock in `provider_sent_at` and Sendblue rows never do, so ordering on it would sort the two channels on different clocks. Rows sort on `(created_at, id)`, the same total order `pickNewer` uses, because one Instagram delivery can insert several rows in the same millisecond. Output through `createRunLog` per the harness convention, one row per pair, checkpointed rather than buffered.
- `scripts/measurement/channel-self-reference-replay.ts` (TAC-502, `npm run measure-channel-self-reference`) — does handing the grounding verifier the conversation's channel stop it flagging TRUE statements about that channel, without making anything else permissible? Verifier-only: it calls `verifyGrounding` directly against **hand-built, self-contained fixtures**, so no database, no venue lookup, no generation and no send, and the bodies cannot drift underneath the thing being measured. Needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so it cannot run in CI, same posture as `measure-order-attribution.ts` and `prose-promise-catch-rate.ts`. **Two arms, one variable: whether the `## Conversation channel` section is in the source material.** `channel` supplies the fixture's real channel (what production does now); `null` supplies none, reproducing the source material a pre-TAC-502 call had. **Be precise about the `null` arm, because it is easy to overclaim**: it runs against the v1.6.0 SYSTEM PROMPT, so it is "new prompt, no channel section", never a measurement of v1.5.0. That is the right control — the bullet is explicitly conditional on the section being present, so with no section it has no referent — but the distinction belongs in any report of the numbers. **The arm-integrity check is the reason the control arm exists**: the two self-reference fixtures must flag in the `null` arm, or the replay has not reproduced the defect and can say nothing about whether the fix addressed it — and a silently broken arm produces exactly the "the fix works" shape (the trap `grounding-entry-replay.ts`'s own header documents paying for). Eight fixtures: two self-reference (text and Instagram — the Instagram half being the gap the audit named, since every prior run on this defect hard-coded text), two TAC-501-shaped numbers named for someone not in the conversation, the two genuine production catches AC5 names with each body verbatim, and two added on code review. **`self_referential_number_on_text`** writes a number out and presents it as THIS conversation's number, which is where the bullet's first half and its number exclusion pull hardest against each other and which neither other number fixture reached. **`cross_channel_future_promise_on_text`** is the Q1 boundary made measurable: a bare same-channel promise ("I'll text you when I hear back") is not independently an unsupported claim, so a clean verdict there is ambiguous between "the scope held" and "there was nothing to flag" — which is why the plan declined to fixture it — but naming the OTHER channel is independently ungrounded, so a widened exemption would show up as a clean cell. **A flag fixture must also name the RIGHT claim** (`claimMustMatch`), because the script collected every claim and read none of them: `hold_promise_no_holds` carries a hold promise AND a channel-adjacent line, so flagging only the channel line is a false positive that would still score 10/10 on the fixture whose job is proving the hold flags. That is the `comp_regex_backstop` shape — a gate whose green signal was never checked against what it fired on. It named the hold, 10/10. **The sharpest of them is `hold_promise_no_holds`**, because that reply contains a genuine hold promise AND a channel-adjacent line in the same breath, so an exemption that over-applied would take the whole reply clean. **The two arms are held to DIFFERENT criteria, and the split is deliberate.** The `channel` arm is the claim under test and is strict: every repeat must go the expected way, since the point of repeating is to see instability and a 3/5 reported as a pass hides the "no stable verdict at all" case TAC-409 found. The `null` arm of a self-reference fixture is a CONTROL and only has to reproduce the defect — flag at least a third of the repeats, and more often than the channel arm — because the defect is a probabilistic verdict at temperature 0.2 rather than a deterministic rule, and the ticket's own prior measurement counted cells at 5/5 and 1/5 alike as evidence of it. **The floor exists because the first criterion was weaker than its own prose**: "more often than the channel arm" collapses to "at least once" whenever the channel arm passes, since a passing channel arm is 0 by definition, so at REPEATS=5 a single flag would have printed as "the defect reproduced and the comparison means something". Caught in code review, not by the run. The `null` arm of a flag fixture stays strict, because those test rules that should not depend on chance. That loosening was made after a real run returned 2/5 and 4/5, and is recorded as a criterion change rather than applied quietly. **Measured at REPEATS=10, 160 calls, zero failed: self-reference 0/10 on both channels in the `channel` arm against 10/10 (text) and 9/10 (Instagram) in the control; every one of the six flag fixtures 10/10 in the channel arm.** So the exemption did not leak, the two production catches AC5 names still flag, and the two boundaries the ruling drew are measured rather than only asserted in prompt text. **One cell missed and it is reported rather than smoothed over**: `self_referential_number_on_text` flagged 9/10 in the CONTROL arm against a strict every-repeat expectation. That arm has no channel section, so the miss is baseline instability on that body WITHOUT the fix, not a leak — the channel arm is 10/10, i.e. more consistent with the section than without it. The criterion was deliberately NOT loosened to absorb it. **Two traps this script paid for, both worth carrying to the next harness.** (1) **A failed call flags nothing, so a fixture bug reads as a clean measurement.** The first run cast its `venueInfo` fixture (`{...} as VenueInfo`, menu items shaped `{name, priceCents}` against a schema wanting `category` and `isOffMenu`), `formatMenuItems` threw on `a.category.localeCompare`, ALL 60 calls failed — and the report printed "flagged 0/5 ... as expected" for the two fixtures whose clean result IS the ticket's claim. Fixed twice over: the fixture is `VenueInfoSchema.parse`d so a malformed one throws at startup, and no cell with a failed call can meet its expectation whatever its flag count reads. (2) **An unfaithful reconstruction is not a control.** The AC5 order-history fixture first put a Pink Panther in `## Visit history` and went 1/5 and 0/5; TAC-483's own checked-in fixture records that the live prompt held one blossom tonic and NO Pink Panther, because that row was written by the fire-and-forget extractor after the turn's inbound. Corrected against the repo's record, it is 10/10 — tuning the fixture until it flagged would have been fitting the evidence to the answer.
- `scripts/measurement/prose-promise-catch-rate.ts` + `fixtures/prose-promise-replies.json` (TAC-401) — the replay behind the measured catch rate under *Approval policy gates*. A replay against FIXED bodies rather than a fresh generation run: the 220 synthetic replies from the 2026-09-15 measurement, every one hand-read and labelled, so the check is the only variable and the bodies cannot drift underneath it. Reports **four cases, not a rate** (at n=4 an aggregate reads as a precision the measurement does not have), false positives **per category** (an apology idiom and a reply that offers nothing fail for different reasons and have different fixes), and N repeats per body because the check runs at temperature 0.2 and one verdict is a draw, not a property of the body. Run with `npm run measure-prose-promise`; `REPEATS` and `CONCURRENCY` are env overrides. It calls `lib/ai/verify-prose-promise.ts` DIRECTLY, not the stage, so it fires no telemetry and does NOT exercise the stage's skips or its retry — what is under test is the check's judgement, which is what a prompt change moves. The fixture is synthetic bodies only; **no production message body is in it and none may be added**, because this repo is public.
- `scripts/measurement/prose-promise-elliptical.ts` + `fixtures/prose-promise-elliptical.json` (TAC-527, `npm run measure-prose-promise-elliptical`) — does handing the prose-promise check the guest's own message let it catch an ELLIPTICAL promise ("ugh, that's on us too") without making anything else flaggable? Verifier-only against hand-built pairs, so no database, no generation, no send, and the bodies cannot drift; needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, same posture as its TAC-401 sibling. **Two arms, one variable: whether the guest's message is supplied.** `body_only` is the control, and **it runs the v1.1.0 prompt with NO guest message, so it is "new prompt, no inbound" and never a measurement of v1.0.0** — the same caveat `channel-self-reference-replay.ts` carries, and the distinction belongs in any report of the numbers. **The arms are held to DIFFERENT criteria on purpose**: `with_inbound` is the claim under test and is strict (every repeat), because a 6/10 reported as a pass hides the no-stable-verdict case; a `body_only` cell on an elliptical row only has to REPRODUCE the defect, since the miss is probabilistic at temperature 0.2; a `body_only` cell on a must-stay-clean row is strict, because those rows test rules that should not depend on chance. A failed call disqualifies its cell whatever the flag count reads (TAC-502's replay counted errored calls as "did not flag" and scored a wholly broken run as clean). Fourteen rows, five labels, and the criteria live in `EXPECTATION`, a total `satisfies Record<Label, Record<Arm, Expectation>>` map — per-arm, because a boolean plus a special case could not express "flag in BOTH arms", which is what the three `explicit_promise` rows guard. A new label has to state both arms, and a fixture row whose label is not a key of it exits 1 before spending a call (the `satisfies` guard covers the code side; labels are written in JSON, which has no compiler). Synthetic only; the fixture's note records the provenance of the one row shaped after the operator's own device test. **Read the bodies, not the table** — the `names:` lines are printed for exactly that, because a rate cannot tell a correct catch from one that named the wrong item, which is how the `ell-11` finding below surfaced.
- `scripts/measurement/complaint-then-report.ts` (TAC-513, now TAC-514's evidence base) — the second checked-in user of `createRunLog`, measuring whether a plain report of a second item after a complaint still gets comped. Generate-only; nothing is sent and nothing is written. Three arms: `off` is the SHIPPED prompt untouched, `on` and `candidate` INJECT their paragraph after the block's opening assertion. **That direction is the inversion worth knowing**: during TAC-513 the paragraph was briefly committed and `off` was "shipped minus the paragraph", sliced out of the live constant; once it was reverted (ruled 2026-09-22) that guard could never match again and the harness would have refused to run forever. Injecting keeps it usable with nothing unshipped sitting in `comp-complaint.ts`. Two startup guards, and both have caught something: the anchor must still be in the block, or every injecting arm composes identically to `off` and the run measures nothing; and the paragraph must NOT already be shipped, or `off` is not a baseline. Four things it does that a first validation run forced, each with the reasoning in the file. **It FORCES `category: 'comp_complaint'`**: the classifier returned `reply` for the incident's own wording, so the block never rendered and both arms were byte-identical, which the guard caught. Forcing is right rather than a workaround — the incident turn WAS classified `comp_complaint` and the fix under test is scoped to that category's generation — and the classifier's own verdict is still logged, which turned out to be the most valuable number in the run (0/50 `comp_complaint` on plain reports, 50/50 on genuine second complaints, so the incident's misread was context-driven). **It composes the prompt and calls `generateObject` directly** rather than going through `generateStage`, because the category instructions are selected inside `composePrompt` and no parameter, context field or option can vary them per arm; the cost, stated in the file, is that it measures GENERATION rather than what ships. **It appends `VOICE_FIDELITY_INSTRUCTION` exactly as `generateMessage` does** — 11 of 14 first-run generations threw `response did not match schema` without it, because `composePrompt` does not include it and the model then answers `voiceFidelity` on a 1-to-10 scale against a `[0,1]` refine; four byte-identical re-asks could not fix it, which is how it showed as systematic rather than intermittent. **It neutralises every other thing the guest carries** (`recentVisits`, `guest.context`, `openIntentions`, `pendingQuestion`), because this is the incident guest and the model quoted its own history back: "Last time they said this, it turned out the blossom tonic was fine." That would not bias the arm comparison but it can suppress the defect on BOTH arms, and an `off` arm that does not reproduce proves nothing either way. **Every scenario item is on the venue's real menu**, because an earlier set used generic cafe items and the model correctly answered "we don't actually have a matcha on the menu", which would have scored as the desired question while measuring item existence. **Run-to-run variance is large and is the reason to pool**: the identical `off` arm scored 11/50 then 18/50 on the defect population and 15/25 then 11/25 on the control, same code and same N, across two runs an hour apart.
- `scripts/lib/` — shared, pure, testable helpers consumed by top-level scripts that aren't part of the onboarding pipeline (`scripts/onboarding/` owns that one). Plain `.mjs` (no `@/*` imports, no SDK init at module load — these run inside GitHub Actions workflow steps, not this app's Next.js/vitest process, so they colocate a `module.test.ts` the same way `scripts/onboarding/*-pure.ts` modules do, importing the `.mjs` directly rather than needing a `-pure` split). `comment-provenance.mjs` (TAC-396) is the first: `unescapeBrackets`, `isBotComment`, `commentMarker`, `isRulingComment`, `isContextChatComment` — the shared, tested definition of "does this Linear comment open with the `**[FROM CLAUDE CODE]**` prefix, and what's its marker," extracted out of `scripts/slack-rulings.mjs`'s own inline regex so the two can't drift the way `build-ready.yml`'s and `audit-new-todo.yml`'s duplicated jq once did. `isRulingComment`/`isContextChatComment` have no call site in code: their consumers are the CHAT-vs-RULING rule in `.claude/process.md`'s "Comments" section and `.claude/commands/work-ticket.md`'s Phase 0 step 2b, prose read by an LLM rather than code that imports a JS function. Don't read them as dead code to clean up. That rule and the unescape-then-`startsWith` rule landed in the prose in a second TAC-396 PR, after a CI session was refused writes to both files as "sensitive" with no human present to grant it. **`build-ready.yml`'s jq resume check still applies neither**: it anchors on the CC prefix without unescaping, so it can start a session on a plain `[FROM CLAUDE CHAT]` comment or on an escaped CC prefix, and the session applies both rules. That gap is pinned as a `KNOWN GAP` test in `analog-operator` PR #57 and closes in both repos together or neither. `bash-allowlist.ts` (TAC-471) is the one `.ts` module here, and test-only: nothing in a workflow imports it. It is the model of Claude Code's `Bash(x)` and `Bash(x:*)` rules, with `permits` (an allow rule admits the command and no deny rule does), `permitsCommandLine` (each part of a compound command checked, the shell forms the build prompt says CI denies refused, one `cd` inside the checkout admitted) and the readers for a workflow's `claude_args`, shared by `linear-prompts.test.ts` and `bash-allowlist.test.ts`. The second checks the build allowlist against written-out lists of permitted, refused and known-gap commands, every command all of `work-ticket.md`, the build prompt and CLAUDE.md's test baseline teach, and CLAUDE.md's own lists of what stays refused and what passes.
- `scripts/linear.mjs` (TAC-444) — how a CI Claude Code session writes to Linear: `comment <issue> <file.md>`, `describe <issue> <file.md>`, `label add|remove <issue> "<name>"`, `state <issue> "<name>"`. The text of a comment or description comes from a plain markdown file the session writes with the Write tool, so nothing is JSON-escaped by hand; the helper looks up every id, posts comments flat, and exits 0 only when Linear returns `success: true` (1 on a failed write, 2 on bad usage or a missing key). It reads `LINEAR_API_KEY` from its environment, sends it only as the Authorization header, and redacts it from every line it prints. It refuses a comment that doesn't open with the `**[FROM CLAUDE CODE]**` prefix and a marker, using `comment-provenance.mjs`'s `isBotComment`/`commentMarker` rather than a second copy of the rule, because an unprefixed agent comment reads to the automation as human input and would resume a ticket as if Jaipal had answered. The logic is in `scripts/lib/linear-cli.mjs` (pure: `run` takes injected fetch, readFile, stdout and stderr); the entry only wires the process, and imports nothing outside Node's standard library, because the audit workflow runs it without `npm ci`. `scripts/lib/linear-prompts.test.ts` reads both workflow files and `work-ticket.md` as text, and fails if the two Linear blocks differ, if either teaches a helper call the helper rejects, or if the hand-escaped JSON write form comes back. CI only: locally the Linear MCP is the write path. **Both allowlists carry `Bash(node scripts/linear.mjs:*)`, the helper and no other node command, and no python at all (TAC-449).** They carried `Bash(node:*)` and `Bash(python3:*)` until then, both added by TAC-439 for YAML checks (`node -e`, `python3 -c`) before the helper existed, and nothing taught either for anything else; the narrow entry is the one analog-operator ships (TAC-451), and its audit run 35303513132 shows Claude Code admitting it. Operator's `main` never carried python; its TAC-439 review dropped it as too broad. A script a CI session must run gets an entry of that form, never a bare interpreter: a session that can run any program can read every secret in its environment, `LINEAR_API_KEY` included. `linear-prompts.test.ts` parses both workflows as YAML (operator's test, copied) and fails if either allowlist loses the entry, denies it, or carries any other rule naming node, nodejs or python (any version, with or without a path, so the runners' own `python3.12` too), a wildcard that would admit one, or a bare `Bash`. It does not see a rule that reaches an interpreter another way, such as `Bash(env python3:*)` or `Bash(bash:*)`. `npx vitest run scripts/lib/linear-prompts.test.ts` is now a build session's YAML check for those two files (nothing parses the other six workflows). **The narrow entry removes the obvious door, not the exposure**: a session can Read and rewrite the helper and then run it under this entry, a build session runs code through `npx vitest`, `npm run lint` and git hooks (husky shims the hooks that commit, checkout, pull and push run, and each runs a hook file the session can write), and the taught curl read can send the key to any host. Closing it at the credential is TAC-449's open half.
- `scripts/run-report.mjs` (TAC-447) — what the build workflow's check step says when its session runs into the turn limit. `ending <execution-file> <max-turns>` prints how the session ended: `finished`, `finished-over-limit` (it finished and claude-code-action failed the run afterwards for going over, as run 35288433905 did at 128 against 120), `stopped-at-limit` (the CLI's own `error_max_turns`), `errored` or `no-record`. `notice <ticket> <execution-file> <max-turns>` prints the comment for the two limit endings, `[TURN-LIMIT]` (blocking) or `[OVER-LIMIT]` (bookkeeping), and nothing otherwise. Both report what reached GitHub, read from the runner's own git refs after the session: `git push` moves `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` only when it succeeds, and the checkout fetched every branch at the start. They also list what each side folder holds uncommitted (TAC-471): every worktree `git worktree list --porcelain` names after the checkout, read with `git -C <path> status --porcelain`, because a resume edits its branch in a gitignored folder the checkout's own status cannot see. A side folder git cannot read, or a worktree list it cannot read, is reported as unknown, never as none. Logic in `scripts/lib/run-report.mjs` (pure, injected `git` and `readFile`, key redacted through `linear-cli.mjs`'s `redact`), which has a test against a real temporary git repository, because a fake `git` answers only the arguments it was written for and cannot tell a wrong range from a right one. Run by the workflow, never by the session, so no allowlist applies, and from a copy the workflow takes before the session starts (`$RUNNER_TEMP/turn-limit-reporter`): by the time it runs, the checkout is the session's branch, which may predate the script or be a ticket that edits it. If it fails, the check step falls back to its pre-TAC-447 behaviour.
- `scripts/claims.mjs` (TAC-448) — the build selection's check that no other session has a ticket before it takes one. The queue step's jq lists every candidate, in priority order and without a limit, with its comments and the time its ruling landed (`newestAt`); `node scripts/claims.mjs` skips each claimed one with a `skipped <ticket> (<mode>, <state>): another session has it: <reason>` line on stderr, then takes `LIMIT` from the rest, so a claimed ticket never uses up the run. It reads claims through `comment-provenance.mjs` (unescaped prefix, marker right after it), branch commits from the checkout's own `refs/remotes/origin` (the checkout fetched every branch), and open PRs with `gh` (`GH_TOKEN` in the step env). It fails the step when it cannot read the branches or they come back without `main` (nothing fetched from GitHub; a shallow checkout of main still lists `main` and would silently drop every commit signal, so a test pins `fetch-depth: 0`, and that pin, not the guard, protects the scheduled run), and warns and carries on without the PR signal when it cannot list PRs. A local `[CLAIM]` edited to `released` holds nothing; one that is not released holds whatever the ruling time. Logic in `scripts/lib/claims.mjs` (pure, injected `git`/`gh`/`now`); its tests carry TAC-396's real thread and branches from the incident, including the half no check can catch. Liveness has one owner: the jq no longer reads `[POLLING-STATE]` itself, and a test keeps it that way, because two liveness rules is how the resume path went unchecked.
- `scripts/reconcile-status.mjs` (TAC-466) — writes a ticket's status from public GitHub state, every build run: a branch `jaipal/tac-xxx-...` on GitHub moves it to In Progress, a merged PR moves it to Ready For QA. Exists because nothing in this repo's own GitHub-Linear integration attaches an analog-guest PR to its ticket (confirmed 2026-09-18: TAC-467's PR merged after the "Public repositories" integration setting was fixed, and TAC-467 still shows no PR attachment), so the "In Progress on PR open, Ready For QA on merge" behaviour `.claude/process.md` and `work-ticket.md` used to describe never happened here. Both files still need that correction (TAC-466's [NEEDS-ACTION]) — a CI session is refused Edit/Write on either as a sensitive file, with no human present to grant it, the same restriction TAC-396 hit; a human, or a locally-run session where Jaipal can approve the prompt, has to apply it. Reuses `isTicketBranch` / `parseRefs` / `REF_FORMAT` from `claims.mjs` so branch matching can't drift between the claim check and this. The queue step runs it over every owner-matched Ready/In Progress candidate, not just what `claims.mjs` selected this run, and that is safe rather than a second claim signal: a derived status is a projection of public state — a branch existing, a PR having merged — and carries nothing a claim doesn't already carry more precisely, and `claims.test.ts` pins that neither `claimOf` nor `pickUnclaimed` reads `.state`. Forward-only (`deriveTargetStatus` compares against a fixed `PIPELINE`, never invents a status outside it, never moves a ticket backward) and **fails SOFT, the opposite of `claims.mjs`'s fail-closed posture**: an unreadable branch list, an unreadable merged-PR list, or a failed Linear write just leaves that ticket's status stale until the next run, because there is no two-sessions hazard here to fail closed against — "reconciled every run" is what recovers a missed write, not a retry.
- `scripts/pending-question.mjs` (TAC-453) — the build selection's check for a Ready, unblocked candidate whose thread still asks a question nothing has answered: a human cleared `Needs Decision` or `Needs Action` without a reply, so starting the ticket again would only rediscover the same stop and spend the run's one ticket (TAC-447) on it. The queue step's jq narrows `$RESPONSE` to exactly the population it would otherwise call `"start"` (Ready, single-repo-labelled, carrying neither label) and hands `{id, identifier, comments}` to `node scripts/pending-question.mjs`, which returns the ones still pending as `[{id, identifier, label}]`; their identifiers feed `$pendingIds` into the mode `if`, so a flagged ticket is never selected. `pendingQuestionLabel` (`scripts/lib/pending-question.mjs`) reads the newest turn — skipping bookkeeping and a plain, non-ruling `**[FROM CLAUDE CHAT]**` comment, since neither can advance a gate (`comment-provenance.mjs`'s `isBookkeepingComment`/`isContextChatComment`) — and maps its marker to a label: `[NEEDS-INPUT]`/`[PLAN]` → Needs Decision, `[NEEDS-ACTION]` → Needs Action, `[AUDIT]` → Needs Decision only when `auditHasQuestions` finds a real numbered question outside any "Decided without asking" subsection. **Deliberately excludes `[HUMAN-REVIEW-REQUIRED]`** (no label ever belongs there — `.claude/process.md`, "Remove Needs Decision") **and `[BUILD-SKIPPED]`/`[AUDIT-SKIPPED]`/`[SILENT-RUN]`/`[TURN-LIMIT]`** — those four resolve by an edit to the ticket or by fixing whatever the run hit, never by a comment reply, so re-selecting one without a reply isn't guaranteed to repeat itself the way an unanswered question is (`work-ticket.md`'s own `lastQuestionComment` draws the identical line). A flagged ticket gets `[LABEL-DRIFT]` restoring the label it lost, so the drift is visible rather than a silent non-selection. Fails SOFT like `reconcile-status.mjs`, not closed like `claims.mjs`: there is no two-session hazard here, so a read this can't make costs one wasted selection at worst. **Narrower than, and does not replace, TAC-446's planned `deriveNeedsDecision`** (not yet built): that check reconciles whether a label is true in general, for every marker, on every run, silently; this one only stops a ticket from being started on the very run that would otherwise waste on it, for the subset of markers only a reply resolves — see the workflow header for the full division of ownership. `auditHasQuestions` / `isBookkeepingComment` / `BOOKKEEPING_MARKERS` live in `comment-provenance.mjs`, for TAC-446 to import rather than re-add if it lands after this.
- `scripts/reconcile-needs-decision.mjs` (TAC-446) — writes whether `Needs Decision` should be on a ticket, derived from its comment thread, every build run. Exists because the label was set only imperatively — at the point a `[PLAN]` posts, at the point every open question gets ruled — and each of those write sites can be skipped, denied, or simply missed: TAC-396's plan never got the label at all (a denied write), TAC-396's approval ruling never cleared it, and TAC-325's plan ending "Open questions: None" left it on. `deriveNeedsDecision` (`lib/reconcile-needs-decision.mjs`) folds a ticket's comments in `createdAt` order per `.claude/process.md`'s Comments table: a bookkeeping comment (`comment-provenance.mjs`'s `isBookkeepingComment`) is unchanged; `[PLAN]` / `[NEEDS-INPUT]` / `[BUILD-SKIPPED]` / `[AUDIT-SKIPPED]` / `[SILENT-RUN]` / `[TURN-LIMIT]` set it true; `[HUMAN-REVIEW-REQUIRED]` sets it false; `[AUDIT]` sets it to whatever `auditHasOpenQuestions` finds in its `3. QUESTIONS` section (a numbered line outside any `Decided without asking` subsection — tolerant of both the bold `**3. QUESTIONS**` and markdown `## 3. QUESTIONS` headings seen in real audits, and defaulting to true, keep the label, when the heading can't be found at all); any other bot marker (`[NEEDS-ACTION]` — a different label — `[FINDING]`, the `[POLLING-*]` markers, a bot comment with no marker) is unchanged; a plain `**[FROM CLAUDE CHAT]**` comment is unchanged (context, never a decision); anything else — unprefixed human input, or a `**[FROM CLAUDE CHAT — RULING` comment — sets it false. `reconcile` turns a set of candidates into only the writes that disagree with the stored label, skipping any candidate already carrying `Needs Action` (Linear's `Blocked On` group holds at most one, and correcting a simultaneous drift there isn't one of the documented incidents). Needs no `git`/`gh` call, unlike `reconcile-status.mjs` — every candidate already carries its own comments from the same Linear query the queue step already ran. The queue step runs it over the same every-owner-matched-candidate set as the status reconcile, with the same fails-soft posture: a derived label is a projection of the thread, never a claim, so correcting one on a ticket another session has is safe. Its test fixtures are the real comment threads from TAC-396, TAC-325 and TAC-389 (trimmed of prose that doesn't affect classification, never invented), and pin both documented incident moments: the label goes true the instant TAC-396's `[BUILD-SKIPPED]` posts and false the instant its 23:10:24 approval ruling posts (which the real ticket got wrong), and TAC-389's ruling closing every open question clears it too.

### Database

- `db/migrations/` — SQL migrations (single source of DB truth). Hand-written. See "Migrations" section.
- `db/types.ts` — auto-generated by `npm run db:types` against the live Supabase schema. May be hand-patched temporarily after a migration lands but before `db:types` runs; the next `db:types` run overwrites the patch with canonical output.

### Tests

- `*.test.ts` colocated next to source files. Vitest is the runner. Run all: `npx vitest run`. Run single file: `npx vitest run path/to/file.test.ts`.
