## Scripts

One-off scripts live in `scripts/` and run via `tsx` with env loading from `.env.local`. To add a new script: drop the file in `scripts/` (CLI orchestrator) and `scripts/onboarding/<name>.ts` (helpers, if it's part of the onboarding pipeline), add a `package.json` entry of the form `"<name>": "tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/<file>.ts"`, run with `npm run <name> -- <args>`.

### Measurement harness convention (TAC-426)

A measurement harness is a throwaway `scripts/sandbox/*.ts` script (gitignored — `scripts/sandbox` is not checked in) written to answer a question about live system behavior via many expensive AI calls, e.g. "how often does a safety check actually catch a real problem." **Its default shape destroys its own evidence, and this has already cost the project twice in one hour.** On 2026-09-16, `tac394-make-it-right-gate.ts` took its output path as `process.argv[2] ?? 'tac394-make-it-right-gate.json'` — two re-runs without an explicit path silently overwrote a prior 60-reply result set, and only one of three runs survived. [TAC-409](https://linear.app/the-analog-company/issue/TAC-409)'s own replay prep script hit the identical shape within the same hour: it built an expensive fixture set, wrote once at the end, then threw on an unrelated bad UUID and lost every generated body. Neither script is being fixed — they're gone, and per [TAC-426](https://linear.app/the-analog-company/issue/TAC-426) that's out of scope — but the failure is not a mistake anyone makes once; it's the default shape of a script written under time pressure. **This project's rulings rest on these measurements** (TAC-394's 27-of-60, TAC-401's 20-of-60 and 0-of-220, TAC-409's replay) — see "Measured, not predicted" under migration 046 and the single-verdict-sampling gotcha under Common gotchas for why a measurement that can't be re-examined is close to no measurement at all.

Every new measurement harness should follow four properties, not as aspiration but because the failure above is what skipping them produces:

1. **Timestamped output by default.** `results-<ISO>.jsonl`, never a fixed `results.json`. An explicit path may override; the *default* must never collide with a previous run.
2. **Checkpoint as you go.** Write (and flush) after each unit — each generated body, each fixture, each trial — never buffer to one write at the end. The expensive half of a measurement run is the model calls; losing them to a late throw in the cheap half is the specific failure both incidents hit.
3. **Never overwrite an existing results file without an explicit flag**, mirroring `seed-venue`'s hard-refuse-then-`--force` shape (`scripts/onboarding/seed-supabase.ts`).
4. **Record the arm and the code state in the file itself** — prompt version, git SHA, the constant under test. TAC-409's replay needed `VERIFY_GROUNDING_PROMPT_VERSION` inside each row to tell its two arms apart afterwards; a file that doesn't say which arm produced it is not much better than one that was overwritten.

A fifth property is not `run-log`'s to give and belongs to whatever reports the run: **a failed unit is not a result.** A model call that errored produces no verdict, and a harness that counts "how many units came back positive" will score it identically to a unit that came back negative — so a wholly broken run reports as a clean one. TAC-502's replay hit this on its first run (all 60 calls failed on a fixture that had been cast rather than parsed, and the report said "as expected" for the two cells carrying the ticket's whole claim). Make a unit's failure disqualify it from meeting any expectation, and print the failure count per unit rather than only in aggregate.

**The sibling of that, from TAC-526, and it is the sharper version because the failure produced its OWN FALSE PASS: A CRASHED OR SKIPPED RUN IS NOT A RESULT EITHER, AND IT READS AS A SURVIVOR.** Mutation-testing an unbounded recursion (the retry with its depth bound removed) made the vitest WORKER die — `Worker exited unexpectedly` — and a crashed worker STILL PRINTS A SUMMARY LINE. So the harness matched `Tests N passed`, parsed `0 failed`, and reported **SURVIVED** on the two mutants the bound exists for. Twice, across two separate runs, before anyone probed one directly. The loop was real, the mutant was live, and the report said the opposite of all of it.

Three rules follow, and the first is the generalisable one:

- **Check for a crash or a skip BEFORE reading any count.** `Worker exited unexpectedly` and `Tests N skipped` both mean the run did not happen; treat them as INVALID, never as evidence either way. A harness that only knows "failed" and "passed" has no way to say "did not run", which is exactly the state a hang or a crash leaves it in.
- **Make every failing fixture SELF-LIMITING** so a mutant that removes a bound terminates and fails an assertion instead of dying. This repo has now paid for that twice in one ticket: the extension bound (an endless supply of fragments) and the retry bound (an unconditional failure, and a trace-flush control that was a boolean when it needed to be a count). A finite supply turns a hang into a number.
- **A hang and a crash are BAD KILLS even when they do stop the suite**: the harness times out, prints nothing useful, and — worse — leaves the mutant applied on disk, which the next run then measures against. Restore from a file copy and verify the tree before believing the next result.

**A fifth property, added by TAC-423 after paying for it twice in one ticket: a detector that classifies free text must be checked for ASYMMETRY between the arms, not just for accuracy.**

That harness compared a prompt that SCRIPTED a question against one that left the model to write its own, and scored the replies with an exact-phrase list. It broke twice, and both times in the same direction:

1. The list held `what did you get`. The scripted arm echoed that long form and matched; the unscripted arm wrote `what'd you get?` and did not. Reported 0/3 for an arm that had asked the question twice.
2. Fixed, the list still held no adverb. The shipped opener then said `Ask what they **just** got`, so the model wrote `what did you just grab?` and the list missed that too. Reported 71% for a wording that asks it every time.

**Both misses landed on whichever arm was not echoing a script, because a script is what makes a model reproduce one exact phrasing.** So the arm being tested is systematically the one a phrase list under-counts, and the error always flatters the scripted control. A detector that misses one arm more than the other does not measure a difference between arms, it manufactures one.

Three things follow, and the first is the cheap one:

- **Read the bodies before believing a rate**, at least a handful per arm. Both bugs were found that way and neither was visible in any number. The run log stores bodies verbatim precisely so this costs nothing and so a detector fix can be applied to data already generated (`first-touch-question-score.ts` re-scores a finished log; no model calls were repeated for either fix).
- **Prefer a pattern with an optional slot over an exact-phrase list** for anything a model phrases freely. Each new wording breaks a list in a new place.
- **Re-score the EARLIER runs after fixing a detector**, and say whether their numbers moved. TAC-423's 55% was unchanged by both fixes, which is the only thing that showed the ruling rested on a real difference rather than on a detector gap.

**A sixth property, from TAC-519, and it decides whether a run can be read charitably: STATE THE CEILINGS BEFORE THE RUN AND EVALUATE THEM IN CODE.** A bar answers "did the change work"; a ceiling answers "did it break something while working", and only the second catches a change that improves the number you are watching by doing the thing you were trying to prevent. TAC-519's balance arm hit a plausible rate and produced `Did you just come by today? What did you grab?`, two questions in one reply, which is the interrogation failure the block it edits exists to prevent. The pre-registered rule was that **a ceiling breach fails the arm whatever its rate**, so it failed at 1 occurrence in 40. Read as a rate that is 2.5% and dismissible; read as a ceiling it is disqualifying. The harness prints `FAIL  ceiling: ...` itself rather than leaving the judgement to whoever reads the output afterwards.

Three defects TAC-519 fixed in the harness it inherited, all one family, none visible in any number the run printed:

- **Errored calls counted in the denominator** while they could never increment a verdict, so a wholly broken run reported as a clean one with a low rate. On a ticket whose finding IS a low rate, that is indistinguishable from the result.
- **A transformation guard that could not fire on the population under test.** The opener replacement required exactly one match for every arm, but an ordinary mid-conversation turn has no opener, so every candidate arm would have gone INVALID on every ordinary turn and the run would have reported four empty arms. Asserting a thing's ABSENCE is as load-bearing as asserting its presence.
- **A refusal with a test asserting it fired, that could not fire.** The block-move module refused a guest body forging a `## ` heading; the splitter reads a forged line as a genuine block boundary, so the forged line was found, moved, and the refusal was unreachable code under a green test. Whole-line anchoring fixed it. Same shape as this file's other "a test whose stated rationale was never true" entries.

**A seventh, and it is about the verification rather than the harness: MUTATION TESTING BY THE TEST'S OWN AUTHOR VERIFIES THE MUTANTS THEY ALREADY THOUGHT OF.** That is a real guarantee and a narrow one. It proves the tests catch the failures their author imagined; it says nothing about the failures they did not.

TAC-519 is the worked example. Its author ran two mutants against a new pair of block-order tests and both died, so the tests were reported as mutation-verified. A code review then found two more that passed the entire suite, and the first was severe: **both tests were pinned on `category: 'follow_up'`, a category on which the block they guard cannot render in production at all** (`build-runtime-context` only derives `openIntentions` when there is an inbound), so a mutant reverting the change for every real category was invisible. The author's two mutants were about WHERE the block moved. The reviewer's were about WHETHER the fixture could reach the code — a question the author had already answered wrongly when writing the fixture, which is exactly why they could not think of it. TAC-520, the same night, has its own version of this two findings deep in its entry: "code review found two assertions that could not fail."

So: **a mutation pass by the author is a floor, not a ceiling, and "mutation-verified" should not be written as though it settled the question.** Two cheap habits close most of the gap. Ask what the FIXTURE cannot express, not only what the code could get wrong: a fixture that pins one category, one channel, one flag state, or one delivery status can only guard that one. And on anything whose guard matters, get a second reader whose first question is "can this test fail at all", because that is the question its author has structurally already answered.

**TAC-473 gives the sharpest statement of WHY the author's own pass misses what it misses, and it is worth carrying as a rule of thumb: an author's mutants ask WHAT THE CODE COMPUTES; the ones that survive ask WHETHER THE FIXTURE CAN REACH THE CODE, or whether the caller is wired in at all.** Nine mutants were run by hand, all killed, every one a change to a comparison, a filter value, an ordering or a returned field. A review then found a blocker and four majors that all nine missed, and every one of the five was the second kind:

- a route's venue filter was applied `if (allowedVenueIds.length > 0)`, which no mutant of the route's LOGIC can reach, because the defect is that the guard has the wrong SHAPE for its auth path;
- a fixture answered identically with a field passed and without it, so deleting the wiring survived all 5993 tests;
- a test double discarded the filters it existed to pin, so removing a query's venue scoping passed every test in the file;
- a module had no test file at all while its own header said the invariant was "asserted in the tests";
- and a new enum value fell through a switch **in a file the diff never touched**, which no mutant of the diff can reach by construction.

The author cannot easily generate these, because writing the fixture is the same act as deciding what it can express: the question "can this fixture reach the branch" has already been answered wrongly, by the same person, in the same keystroke. So the mutation count is worth reporting and is not the number that tells you whether the tests are any good. **Two questions get at the second kind directly, and both are cheap: does anything call this, and does any fixture differ from its neighbours in the one dimension the code branches on?** The first catches a module nothing tests and a caller nobody wired; the second catches a fixture whose two readings agree.

**And when an arm cannot differ from the control by construction, say so as a pre-registered validity check rather than as an expectation.** TAC-519's position arm is byte-identical to its baseline on a first-touch turn, because every block between the old slot and the new one is empty there. That was stated before the run, verified afterwards by string comparison rather than inferred from the rate delta, and a difference would have voided the run instead of reading as a result.

`scripts/measurement/run-log.ts` (documented under "Folder layout" above) gives all four for free — import `createRunLog` from a sandbox harness rather than reimplementing this. Prior art for the same failure in a different medium: `scripts/onboarding/tab-retention.ts` (TAC-347) fixed "a single reused Google Sheets tab destroys the previous run's result set" with timestamped tab names + retention. Different API, same idea — a pointer, not something to import from a local script.

### Available scripts

- `npm run send-test -- <phone> [body]` — sends a test message via the messaging module to the given E.164 phone number. Requires `TEST_VENUE_ID` in `.env.local` pointing to a venue row that has `messaging_phone_number` set.
- `npm run extract-venue-spec -- <slug> [--dry-run] [--force] [--interview-date YYYY-MM-DD]` — reads the venue's onboarding transcript + Airtable record + menu CSV from Drive, calls Sonnet to extract a structured venue spec, runs the TAC-346 verification pass (`scripts/onboarding/verify.ts`) against the draft, appends the result as a `## Needs confirmation` section, and writes the combined markdown as `06-{slug}-venue-spec-draft.md` to the venue's Drive folder. **Refuses to run if a `06-` file already exists in the venue folder** (TAC-346, mirrors `seed-venue`'s guard) — pass `--force` to overwrite anyway. `--dry-run` (TAC-331) is exempt from that guard (its purpose is testing against a venue that already has a live 06-file without touching it) and also skips only the Drive write — transcript/menu/Airtable reads still hit real data — saving the draft under `os.tmpdir()` instead and logging the path. `--interview-date` (TAC-346) sets the explicit anchor for resolving relative dates in the transcript ("next month", "this Saturday"); omit it to fall back to inferring a submission date from the Airtable record. **If verification fails after one retry, nothing is written anywhere (Drive or disk) and the process exits 1** — an existing `06-` file is left untouched, and every `06-` file that does land in Drive has passed verification.
- `npm run extract-test-scenarios -- <slug> [--regenerate]` — writes `07-{slug}-test-scenarios.json` to Drive from two independent sources merged into one unified `Scenario` shape (`scripts/onboarding/scenario-schema.ts`, TAC-347 Stage 1): (1) the existing markdown+LLM path (THE-180) — reads the venue spec + the 17-category fixture, calls Sonnet, generates `scenario_source: 'behavior'` rows only (mechanics-derived generation moved out of this path, see next); (2) a new DB-driven path (`scripts/onboarding/generate-db-scenarios.ts`) that reads `knowledge_corpus`, `venue_configs.venue_info`, and `mechanics` directly and generates `knowledge` / `fact` / `menu` / `unanswerable` / `mechanic` / `routing` scenarios with no LLM call — deterministic, content-stable sample ids (`knowledge:{corpus_id}`, `mechanic:{mechanic_id}:{state}`, ...), and an `expected_route` per scenario for the Stage 3 routing grader (not built yet). Each scenario also carries `expected_facts`/`forbidden_claims`/`source_row_ids` for the Stage 3 knowledge grader. `--regenerate` (accepts `--force` as an alias) overwrites an existing 07-file; coverage gaps (DB rows with no covering scenario) print as a warning. Register variety for the DB-driven sources ("terse, typos, emoji-heavy, long") comes from fixed deterministic transforms in `scripts/onboarding/register-variants.ts`, not an LLM call.
- `npm run seed-venue -- <slug> [--messaging-phone <e164>] [--force]` — reads the 06-spec markdown from Drive, parses it via Zod schemas, ingests into the database (venue, venue_configs, mechanics, voice_corpus + embeddings via Voyage). Optional `--messaging-phone` sets `venues.messaging_phone_number` at seed time. First-write-only: hard-refuses when a venue with the slug already exists, across every store it writes, not only menu items. `--force` (TAC-343 Phase 0b, narrowed on plan review) deletes and rewrites CONFIG STORES ONLY — `venue_configs`, `mechanics`, `voice_corpus`+embeddings, `knowledge_corpus`+embeddings — reusing the existing venue's id; it never touches the `venues` row or any guest-relationship table, and refuses outright, even with the flag, if the venue has any `guests` or `messages` rows (re-seeding a venue with real guest history is not a supported workflow — that venue is edited on its config page instead). Logs exactly what it's about to delete first. Nothing in this repo calls `--force`; it exists so a deliberate wipe-and-reseed of a mock venue during development doesn't require a hand-run SQL `DELETE` first. CLI entry point is `scripts/seed-venue.ts`; the heavy lifting lives in `scripts/onboarding/seed-supabase.ts`.
- `npm run run-test-scenarios -- <slug> [--sample-ids id1,id2,...] [--topic t1,t2] [--category c1,c2] [--mode graded|exploratory] [--limit N] [--concurrency N] [--max-cost USD] [--owner-review]` — seeds the four synthetic guests, runs the selected scenarios from the 07-sheet's Scenarios tab through the real agent pipeline decision-only (no Sendblue, no human-feel delay, no fidelity gate), grades each via Stage 3 (deterministic voice + LLM knowledge/voice/routing), and writes the results as a fresh timestamped `Report {date} {time}` / `Run {date} {time}` tab pair on the same 07-sheet — **TAC-347 Stage 4**: replaced a single reused `Report`/`Run` tab per sheet, which meant every run silently destroyed the previous run's result set (a 455-scenario run was lost this way); the 10 most recent tabs of each name are kept, older ones pruned after the new tab writes (`scripts/onboarding/tab-retention.ts` + `pruneTabsByPrefix` in `drive.ts`). The selection flags (`--sample-ids`/`--topic`/`--category`/`--mode`/`--limit`) narrow which scenarios run. `--owner-review` (also TAC-347 Stage 4) is mutually exclusive with those — it selects its own diverse ~30-scenario pool instead (`scripts/onboarding/owner-review-selection.ts`: excludes adversarial/safety-critical/unanswerable content, weights toward greeting/recommendation/menu-question/complaint/perk-request situations spread across guest states, filters to scenarios that passed knowledge+routing grading and produced real deliverable text) and additionally writes a separate `08-{slug}-response-review` gsheet in the exact shape `ingest-response-review`'s `parseReviewSheet` expects (`scripts/onboarding/owner-review-sheet.ts`), so `ingest-response-review` works against it unchanged. Throws after logging all four synthetic-guest tuning outcomes if any state landed in the wrong band. **TAC-367, widened by TAC-424: `grounding_check_failed` can surface as a routing-grade FAIL.** The harness calls the real `verifyGroundingStage`, so a verdict it could not read flips that scenario's `route` from `send` to `queue` and `grade-routing.ts` grades it as a routing defect. It isn't one — it is infrastructure, and at `--concurrency` the 429s that cause it are the harness's own doing. **Since TAC-424 this applies to transient faults too, which is strictly more of them**: a 429 that survives one immediate retry now queues where it used to pass through, so expect this row to appear more often on a concurrent run, and expect the paired `grounding_verifier_unavailable` Slack relay with it. Read a `grounding_check_failed` row as "the check didn't complete", not as a routing bug — and look for `grounding_check_degraded` in the Run tab's **`all_triggers`** column to tell a rate-limited call apart from a truncated one. (A harness run writes no `messages` row at all, so `review_triggers` is the wrong place to look here; that column exists only in production.) **Run it during the venue's open hours (TAC-301).** `## Right now` now carries an open/closed status line, so a run executed after close injects `CLOSED right now. Do not tell the guest to come by now...` into every scenario — including the `--owner-review` pool that becomes the 08-sheet an owner signs off on. Results are not comparable run-to-run by `sample_id` unless both runs fell in the same open/closed state.
- `npm run ingest-response-review -- <slug>` — reads the 08-Sheet, ingests `verdict=edit` rows into `voice_corpus` (Voyage embedding on `edited_message` text only, source_ref upsert key for idempotency), appends `rule:`-prefixed comments to `brand_persona.voiceAntiPatterns`, appends a dated `## Phase 5 review additions` subsection to the 06-spec markdown in Drive (THE-178). Skips rows with `expected_failure:` markers entirely. Skips the markdown append if zero net new ingestions.
- `npm run instagram-smoke -- --venue <slug> --guest <guest-uuid> --confirm [--show-ids]` — TAC-469's one-off Instagram outbound smoke test, run by hand against a TEST account: it sends up to three real messages from the venue's Instagram account and refuses to do anything without `--confirm`. It settles the three things no unit test can. **A: the Send API's `message_id` is the echo's `mid`** — every reconciliation on both arms rests on that being one identifier, and if it is not, the duplicate-key collision never fires and every send leaves two rows. **B: the 1000-byte boundary** — it sends exactly 1000 bytes through the transport, then posts 1001 straight at Graph, bypassing our own guard, to see which side of the line Meta draws. **C: one row whichever write lands first** — it exercises the echo-first and our-write-first orders against the real database and the real webhook. Each check prints PASS, FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE or NOTE and the rows it touched; exit 1 on a failure, 3 when something was inconclusive. **The token is deliberately not read from a committed file**: pass it for the one run (`INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN=... npm run instagram-smoke -- ...`), which wins over `.env.local`, so it can stay commented out there. It never prints the guest's scoped ID, the token or a mid; `--show-ids` prints mids and exists for diagnosing a check-A mismatch.
- `npm run measure-prose-promise` — TAC-401's replay of the prose-promise check against the 220 labelled synthetic replies (`scripts/measurement/fixtures/prose-promise-replies.json`). Generates nothing and writes nothing to the database; it re-judges fixed bodies, so it costs one Haiku call per body per repeat (1100 at the default `REPEATS=5`). Re-run it whenever that check's prompt changes.
- `npm run measure-prose-promise-elliptical` — TAC-527's two-arm replay of the same check against 14 inbound-bearing pairs (`scripts/measurement/fixtures/prose-promise-elliptical.json`). Generates nothing and writes nothing to the database. 28 cells x `REPEATS` (default 10) = 280 Haiku calls. Re-run it alongside `measure-prose-promise` whenever that check's prompt or input changes: the two cover different populations and the 220-body one is body-only by construction.
- `npm run db:types` — regenerates `db/types.ts` from the live Supabase schema. Run after applying any migration.

## Phase 5 onboarding pipeline

Phase 5 is the voice-quality cycle that completes venue onboarding. Five files in the venue's Drive folder, numbered 04-08:

- `04-{slug}-menu` (gsheet) — menu CSV, owner-editable
- `05-{slug}-transcript` — onboarding interview transcript
- `06-{slug}-venue-spec-draft.md` — structured venue spec extracted from transcript + airtable + menu. **Central voice brain for the venue.** Original extraction at top; a `## Needs confirmation` section is appended by `extract-venue-spec`'s own verification pass (TAC-346, not seeded — see below) immediately after every extraction run, before any human has looked at the draft; Phase 5 review additions are a SEPARATE, LATER append by `ingest-response-review` after the Phase 5 meeting, in dated subsections at the bottom. Both are append-only. Regenerating only happens if the spec genuinely needs to change — Phase 5 voice training does NOT trigger a re-seed.
- `07-{slug}-test-scenarios.json` — venue-tailored test scenarios (~180 rows for le-mils-coffee, ~180 for mock-sextant-coffee-roasters as of TAC-347 Stage 1's database-driven expansion — see the `npm run extract-test-scenarios` entry above for the full source breakdown). Generated by `extract-test-scenarios` from the 06-spec + the categories fixture (behavior-category rows) merged with DB-driven rows read directly from `knowledge_corpus` / `venue_configs.venue_info` / `mechanics`.
- `08-{slug}-response-review` (gsheet) — populated by `run-test-scenarios`. Owner reviews collaboratively during the Phase 5 meeting, marks `verdict` (approve/edit), provides `edited_message` for rejections, adds `rule:`-prefixed comments for anti-patterns. Then `ingest-response-review` reads it back and updates the corpus + persona surgically.

The pipeline is idempotent at every step. Re-running any script is safe. **Exception (TAC-346):** `extract-venue-spec` hard-refuses to re-run against a venue folder that already has a `06-` file, mirroring `seed-venue`'s existing-slug guard — pass `--force` to override, or `--dry-run` (exempt from the guard) to test without touching the real file.

**Extraction hardening: verify every claim, flag gaps, fix where content lands (TAC-346).** The first real non-mock extraction (Le Mil's) needed ~40 hand edits, all tracing to `extract.ts`, not to `parse-venue-spec`/`seed-venue`. Two changes: (1) a second LLM pass, `scripts/onboarding/verify.ts` — `runVerification` reads the draft plus the same raw sources extraction had (never a `parseVenueSpec`-parsed object; the parser's own ≥5-voice-corpus-entry throw would crash the exact thin-corpus case this pass exists to report gracefully) and returns structured flags across five categories (unsupported claims, uncovered transcript answers, missing information, resolved dates, and a **mandatory per-mechanic `requires_operator_approval` review** — every mechanic is listed regardless of whether anything else about it is flagged, with a `⚠` marker when verify's own independent transcript read disagrees with the value extraction wrote). `scripts/extract-venue-spec.ts` runs this immediately after extraction and appends the result as an unnumbered `## Needs confirmation` section (never seeded — `parse-venue-spec.ts`'s `h2s.find` per-numbered-section lookup already ignores any unrecognized H2, proven in production by sections 8/9 today). **Verify failure aborts the whole run**: one retry, then nothing is written to Drive or disk and the process exits 1 — every `06-` file that lands in Drive has passed verification, no partially-verified draft ever ships. (2) `extract.ts`'s prompt rules tightened: `knowledge_corpus` now covers plain operational facts (policies, logistics, ordering, shipping, retail, wholesale, catering, private events, merch — using the existing `policies`/`logistics` primary tags) with no upper cap, not just narrative; `voice_corpus` permits ONLY `source_type='voicenote_transcript'` (no `manual_entry` padding, no floor to hit — a real corpus can come in under 5, with the shortfall reported in Needs confirmation rather than papered over, since `parse-venue-spec.ts`'s seed-time floor of 5 stays unchanged); `currentContext` vs. permanent fields are mutually exclusive, and every `expiresAt` must resolve to a real ISO date (never a relative phrase — `filterActiveContext` silently drops a malformed `expiresAt`, so leaving one unresolved is worse than a best-guess date); `bannedTopics`/`voiceAntiPatterns`/`signaturePhrases` may never carry routing or handoff instructions; mechanics may only be practices the operator already does (brainstormed ideas are omitted from section 5 entirely, never routed there as an instruction); `trigger.type` is constrained to `MECHANIC_TRIGGER_TYPES` (imported from `lib/schemas/mechanic.ts`, not hand-copied — this also fixed a live defect where the fixture's own example listed a non-canonical `date_match` value); `venue_info.staff` is employees only, with collaborators/suppliers routed to `knowledge_corpus` instead. **Extraction prompt rules never name "Needs confirmation" as a destination** — omitted content is just omitted; the verification pass independently looks for the same brainstormed ideas and handoff statements and reports them under uncovered answers, so the two passes can't silently disagree about what got dropped and why. Relative dates resolve against an interview-date anchor: an optional `--interview-date YYYY-MM-DD` CLI flag on `extract-venue-spec`, falling back to the Airtable-inferred "Submission date" already written into section 2 when omitted. The fixture (`venue-spec-example.md`) dropped its self-attested "Pre-seed validation checklist" section entirely — it was model-authored and Le Mil's draft checked "at least 5 voice_corpus entries" against a padded corpus, a green signal nobody had actually confirmed; `## Needs confirmation` (independently generated, not self-attested) replaces it.

**Extraction routes opinionated recommendations to `knowledge_corpus`, never `venue_info` (TAC-331).** Owners describing their business speak in advice ("for a first-timer I'd start them on the latte, don't over-program the first visit") — extraction was recording that faithfully into `venue_info.menu.highlights` / `menu.notes`, where it renders into every prompt turn as if it were a structured fact, indistinguishable from one by the time it reaches the model. `extract.ts`'s system prompt already listed "opinionated recommendations" under `knowledge_corpus` (it's a narrative-knowledge store, gated by retrieval — it only surfaces when the guest's message is actually about what to order), but had no worked example for this exact pattern and the few-shot fixture's own `menu.highlights` placeholder used the leaked vocabulary ("first-timer pick", "perfect-order anchor") as an "e.g." hint, which the model echoed verbatim. Fixed by (1) an explicit routing rule in `extract.ts` with a WRONG/RIGHT worked example matching the live incident, (2) a separate, narrower mood rule for content that legitimately stays in `venue_info` prose (the perfect-order narrative, sourcing description) — must read as description of the venue, never an instruction to the assistant, and (3) a new `knowledge_corpus` fixture example (Entry 5) modeling the correct attributed-indicative form with `primary_tags: ["recommendations"]` — a positive template, not just prose instruction. No schema change, no migration, no serializer change: the `recommendations` primary tag and the `knowledge_corpus` section-7 parser both already existed (see `lib/schemas/knowledge-tags.ts`, `parse-venue-spec.ts`); this was a placement defect in the extraction prompt, not a missing destination. `scripts/onboarding/extract.test.ts` canaries the fixture against reintroducing the leaked vocabulary. Deliberately does not re-extract any live venue — see the ticket for why Mock Sextant's `venue_info` (already hand-fixed in place per TAC-330) and this fix now intentionally disagree in form.

### File-naming convention

The 04-09 numbering is meaningful and reserved. Don't introduce other 04-09 files in venue folders. Each script reads its expected files by prefix (`04-`, `06-`, `07-`, `08-`) — adding ambiguous matches will trip the existence guard.

The `-draft` suffix on the 06-file is misleading post-Phase-5 (the file is canonical at that point, not a draft). Slated for rename in THE-185 — bundle with the next touch of any of the three pipeline scripts that reference the filename.

## Drive integration

Google Drive auth uses Application Default Credentials (ADC) via `gcloud auth application-default login`. The OAuth client lives in the analog Google Cloud project; client JSON is a `client_secret_*.json` file under this repo's `Minimum-Viable-Product` parent directory, not at a fixed path — locate it with a glob (see below). Scopes: `openid`, `userinfo.email`, `cloud-platform`, `drive`.

Workspace org policy blocks the stock gcloud OAuth client. Use the project-owned OAuth client (Desktop app type) instead — Workspace's third-party policy doesn't apply to your own org's apps. Pass the client JSON via `--client-id-file` to `gcloud auth application-default login`.

Drive helpers are in `scripts/onboarding/drive.ts`:

- `getDrive()` — auth + Drive client
- `findVenueFolder(drive, parentFolderId, slug)` — locates the venue's folder by slug
- `listVenueFiles(drive, folderId)` — lists files in a venue folder
- `findByPrefix(files, prefix)` — finds the unique file with a given prefix; throws on ambiguity
- `readDriveFileAsText(drive, fileId)` — reads a Drive file as text. For gsheets, exports as CSV.
- `writeMarkdownFile(drive, folderId, name, body)` — writes/upserts a markdown file by name
- `writeJsonFile(drive, folderId, name, obj)` — writes/upserts a JSON file by name (pretty-printed)
- `writeSheetFile(drive, folderId, name, csvBody)` — writes/upserts a native Google Sheet from CSV body. Uses `mimeType: 'application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet'` + `media.mimeType: 'text/csv'` so Drive auto-converts on upload. The update path explicitly pins both mimetypes to preserve sharing.

### ADC token refresh (when Drive scripts fail)

Two distinct failure modes land here, both fixed by the same command:

- `Request had insufficient authentication scopes` — ADC has never been granted Drive scope at all (or was granted it, then re-authed without `--scopes` and lost it).
- `invalid_grant` / `reauth related error (invalid_rapt)` — ADC previously had Drive scope, but the token expired or the reauth policy (RAPT) lapsed. This is time-based, not a one-time setup gap — expect to hit it again after enough elapsed time even with everything configured correctly before.

Either symptom means: `run-test-scenarios`, `extract-venue-spec`, `seed-supabase`, `extract-test-scenarios`, or `ingest-response-review` needs reauth with explicit Drive scope:

```bash
F=$(ls ~/dev/Ideas/the-analog-company/Minimum-Viable-Product/client_secret_*.json) && gcloud auth application-default login \
  --client-id-file="$F" \
  --scopes="openid,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive"
```

**Canonical client file path:** there isn't a fixed one — `~/.config/analog/oauth-client.json` does not exist on the operator's machine and was never a real path. The file is `client_secret_*.json`, dropped directly under `Minimum-Viable-Product/` (this repo's parent directory) rather than into a dotfile config location. Locate it with a glob, not a hardcoded path: the filename embeds the client ID. The directory has been `~/dev/Ideas/the-analog-company/Minimum-Viable-Product/` since TAC-425 (2026-09-16) moved it off the iCloud-synced Desktop, whose path carried a curly apostrophe (`Desktop’s`) that silently broke hand-typed paths. Client ID `262219665239-3fi6pt39u9m8i0nh9vfcouhqi0t6n9qt`, GCP project `analog-venue-onboarding`. **Never write the client secret itself into CLAUDE.md or any tracked file** — `client_secret_*.json` is in `.gitignore` as a backstop against it landing in the repo by accident.

**Why this is needed:** the default scopes for `gcloud auth application-default login` (with no `--scopes` flag) do NOT include `drive` — **plain `gcloud auth application-default login` with no flags succeeds and reports a healthy login, then every Drive API call still fails.** gcloud's built-in ADC OAuth client cannot request Drive scope at all, regardless of flags — that's what the project-owned client (below) is for. The `--scopes` flag is mandatory for any script that touches Drive; there's no way to add it after the fact short of re-running the full command again.

**Why the `--client-id-file`:** Workspace org policy blocks the stock gcloud OAuth client. The project-owned OAuth client (Desktop app type, `client_secret_*.apps.googleusercontent.com.json`) bypasses that policy because Workspace's third-party policy doesn't apply to your own org's apps.

**This procedure is interactive and human-only.** It opens a browser consent flow — there is no non-interactive or scripted path around it. Claude Code cannot complete this reauth itself; when a session hits `invalid_rapt` or the insufficient-scopes error, it should stop and hand off to the operator rather than attempting a workaround.

## Testing

Vitest is the test runner. Tests are colocated with source files (`module.test.ts` next to `module.ts`). Pure functions get unit tests; DB-touching code generally doesn't (live-DB tests aren't worth the harness yet).

- Run all: `npx vitest run`
- Run single file: `npx vitest run path/to/file.test.ts`
- Watch mode for development: `npx vitest`


Test count baseline: **6172 tests across 268 files as of 2026-09-23** — most recent (TAC-526, a guest's burst becomes one turn: **+102 tests / +2 files** over **6070/266**, BOTH ENDS measured against clean `origin/main` 5231b32 in a `.worktrees/baseline` worktree, removed straight after — while it is there a local `npx vitest run` collects its copy too. **Re-measured after EACH of two rebases rather than carried**: the branch first read +79 over 5906/260; TAC-473 landed and took migration 056 (forcing the renumber to 057), then TAC-527 landed, and every one of those moved both ends. The DELTA held at +102/+2 across the last two, which is the consistency check worth having — the totals are not. The delta reconciles per file, measured on both trees: the new `lib/agent/coalesce-turn.test.ts` 64, the new `lib/agent/coalesce-inbound.test.ts` 35, `lib/schemas/inbound-turn-outcome.test.ts` 9 → 10, and `lib/agent/record-inbound-turn-outcome.test.ts` 27 → 29. `lib/agent/handle-inbound.test.ts` is unchanged at 93, which is worth stating rather than leaving to be noticed: **all 93 pass with the gate ON**, because the claim fails open against that file's mocked client — the strongest evidence the flip is safe, and it holds because the fail-open path puts them on today's behaviour rather than because anything was adjusted to suit it. **Mutation-verified against 44 mutants across five passes, and the passes are the point.** A code review found SEVEN surviving the first three commits — two were BLOCKERS in the code (a failed read at close time silencing a folded message, and the `coalesced` ledger mapping bound to nothing) and five were tests that could not fail, four of them one mistake: **a fixture seeding a message at the wrong moment.** The crisis test needed THREE placements before it could fail (up front the settle adopted it; during the dispatch was too late; only during CLASSIFY, after the adopt and before the branch, is the window), and even then it survived until the assertion became a COUNT, because the mutant only adds a SECOND context build and the test read `calls[0]`. **The sharpest single finding: dropping `.eq('direction', 'inbound')` from the newest-message query survived the whole suite**, and in production that makes every turn find its own outbound reply as the "newer inbound", re-enter with an outbound id and throw in `loadInbound` — discarding a reply it had already generated. One deleted line, total silencing, zero coverage; the in-memory fakes could never have shown it, which is this repo's "a fake that enforces the guarantee cannot show the QUERY carries it" rule applied to three queries and missed on the fourth. **THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON IS ABOUT THE HARNESS, NOT THE CODE: A CRASHED WORKER READS AS A SURVIVOR.** Removing the retry's depth bound makes the chain recurse until the vitest worker dies (`Worker exited unexpectedly`), and a crashed worker STILL PRINTS A SUMMARY — so the harness parsed `0 failed` and reported SURVIVED on the two mutants that are the entire point of the bound. The loop was real and the result said the opposite, twice, across two separate runs. Two fixes, both needed: the harness treats a crashed or skipped run as INVALID before reading any count, and **every failing fixture is self-limiting** (`failFirst(n)`, and the trace-flush control became a COUNT rather than a boolean) so the unbounded build terminates and fails an assertion instead of dying. Same shape as the extension bound earlier in this ticket, which had to be rewritten for the identical reason. **And a test-isolation bug the same change exposed**: handoffs and retries run under a `waitUntil` this file mocks to `(p) => p`, so a chain started in one test is still running when the next begins and consumes shared mock state — a straggler swallowed the one-shot flush failure, and the test that needed it passed IN ISOLATION and failed IN THE FILE, which is the signature. An `afterEach` drain fixes it. **`"Never throws"` was a claim in a docstring and was FALSE, and no mutant could have found it**: supabase-js throws on some failures rather than returning `{ error }`, and an escaping throw fails the whole turn CLOSED. A type cannot express "does not throw"; what exposed it was the entire orchestrator suite going red the moment the flag constant changed — the change itself was the test. **No `PROMPT_VERSION` bump: this ticket touches no prompt copy at all**, which is a property of the design rather than of its scope — the fix is "only one run may produce a reply", so context assembly and every prompt file are untouched and there was no grep sweep to run.) Prior entry: **6070 tests across 266 files as of 2026-09-23** — most recent (TAC-527, an approved prose comp promise creates the commitment: **+40 tests / +0 files** over **6030/266**, both ends measured against clean `origin/main` 3a561dd in a `.worktrees/baseline` worktree, removed BEFORE the after-count so the run could not collect both copies. **The headline is the tree after merging `main` back in**, and both ends were RE-MEASURED there rather than carried: TAC-473 landed mid-ticket and moved both, so the pre-merge reading of 5946 over 5906/260 describes a tree that no longer exists. The DELTA is +40/+0 either way, which is the consistency check worth having; the totals are not. **The prior line was ACCURATE**, matching the measured baseline exactly — recorded because several recent entries found it stale, and a run of accuracy is not a reason to stop measuring, only the reason measuring is cheap. (Note the trap that nearly put a false "four merges stale" claim here: a session's own loaded copy of CLAUDE.md comes from the MAIN checkout at session start, not from the branch's worktree, so the two disagree whenever main has moved. Read the file in the tree you are measuring.) The delta reconciles per file, every number measured on both trees: `lib/ai/verify-prose-promise.test.ts` 12 → 25, `lib/agent/stages.test.ts` 324 → 329, `lib/agent/two-pending-slots.test.ts` 34 → 38, `lib/operator/queue.test.ts` 67 → 85 (its base moved from 59 when TAC-473 landed, which is why a per-file figure is re-measured rather than carried across a merge too). `handle-operator-decline.test.ts` is UNCHANGED at 25, which is the tell that the decline half was reverted rather than merely disabled (TAC-531). **Ten of those came from a code-review pass, which is the interesting half** — see the four findings below. **No new test file, deliberately**: the incident replay went into `two-pending-slots.test.ts` rather than the new `prose-promise-carrier-replay.test.ts` the plan named, because the harness there runs the REAL gate and the REAL persist layer against an in-memory `messages` table and can assert the persisted row — a new file would have duplicated that fake to make a weaker, mock-shaped claim. **Mutation-verified against 18 mutants, each killed by the test named for it with tests collected and the tree restored byte-identically after each.** Seven on the widened input: the stage dropping the inbound, hardcoding null, the retry restating its input literal and diverging, the guest line rendered AFTER the reply, the blank-inbound guard dropped, the approved carve-out INVERTED so accepting a named complaint stays clean, and the guest-message scoping paragraph deleted so the widened input becomes a licence. Four more ran against the decline-path half and are recorded as HISTORY, not coverage: the persist options dropping the carrier, the slot identity reverted to `draftCommitmentIdentity`, the check never running, and the `./stages` mock dropping the new stage. All four died at the time and none of that code ships — the half was reverted to TAC-531. Seven on the card copy: the creates-nothing suffix applied even WITH a carrier, hold and discount sentences swapped, the em-dash strip removed, the cap removed, secondary chips ignoring the carrier so the primary and the chip disagree, and the carrier read failing hard instead of soft. **ONE SURVIVED a first pass and is the entry worth reading**: widening the dynamic sentence to `commitment_type_gated` passed all 71 tests, because the copy table renders that trigger with NO carrier and the dynamic branch was unreachable for it — so an approved scope boundary existed only in a comment. A comment claiming a guard is not a guard; it has a test now and the mutant dies. **Two of my own assertions could not fail and were rewritten rather than re-expected**: the description-cap test asserted a negative regex (`/\w\.\sYour call\.$/`) that no implementation could match, since the sentence always ends in a word character before ". Your call.", so it passed against a version cutting mid-word; and a sibling `describe` block does not inherit another's `beforeEach`, so its call-count assertion was reading the whole file's accumulated mock history. **A CODE REVIEW FOUND FOUR MAJORS THE 18 MUTANTS MISSED, and two are worth carrying.** (1) **The card copy was FALSE on a case the suffix was never checked against**: `comp_regex_backstop` beside a RECOMMENDATION carrier rendered "Approving won't create anything", while `createCommitmentFromPending` inserts from the carrier whatever its type and migration 037 means a recommendation effectively never leaves `open`. The existing recommendation test used `prose_promise_backstop`, where that fallback wording happens to be true, so the gap survived the suite. "No carrier at all" and "a carrier this sentence cannot name" are now distinct (`CardCarrierInfo.obligation`), with the malformed case deliberately on the first side because dispatch skips materialization on a parse failure and so genuinely creates nothing. (2) **A surviving mutant on the half of a guarantee that was only half-asserted**: narrowing the system-prompt decision from `hasGuestMessage(input)` to `input.guestInboundBody !== null` — dropping only the trim check — passed 348 tests, because the blank `it.each` asserted `prompt` and the byte-identity test asserted `null` only. Under it a BLANK inbound composed the carve-out into the system prompt while the user prompt rendered no guest line: exactly the 8/20 configuration. Reachable, not hypothetical — a media-only inbound is stored with `body = ''`. The byte-identity test is now an `it.each` over `[null, '', '   ', '\n', '\t']` and the mutant dies to four of them. (3) **"Only the carrier changes" was false**, and this is what split the ticket: a flagged decline has an obligation identity, so its SLOT can move, costing TAC-299 decision #2's supersession on one branch and a 502-without-cancellation on the other. Ruled 2026-09-23 — a swipe-left that errors and loses the cancellation is worse than the defect it would fix — so the whole decline half was REVERTED out of this branch and filed as TAC-531, rather than bundling a second undecided behaviour change into this one. (4) `captureProsePromiseCaught` omitted the guest inbound, so the one input deciding the new verdicts was absent from the only production signal and a correct catch was indistinguishable from the `ell-11` shape; it carries `guestInboundBody` now, above the reply in the Slack lines. Plus MINORs: two more surviving mutants in `loadCardCarriers` (the empty-`draftIds` early return and the blank-after-sanitize guard, both now tested), a fixture row whose label is not a key of `EXPECTATION` now exits 1 before spending a call, and the check is `Promise.all`ed with the slot read rather than sitting in front of it on the screen TAC-304 filed a lag on. **The test harness's routing grades are not comparable across this deploy**: `run-test-scenarios.ts` passes a real inbound, so every scenario now runs the inbound-bearing configuration and a reply that elliptically accepts a complaint can flag where it did not, flipping `route` to `queue`. Read a diff across this bump as a baseline reset, as TAC-380 and TAC-301 each record. **No `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE` bump and therefore no grep sweep**: the version moved is the module's own `VERIFY_PROSE_PROMISE_PROMPT_VERSION` (v1.0.0 → v1.1.0), which never touches the classify/generate contract — the independence rationale it has carried since TAC-401.) Prior entry (TAC-473, the operator app's Instagram fields, echo resolution and the one-hour push: **+124 tests / +6 files** over **5906/260**, measured on clean `origin/main` bc3831b in the ticket's own worktree before branching. The line this replaces was ACCURATE, matching that measurement exactly — recorded because the last several entries all found it stale, and a run of accuracy is not a reason to stop measuring, only the reason measuring is cheap. The delta reconciles per file: the four new test files are `lib/operator/instagram-fields.test.ts` 18, `lib/messaging/instagram/resolve-external.test.ts` 19, `lib/agent/instagram-window-warning.test.ts` 16 and `app/api/operator/messages/[id]/resolve-external/route.test.ts` 14; plus `lib/operator/queue.test.ts` 57 → 67, `lib/operator/conversations.test.ts` 7 → 11, `app/api/cron/pending-timeout/route.test.ts` 5 → 9, `window-import-guard.test.ts` 8 → 10, `pending-slots.test.ts` unchanged at 134 (one test rewritten, none added) and `app/api/webhooks/instagram/route.test.ts` 55 → 56 (one `it.each` split into two honestly-named tests). **Mutation-verified against 9 mutants, each killed by the test named for it with tests collected.** On the projections: `guestChannel` derived from the GUEST instead of the card (2 tests — the load-bearing one, since a guest-derived channel can disagree with where approving actually sends), the 24-hour addition dropped from the deadline (8 tests across two files), and `guestChannel` dropped from the projection entirely (5 tests AND `tsc`, because the interface field is required rather than optional). On echo resolution: the window guard removed, the one that would let the agent close its own cards (2 tests); oldest→newest card selection (2); and the `channel = 'instagram'` filter dropped, so an Instagram echo resolves an SMS card (1). On the push: the marker filter dropped from the scan (sixty pushes an hour), the CAS losing its never-warned guard, and expired drafts warned anyway. **Two tests were rewritten rather than re-expected, and both had stopped meaning what they said.** Two route tests asserted `waitUntil` was never called for an echo — a proxy for "an echo does nothing" that this ticket made false — and now assert the two things that proxy stood for: an echo never reaches the agent and never refreshes a profile. And one new processor test was named "keeps going when one draft fails" while its fixture only produced an unknown window; it now makes the anchor read actually throw. **One vacuous assertion was caught and deleted before commit** — a describe block asserting that a `vi.fn()` nothing had called had not been called — which is this file's own documented antipattern, written by hand into the very ticket that cites it. **Three source guards took a deliberate entry**, each with its reason at the entry rather than only in a commit message: the window import guard TWICE (`lib/operator/instagram-fields.ts` for the constant and `lib/agent/instagram-window-warning.ts` for the processor — **the plan claimed ONE and it is two**, because the processor belongs with its cron siblings in `lib/agent/` rather than inside the provider folder); the `provider_sent_at` mention list once (prose only, the same basis the Instagram send arm is on it); and TAC-394's per-guest single-row pending read list once. **That last one was strengthened rather than merely widened**: its guard-the-guard test asserted only that one file was found, so it now asserts that EVERY allowed read orders by `created_at`, which is the property the describe block is named for — a file added to the allow-list without an ORDER BY now fails instead of passing silently. **THE CODE REVIEW THEN FOUND A BLOCKER AND FOUR MAJORS THAT ALL 9 OF THOSE MUTANTS MISSED, and the shape is one this file keeps recording: the author's mutants were about what the code COMPUTES, and every survivor was about whether the fixture could REACH the code or whether the caller was wired in at all.** (1) **The BLOCKER is an authorization hole and is worth reading as a general trap.** `/resolve-external` applied its venue filter only `if (allowedVenueIds.length > 0)` — which is correct on the COOKIE path (`lib/auth/require-admin.ts`, where empty deliberately means analog-admin scope, i.e. every venue) and a fleet-wide grant on the OPERATOR BEARER path, where `verifyOperatorRequest` builds the array from the operator's literal `operator_venues` rows so empty means allowlisted for NOTHING. Seven siblings short-circuit it to a deny. **Two auth paths, one field name, opposite meanings**, and the route was shaped from the wrong one. An operator with no grants and a valid JWT could resolve any pending card in the fleet by id, and the fallback lookup leaked `review_state` for any message. **The identical shape is live on `main` at `lib/operator/dispatch-operator-outbound.ts:177`** and is reported as a finding rather than fixed here — filed as TAC-530 (Urgent, before launch), which also carries the suggestion that the ambiguity be removed at the type rather than at each call site, since the next route copied from either path inherits whichever meaning it copied. (2) The `lastInboundChannel` wiring was **unfalsifiable**: its fixture set a phone AND `last_inbound_channel: 'text'`, and `resolveConversationChannel` answers `'text'` for that fixture whether or not the field is passed, so `lastInboundChannel: undefined` survived all 5993 tests. Only a phone-plus-Instagram guest whose last inbound was INSTAGRAM separates the two readings. (3) The resolve-external route's `select()` double DISCARDED its filters, so removing the lookup's venue scoping passed all 14 tests. Both sides are now normalized (quote entities decoded, typographic quotes folded to ASCII, whitespace collapsed so a prettier-wrapped paste can't hide behind a newline), mutation-verified against all three forms: raw literal, entity-escaped JSX text, and entity-escaped plus line-wrapped. **What it still cannot catch is a PARAPHRASE**, stated in the test's own header rather than left to be assumed: prose that describes a prompt line without quoting it passes and can still go stale. That limit is not hypothetical — it is why the gating copy was rewritten mid-build to describe the menu-mention rule instead of quoting the line it suppresses, the first draft having quoted it, which is the same drift the ticket forbids one layer removed. The satisfaction truth table in `definitions.test.ts` is a LITERAL table rather than anything derived from the predicates, because a derived expectation would pass against any predicate at all; `satisfies Record<IntentionKey, ...>` on it is what makes a third intention fail `tsc` there. Honest accounting of the three guards, since they are easy to mistake for one: the required field catches a MISSING label, the truth table catches a CHANGED predicate, the source scan catches a COPIED string — and nothing catches a label that is simply WRONG about a predicate nobody touched. A reviewer is still the only guard there.) Among the thirty-four: the strictly-newer check dropped, or comparing the askable time instead of the event (killed only by the same-conversation and window-growth cases, because with an unchanged window the two comparisons agree); a re-arm not waiting on an unanswered prompt, or a pessimistic or unjudgeable prompt holding one up; a re-arm clearing the last prompt; a re-armed row never reopening, or a first-contact one reopening; the mid-conversation hold dropped in each of three ways; the stamp guard reverted to the first version's `eligible_at` comparison, which the in-memory re-arm-then-stamp ordering kills; and the Command Center loader never reading re-armed rows, reading them as unprompted, or dropping `degraded` when nothing is eligible; the hold ignoring a re-suggested recommendation's `updated_at`, in each of three ways; and, from the final review, a failed commitments read lifting the hold, the unreadable flag not passed, touched times arming, and the touched-time block losing its type filter or its `.ok` guard. Don't let regressions land — every PR should keep tests green.

**Update this line when you add or remove test files, and measure rather than estimate.** A stale baseline is what let an "after" count be reported without an "if the delta doesn't match, a file isn't being collected" check — and an uncollected test file is indistinguishable from a passing one in the summary output. To get a trustworthy before/after on a branch, run the "before" in a throwaway worktree, which leaves this checkout and its changes alone (TAC-471; this used to be `git stash`, which CI refuses, and a stash a session never pops is lost work):

```
git worktree add .worktrees/baseline origin/main
npx vitest run --root .worktrees/baseline
git worktree remove .worktrees/baseline
```

**The worktree has to live inside the checkout, which is what `.worktrees/` above is for**: created anywhere else (a session scratchpad under `/private/tmp`, say) Node cannot walk up to this repo's `node_modules`, and the run dies at `Cannot find module 'vitest/config'` while loading the config, which reads as a broken branch rather than a misplaced worktree. Use `HEAD` in place of `origin/main` while your change is still uncommitted, and the parent of your branch's first commit (the oldest one `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` lists, with `^` after it) if `main` has moved since you branched. `--root` runs the worktree's own tests under its own `vitest.config.ts` (checked: a config change made only in the worktree changes what runs) and resolves this checkout's `node_modules`, so nothing is installed and nothing needs a `cd`. Remove the worktree straight after: while it is under `.worktrees/`, `npx vitest run` here collects its test files as well. Then run `npx vitest run` here for the "after", adding `--exclude '.claude/**'` in a local checkout that has worktrees there (the TAC-395 gotcha), so both runs collect the same files. On a resume, the "after" is `npx vitest run --root <checkout>/.worktrees/resume`: run here, it would test the side folder's copy against `main`'s code. `npx vitest list --filesOnly <filename>` proves a specific file is actually collected rather than silently skipped: it prints the path, or nothing.

THE-164 covers expanding test coverage.

## CI

GitHub Actions runs on every PR and push to `main` (workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`):

1. `tsc --noEmit` — typecheck
2. `npm run lint` — eslint
3. `npx vitest run` — unit tests
4. `npm run build` — Next.js build verification

Steps run sequentially with fail-fast (a tsc failure skips the rest). All steps run with mock env vars set in the workflow YAML — no GitHub Secrets configured. If a future test or module-load path requires real credentials, prefer adding a placeholder to the env-mock block first; reach for GitHub Secrets only if the value can't be public.

When CI fails, the GitHub PR check shows which step failed. Reproduce locally with the same command. Most common failures are tsc (run `npx tsc --noEmit`) and lint (run `npm run lint -- --fix` for auto-fixable issues).

CI does NOT make external service calls. If you add a test that hits Voyage/Anthropic/Supabase/Sendblue, CI will either fail (no real API key) or slow down significantly. Mock at the test boundary instead.

Branch protection requires the `CI / ci` status check to pass before merging to `main` (configured in repo settings; see README for the operator checklist).

## Observability and alerting

Three layers, each filling a different gap. Don't conflate them.

- **PostHog events.** Product/event analytics. Captures inbound/outbound events, fidelity scores, classification outputs, etc. Configured to fire to Slack on certain event filters. Today only fires on errors; THE-187 expands coverage to silent failures (low fidelity, empty corpus, classification confidence drops, latency spikes, regeneration cycles, webhook silence). PostHog event emission is wrapped in try/catch — failures must not crash the agent path.
- **Slack alerts** (THE-159). Diagnostic-rich alert content for fired alerts. Narrow scope: improves what existing alerts say, doesn't change what fires.
- **Trace-level observability.** Per-run visibility into the agent's reasoning (corpus retrieval scores, prompt content, fidelity self-rating, etc.). Wired up via Langfuse Cloud (THE-200). `lib/observability/langfuse.ts` is a thin wrapper exposing `startAgentTrace` returning an `AgentTrace` (`span()`, `update()`, `flushAsync()`); spans expose `span()` / `generation()` / `update()` / `end()`. Wrapper invariants:
  - Never throws. SDK errors are caught at the wrapper boundary and logged via `console.warn` — observability is diagnostic, not load-bearing.
  - No-op fallback when `NODE_ENV=test`, `LANGFUSE_ENABLED=false`, any of the three env vars (`LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, host) are missing, or SDK init throws. The host can come from `LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` (preferred — matches the SDK's `baseUrl` constructor field) or `LANGFUSE_HOST` (legacy alias accepted for compatibility with Langfuse's own docs / Vercel integration; slated for removal post-pilot). `BASE_URL` wins when both are set. In no-op mode `trace.id === ''`, all methods are silent no-ops, and agent code runs unchanged.
  - Trace ID is available synchronously the moment `startAgentTrace` returns. `schedule-and-send.ts` writes `trace.id || null` to `messages.langfuse_trace_id` at insert time so traces are queryable from the row.
  - Span tree per agent run: `agent.inbound` (or `agent.followup`) → `context_build` → `classify` (inbound only) → `retrieve` → `retrieve_knowledge` (conditional, gated by `shouldRetrieveKnowledge` in `lib/agent/stages.ts`: always for inbound, only for followup `event` / `manual` triggers) → `generate` → `verify_grounding` (TAC-350; **widened by TAC-376** — `verifyGroundingStage` now runs on every proactive generation too (followups, the knowledge-gap holding message), not just inbound, same verifier/triggers/failure posture; the named `verify_grounding` Langfuse SPAN itself stays inbound-only, since only `handle-inbound.ts` wraps the call in `trace.span('verify_grounding', ...)` — `handle-followup.ts` and `handle-holding-message.ts` call the stage without a dedicated span, a pre-existing asymmetry this ticket didn't touch. Only makes a real call when `generation.knowledgeGap === false` and the guest isn't a demo guest — see `verifyGroundingStage`) → `send`. The `generate` span has post-hoc `generate.attempt_N` sub-spans synthesized from `attemptScores` — these have no real per-attempt timing; threading the trace into `lib/ai`'s regen loop for true timing is tracked in THE-215. Knowledge retrieval degrades gracefully on Voyage / DB error (logs + returns `[]`, span closes normally with `matchCount=0`); voice retrieval continues to fail closed because voice failure breaks voice fidelity itself.
  - Spans carry **metadata always** (counts, scores, IDs in `output` / span input) and **content gated** by `LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT` (full inbound body, full retrieved corpus chunks, full system + user prompts, per-attempt generations, full sent body — folded into `output.content` when on, dropped entirely when off; THE-216). Default-on; set `LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=false` to revert to THE-200's metadata-only shape (e.g. for a venue with strict data-handling requirements). The flag is read once at module init — flipping it requires a redeploy. `lib/agent/trace-content.ts` centralizes the per-stage content shape (`buildRecognitionContent`, `buildCorpusContent`, `buildGenerateContent`, `buildGenerateAttemptContent`); `trace.captureContent` is exposed so handlers can skip building heavy payloads when no one will look at them. Coverage gap doc lives in the THE-216 PR description.
  - `flushAsync` is awaited in the `finally` block of each handler. Both handlers run inside a `waitUntil` keep-alive window from their callers (webhook route, cron) so the flush completes before the function returns.
  - `/admin/health` reports four states via `app/admin/(authed)/health/check-langfuse.ts`: **Active** (all keys + known host, green), **Disabled** (`LANGFUSE_ENABLED=false` set explicitly, neutral), **Misconfigured** (some keys present but not all, or unrecognized host — red, with the specific reason in the detail line), **Not configured** (no `LANGFUSE_*` vars set, neutral — local-dev / no-op is appropriate). The check does not actively probe Langfuse — the SDK has no synchronous ping, and probing on every health-page load would pollute the trace stream.
