## AI agent runtime contract

These constraints are real and have caused bugs:

- **Crisis-safety short circuit (TAC-348):** self-harm/suicidal-ideation or immediate-medical-emergency signals on an inbound get a FIXED, hardcoded reply — never generated, never persona-styled. `ClassifyMessageResult.crisisSafety` (`lib/ai/classify-message.ts`) is an independent boolean alongside `category`, decided by the SAME classifier call (no second LLM round trip). `handle-inbound.ts` checks it immediately after `classifyStage` succeeds — before `retrieveCorpusStage`, `retrieveKnowledgeStage`, `generateStage`, or `applyApprovalPolicyStage` ever run — and on true, dispatches `buildCrisisSafetyResult()`'s fixed body (`lib/agent/crisis-safety.ts`) straight through `scheduleAndSend` (`skipHumanFeelDelay: true`, `reviewReason: 'crisis_safety_reply'`), bypassing the approval gate entirely: no operator flag, by design, because the gate never runs (not because a trigger is suppressed) — same treatment `hold_all_outbound` gives opt-out confirmations. **Why the short circuit sits before retrieval, not just before generation:** `retrieveCorpusStage` fails CLOSED on the inbound path (throws below `MIN_STRONG_MATCHES`), and a crisis message has no reason to resemble venue voice-corpus exemplars — waiting until inside `generateStage` to intervene would let a thin-corpus venue abort the whole run with silence on exactly the turn where silence is worst. **Why fixed text, not a prompt rule:** three prior rounds in `system-template.ts`'s own history (v1.27.0-v1.31.0, the R12 message-splitting saga) show a rule positioned ahead of `# Voice imperative` can still lose to venue persona content rendered later, because that section tells the model the venue's voice wins when the two conflict — unacceptable for a safety reply. `scripts/onboarding/run-test-scenarios.ts` (the TAC-347 harness) carries the identical short circuit in the identical position (right after `classifyStage`, before retrieval), so `adversarial_safety_critical` scenarios grade the actual shipped mechanism, not a full-pipeline generation the code never runs on this turn. `captureCrisisSafetyReplySent` (`lib/analytics/posthog.ts`) is PostHog-only, no Slack relay (owner decision — the reply is fixed and unconditional, so this is audit/count visibility, not an alert). **The classifier's `MAX_CLASSIFIER_INPUT_CHARS` (1000) category-classification cap does NOT apply to crisis detection.** Code review caught that a guest genuinely in crisis may write a long, escalating message where the actual statement lands past that cutoff — silently defeating the whole mechanism with no error and no alert. `classifyMessage` (`lib/ai/classify-message.ts`) appends a SECOND block to the user prompt, bounded by its own more generous `MAX_CRISIS_CHECK_INPUT_CHARS` (4000), carrying the fuller text explicitly scoped to the `crisisSafety` determination only, whenever the body exceeds the category cap — the category-facing block stays truncated and unchanged. Adds nothing to the prompt for the common case (body under 1000 chars).

**Known gap, deliberately out of scope for this ticket:** the guest's NEXT inbound after a crisis reply goes through the normal pipeline unchanged and could produce an upbeat or promotional-sounding reply with no awareness a crisis turn just happened.

**`lib/voices/regenerate-with-critique.ts` mirrors this short circuit too** (its own file header already commits to mirroring `stages.ts` gating changes) — see that file's own TAC-348 note. Without this, an operator who regenerates a crisis-safety auto-sent reply from the Voices playground (indistinguishable in the thread view from an ordinary AI reply — `review_reason` isn't rendered there) would trigger a full persona-driven `generateMessage` call against the original crisis inbound, with zero safety framing, and could commit that output to the voice corpus as a style exemplar. `regenerateWithCritique` now checks `crisisSafety` immediately after its own `classifyMessage` call and returns a distinct `crisis_safety_ineligible` outcome instead of proceeding to generation.
- **Voice fidelity floor (3-tier, TAC-212):** the agent self-rates voice fidelity. Below `SEND_FIDELITY_FLOOR` (0.4) → refused with red alert (existing behavior — `generateStage` returns `'refused'`, no row is persisted, no send). At or above 0.4 but below `AUTO_SEND_FIDELITY_FLOOR` (0.6) → queued for operator review (`applyApprovalPolicyStage` fires the `fidelity_below_auto_send_floor` trigger). At or above 0.6 → continues to the resource-commitment + sticky-pending gates inside `applyApprovalPolicyStage`. Both floors live in `lib/agent/stages.ts`. The intermediate `VOICE_FIDELITY_LOW_THRESHOLD` (0.5) still fires the `voice_fidelity_low` PostHog observation event for the 0.4–0.5 band (now always queued).
- **Corpus retrieval floor:** retrieval is fail-closed *on the inbound path*. Need at least `MIN_STRONG_MATCHES` (1) chunk scoring at or above `STRONG_MATCH_SIMILARITY` (0.3); below that, the agent bails to a fallback acknowledgment. Followup path skips the gate entirely (THE-231) — operator-initiated sends shouldn't be blocked by sparse corpus retrieval. Defined in `lib/agent/stages.ts`.
- **Classifier confidence routing (TAC-240, v1.11.0):** 3-tier handling in `classifyStage`. Above `CLASSIFICATION_CONFIDENCE_LOW_THRESHOLD` (0.7) → keep the classifier's pick, no event. Between `CLASSIFICATION_CONFIDENCE_REROUTE_THRESHOLD` (0.3) and 0.7 → keep the pick + fire `classification_low_confidence` (operator should check). Below 0.3 → rewrite the returned `Classification.category` to `'unknown'` so the agent ships a holding response; original category and confidence are preserved on the PostHog event payload (`autoRoutedToUnknown=true`) and on the returned `Classification` for observability. Regen path (`lib/voices/regenerate-with-critique.ts`) does not apply the reroute — operator iterates on the output. Classifier inputs were also widened to receive `recentMessages` + `guestState` so one-word inbounds ("yes", "iced") can be classified in conversational + relationship context; classifier `temperature` dropped from the SDK default 1.0 to 0.2 (analytical task); inbound is truncated to `MAX_CLASSIFIER_INPUT_CHARS` (1000) before classification while generation still gets the full body.
- **Per-message emoji cadence (TAC-362, v1.48.0):** whether a given message carries an emoji is decided in CODE by a weighted coin, not by the model reading a frequency word. `resolveEmojiDirective(policy, rng)` (`lib/ai/emoji-cadence.ts`) is flipped once per generation inside `buildAiRuntime` — the only place holding both the venue's `emojiPolicy` and the rng, same reasoning as TAC-301's open/closed join — and `runtimeToProse` renders the result as `## Emoji for this message`, the last BLOCK of the user prompt — ahead of the runtime-facts tail, so it is the last INSTRUCTION the model reads rather than literally the last text. `composePrompt` runs once before `generateMessage`'s regen loop, so all attempts of one message share one directive.
  **The measured basis, because the numbers are the whole argument.** Counting every generated outbound per RESPONSE (`coalesce(generation_id, id)` — per-ROW counting reads a split response's first bubble as a clean miss and understates this): `never` 0/52, `sparingly` **0/188**, `frequent` **10/11**. Two conclusions. (1) The model obeys a per-message emoji instruction near-perfectly in both directions, which is what makes moving the decision into `Math.random()` work where a reworded "occasionally" would not — the sentence "an emoji now and then, not in every text" sat in Le Mil's prompt on every one of those turns and still produced 10/11, because a frequency word has no referent inside a single generation. Same failure TAC-319 paid for on splitting, same fix. **Do not read that sentence as evidence of what the venue wanted** — the transcript (1:15:22) has the owner asking for the opposite ("always use emojis... hit them with emojis until they're like why"), so `emojiPolicy: frequent` was faithful and 10/11 was the system obeying. The `tone` sentence matches nothing in the transcript; extraction fabricated it. It is mechanism evidence only. (2) **The enum has three values and two behaviours**: `sparingly` is empirically identical to `never`, because its guidance ends "Default to none" and the model takes that literally. That second finding is RECORDED, NOT FIXED — `EMOJI_PROBABILITY.sparingly` is deliberately `null` (no flip, no block, persona statement unchanged) so Mock Sextant stays at 0%; giving it a probability is its own ticket with its own evidence. `never` is `null` for a different reason: it already works and its persona prohibition always renders, which is what makes "a venue set to no emoji gets none" hold by construction.
  `EMOJI_PROBABILITY.frequent = 0.75` is **a deliberate softening of a stated preference, not a calibration** — the owner asked for MORE emoji and the pre-change ~91% was closer to that request; the product judgment (recorded on TAC-362) is that literal compliance reads as a template rather than warmth. Labelled that way in its own docstring because a guess that reads as a measurement is how `KNOWLEDGE_RELEVANCE_FLOOR = 0.5` survived until TAC-358. **Known consequence, recorded not fixed: there is now no setting meaning "an emoji in nearly every message"** — `frequent` is the top of the enum and caps at 0.75, so a venue that wants what Le Mil's actually asked for cannot express it. It is a CEILING: `'allowed'` is permission the model can decline, never a mandate (a mandate would restore the determinism at a lower rate), so the realised rate sits below it. Verified live at Le Mil's across **48 generations on two different inbounds: 35 `allowed` (72.9%), 32 with emoji (66.7%), and 0 violations across all 13 `none` turns.** Baseline was 10/11 = 90.9% with no variation at all.
  **No strip backstop, deliberately.** `emojiDirectiveViolated` recomputes on the final body and `generateStage` fires `emoji_directive_violated` (PostHog only, no Slack relay — a voice-quality observation, not an alert); the body SHIPS. A regex-strip would be this repo's first post-generation body mutation, against a 0-in-272 measured violation rate, and carries a real empty-body edge (a single-emoji reply strips to nothing, which TAC-309 made load-bearing at the send guard). If that rate moves, the strip lands with evidence behind it.
  **Category-gated, and the gate is the compliance half.** `shouldRenderEmojiDirective` (`serializers.ts`) suppresses the block for `opt_out` and `comp_complaint`, mirroring `shouldRenderOpenIntentions`'s placement and TAC-328's reasoning. Caught in code review, not in the plan: the block renders LAST in the user prompt while a category instruction sits in the SYSTEM prompt, so on proximity the block wins — a trailing "an emoji is welcome here" would have outranked `OPT_OUT_INSTRUCTIONS`' "respectful and final" on ~75% of opt-outs at a `frequent` venue. **TAC-389 adds a THIRD suppression, and it is not a category**: an operator-initiated decline. That turn renders as `manual`, shared with ordinary Command Center follow-ups (THE-232) which keep the directive, so the two are distinguishable only per turn — the gate takes `isOperatorDecline` as a second argument rather than gaining a third entry in the category list. The argument is `comp_complaint`'s unmodified: permission is the wrong thing to hand the model on an apology turn, and a decline apologises for cancelling something the venue promised. At a `frequent` venue it was reaching roughly three decline drafts in four. All three exclusions are strictly NARROWER than what shipped before (the old standing licence applied on every turn), so the gate can only reduce emoji. Scope is otherwise unaudited — not a claim these are the only turns that should suppress it.
  **The grader's `frequent` emoji limit changed from `Infinity` to 1** (`scripts/onboarding/grade-voice-deterministic.ts`), because the per-message block says "at most one" and an unlimited grader would let a four-emoji reply violate the prompt and pass the grade. The count distinction between `sparingly` and `frequent` is no longer per-message; it is the per-message PROBABILITY, which a single-message grader cannot see. The existing "frequent policy never fails on emoji count" test was UPDATED to assert the reversal rather than deleted. **The shared detector also carries four behavioural deltas, enumerated in the grader's own comment** because a first version of that comment undercounted them: text-default pictographic symbols (`®` `™` `©` `‼` `ℹ` `▶`) and plain arrows no longer count (the detector's base is `Emoji_Presentation`, or `Extended_Pictographic` plus an explicit U+FE0F — `Extended_Pictographic` alone would grade "Analog®" as an emoji at a `never` venue); a ZWJ-joined family counts as ONE rather than as each component, which is the delta that flips a `sparingly` verdict; and flag sequences now count at all, which the replaced regex named as a known gap in its own comment.
  **Not fixed here, and it is worse than a misrouting:** `extract.ts` wrote a `brand_persona.tone` sentence stating the OPPOSITE of what the interviewee said — a fabrication in the persona, not a style description filed in the wrong field — and every venue onboarded from here inherits that risk. Filed as TAC-371 (TAC-331 precedent).
- **A link in a reply must be on the venue's curated list, or the draft is held (TAC-509, v1.55.0; scheme rule and prompt copy v1.56.0).** `venue_info.links` is an array of `{label, url}` that Jaipal maintains by hand per venue, and it is the ONLY source of sendable links. **Nothing is derived** — not from retrieved knowledge chunks, not from the composed prompt, not from `venue_info.contact`. A link is sendable because a human put it on a list. **Why a curated list rather than a groundedness check:** the grounding verifier is a semantic judge and would accept a link differing by one path segment, and the threat is not only misquoting a link that exists — the model can build a plausible `lemils.com/products/...` out of what it knows about Shopify with no link in its source material at all. A wrong URL is worse than a wrong phone number because it LOOKS right: that path resolves to a live store, so a fabricated slug is a 404 in the guest's hand.
  **Three pieces.** `lib/schemas/venue-info.ts` stores it as `z.array(z.unknown()).optional().catch(undefined)` and validates per entry at the READ boundary in `parseVenueLinks`; see that field's own comment for why any strictness there is a write-path hazard (the admin venue-info PATCH route re-parses the whole object and writes `validated.data`, so a strict shape would let an admin editing hours silently delete a link, and a throwing shape would take down `buildRuntimeContext` for the venue). A dropped entry shrinks the allowlist, so every failure holds rather than sends. `venueInfoToProse` renders a `## Links` section, ALWAYS, including the empty state — the empty state is what speaks to the invented-link case, and its closing sentence deliberately keeps bare-domain phrasing legal because the venue's own knowledge says "on lemils.com". Its copy instruction names the scheme ("character for character, including the https:// at the start", v1.56.0): the detector now accepts a schemeless link, so this prose no longer decides whether the draft ships, but a link written in full is one the guest can tap in every client, and the instruction it replaced read as satisfied by what the model actually did. `lib/ai/url-detector.ts` is the deterministic check, in `generateMessage`'s per-attempt loop beside `DASH_REGEX` and `matchSelfTalk`, sharing their attempt budget and their sticky-constraint handling (see the em-dash bullet below); the constraint names the offending links, because the usual miss is one character in a slug, and accumulates them across attempts.
  **Matching:** exact string, after trailing sentence punctuation is trimmed and after `canonicalizeUrl` has reduced BOTH sides to one form. It applies exactly TWO normalizations. (1) Exactly one trailing `/` comes off (ruled 2026-09-21 — `https://lemils.com` and `https://lemils.com/` are the same destination and the list should not have to guess which the model writes); a doubled trailing slash is a different path and is held. (2) **A MISSING scheme becomes `https://`** — v1.56.0, from the device UAT that failed v1.55.0 on its first test: asked where to buy the beans the agent wrote the RIGHT page as `lemils.com/products/le-mils-budan-bold`, the way anyone writes a link in a DM, and the draft was held. Applied to both sides, so it is symmetric and a listed schemeless entry matches a drafted `https://` link; the failure needed only one direction, but a one-directional rule is a second thing to remember at every read and the reverse case is the same destination by the same argument. **An EXPLICIT scheme is never rewritten, so `http://` still does not match a listed `https://`** — http is a different, downgradeable destination, not an omission. Nothing else is normalized: case, query string and path stay significant. **Bare domains are not links** and never fire the check — "lemils.com" has no path, and it follows from the trailing-slash rule that "lemils.com/" is the same bare domain. A scheme makes a token a link however short its path.
  **The scheme is supplied at COMPARISON time, never at extraction**, and the two must not share a helper: `canonicalizeUrl` prepends `https://`, whose own `//` would make every bare domain look like it had a path, so `isUrl` calls the slash-only `stripOneTrailingSlash` instead. A mutant pointing `isUrl` at `canonicalizeUrl` dies to four bare-domain tests; the comment at both functions says so.
  **`UNVERIFIED_URL` queues, never sends**, ranked directly above `SELF_TALK_DETECTED`: both are deterministic loop backstops meaning the text is confirmed broken, neither is a money exposure, and a wrong link outranks self-talk because the guest ACTS on it. `PUSH_POLICY` pushes — the card carries no timer, so nothing else surfaces it. `captureUnverifiedUrlHeld` Slack-relays and carries `allowedUrlCount`, which is what separates "the model invented a link" from "this venue has no list yet"; the two are identical on the card and have different fixes.
  **Known and accepted:** `contact.website` still renders into the prompt via `formatContact` but is NOT sendable, so a reply sharing the venue homepage is held until that URL is added to `links`. All three venues had a `contact.website` and no `links` when this shipped. **The operator app was deliberately not touched** — `REVIEW_REASON_LABELS` ships the sentence from this server, so the card reads correctly with no client build, but `analog-operator/lib/review-bucket.ts`'s `BUCKET_BY_CODE` is a hand-kept mirror, so the card sits on the mid-thread ground with a "Needs review" strip until `unverified_url: 'draftWrong'` is added there.
- **Em-dash regen loop (THE-225) — CORRECTED BY TAC-362, the prior wording described behaviour this repo does not have.** R3 in `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE` says no em dashes, but Sonnet still emits them occasionally even at high voice fidelity, so `DASH_REGEX` forces a regen inside `generateMessage`'s per-attempt loop (`lib/ai/generate-message.ts`). **What happens when the attempts exhaust is the part that was documented wrong:** the dash is NOT hard-blocked, NOT rewritten, and the body ships unmodified — `dashViolationPersisted` is a recompute of the BOOLEAN on the final body, and `stages.ts` turns it into a PostHog/Slack observation. `voiceFidelity` is likewise the model's own unmodified number; nothing recomputes it. **There is therefore NO post-generation body mutation anywhere on the generation path**, which matters because the old wording reads as a precedent for adding one: TAC-362 nearly built an emoji strip-backstop on it and only caught the error by reading the code. Third instance in this file of a written claim that was never true (see `approval_policy`'s 102 unread days and the `future-add safety` test that asserted its own opposite) — the lesson generalizes past this line.
  **The regen directives are STICKY for the whole `generateMessage` call (TAC-509 follow-up, ruled 2026-09-21), and every one is worded as a standing constraint.** They used to be rebuilt each iteration from only the just-completed attempt's violations, so a directive left the prompt the moment its own check passed — even when the loop carried on for a different reason. **That drop was safe BY CONSTRUCTION while the dash was the only non-fidelity check**: a dash-clean attempt that also passed fidelity broke the loop, so nothing came after it to put a dash back. TAC-355 (self-talk) and TAC-509 (unverified links) each added a reason to keep looping past a dash-clean body, and since the loop returns the LAST attempt rather than the best one, the dropped directive started costing real drafts. Live, Le Mil's 2026-09-21: attempt 1 had a dash and an unlisted link, attempt 2 fixed the dash and kept the link so the dash constraint left the prompt, attempt 3 worked on the link and put a dash back, and that body is the one that was held. **The wording is part of the mechanism, not presentation** — a sticky directive phrased as feedback ("your previous attempt contained a dash") becomes a false statement the moment it outlives the attempt it describes, which once sticky is every attempt after the first it appears in; so each reads "do not use a dash character", and the unverified-link one states that the named links are not approved rather than that the last attempt used them. The link set ACCUMULATES, so a model that swaps one wrong link for another is told both are unapproved. A test pins that no prompt contains "Your previous attempt", and dropping stickiness kills the test named for the live sequence. **What this does NOT fix is that the loop returns the last attempt rather than the best one** — a dash-clean attempt 1 or 2 is still discarded in favour of attempt 3 whenever another check kept the loop running. That is its own ticket.
- **Visit history block (TAC-234, v1.13.0):** `RuntimeContext.recentVisits` carries up to `MAX_VISIT_HISTORY_TRANSACTIONS` (20) transactions within the past `MAX_VISIT_HISTORY_DAYS` (90) for the guest, most-recent-first. Rendered as `## Visit history` in the user prompt with bracketed time-delta bullets matching the `## Recent conversation` style. Replaces the v1.12 single-transaction `## Last visit` block. The intro line tells Sonnet to use this for pattern recognition (recommendations, "what haven't I tried") — not to recite history back at the guest. Skipped at the block level for `welcome` and `opt_out`. Empty `recentVisits` omits the block entirely (parallels `## Recent conversation`'s skip-on-empty; distinct from `## Venue knowledge`'s render-explicit-no-match — that pattern exists because the model might invent venue facts, R9 is the safety net there). Projection lives in `lib/agent/extract-recent-visits.ts`.
- **Guest relationship surfacing (TAC-234, v1.13.0):** `recognition.state` is now rendered as `Guest relationship: <state>` directly after the inbound framing line, symmetric with the classifier's TAC-240 surfacing. Closes the tone-calibration gap between regulars and new guests. Single source of truth: the recognition snapshot — surfacing only, no recomputation.
- **runtimeToProse field-presence rendering (TAC-234, v1.13.0):** the per-category switch in `lib/ai/prompts/serializers.ts` was replaced with three independent conditional blocks: inbound framing (one consistent `The guest just sent: "..."` line for any inbound), `perk_unlock` data, `event_invite` data. Carve-outs ("just asked", "(opt-out request)") collapsed into the unified inbound line — the category-specific instructions in the system prompt already convey question vs statement intent. The mutual exclusion between inbound and outbound runtime contexts is enforced by the orchestrator entry points (`handleInbound` populates `inboundMessage`; `handleFollowup` populates `perkBeingUnlocked` or `eventBeingInvited`); type-system enforcement is tracked separately as TAC-243 (backlog).
- **Recent conversation block:** the last 14 days of messages between this guest and this venue are loaded into RuntimeContext. THE-173 added this; future changes to the window should consider impact on synthetic-guest seeding (`run-test-scenarios` seeds messages >30 days old to keep this block empty during testing).
  **Every history line says whether the guest received it (TAC-394, v1.50.0).** Until this, the history query had no filter on `status` or `review_state` and `RecentMessage` carried no delivery field, so a pending draft rendered exactly like a sent message. On 2026-09-14 a model regenerating a pending comp ("the next one's on us") read the comp as already offered, replied only to the guest's next question, and TAC-264's regen-in-place replaced the comp with that reply. **The draft stays IN history and is MARKED, never excluded** (ruling): a pending comp the model cannot see is one it offers a second time, which is TAC-398 arrived at from the other side. `deriveDelivery` (`lib/agent/group-responses.ts`) is the one rule, and `RecentMessage.delivery` is required so no construction site can default a line to delivered:
  - inbound → `delivered`
  - outbound with `review_state = 'pending'` → `awaiting_review` (checked BEFORE status, so no status value can make a pending row read as sent)
  - outbound at `sending` / `sent` / `delivered` → `delivered`
  - outbound with `review_state = 'skipped'` and no delivered status → `skipped_by_operator`
  - outbound with `review_state = 'resolved_externally'` and no delivered status → `answered_outside_app` (TAC-473), marked `NOT SENT: the venue answered this in the Instagram app instead`. **Its own value rather than the catch-all**, which is where it landed until code review: its `status` stays `pending_review`, so without naming it here the prompt told the model a send had FAILED on every turn after staff answered by hand, with the echo carrying their actual words in the same history marked delivered. Same reason `skipped` is its own value. **Adding a `review_state` or `status` value is not additive** — audit this function, the reached-guest condition, migrations 041/054's slot indexes, both badge counts and `/undo` before assuming otherwise.
  - any other outbound (failed, rejected, draft, the approved-but-never-dispatched gap, and any status nobody has mapped yet) → `never_sent`
  **`sending` counts as delivered here and NOT in `count_outbound_responses`, on purpose.** The Sendblue webhook maps QUEUED to `sending` and its callbacks arrive out of order, so a message the guest read can sit at `sending` indefinitely. Leaving it out of a reply-rate count under-counts; marking it NEVER SENT in a prompt invites the model to say it again. The Command Center viewer's `TRAVELED_STATUSES` makes the same call. A split response is delivered if ANY bubble was. A delivered status beats `skipped`: an operator can only skip a pending draft, so a skipped row never went out, and if one ever carried a delivered status the guest read it.
  Rendering (`formatRecentConversation`, and `formatClassifierRecentConversation` for the markers and note): each unsent line gets a marker inside its bracket saying WHY it never arrived: `NOT SENT: waiting for the venue to approve it`, `NOT SENT: the venue decided not to send it`, or `NEVER SENT: it failed to send`. One note follows the block when any line is marked. **There is deliberately no instruction about what to do with an unsent line.** v1.50.0 was first built with one (the reply takes the pending draft's place, so offer a pending comp, hold or discount again), scoped by a `pendingDraftReplacedByReply` flag, with pending lines exempt from truncation and knowledge-gap cards given their own delivery value so they never got it. The 2026-09-14 ruling removed the instruction before release, and the flag, the exemption and the gap-card value went with it, since nothing else read them. **A skip gets its own marker** because a bare "never sent" beside "they have not read them" can nudge the model to raise content an operator decided not to send, which is TAC-398 arriving from a third direction. **A history with nothing unsent renders byte-for-byte as v1.49.0**; the note appends only when a marker is present, and in both renderers (the generator's and the classifier's) a test pins the whole block exactly, so anything appended after the note fails it however it is worded.
  **The removed instruction, and why (measured 2026-09-14).** On a turn the gate won't guarantee review (`willBeReviewed` false, e.g. `new_question`), `## What this guest can access` says "Do not offer comps, remakes, replacements, or discounts" (no eligible perks) or "Do not offer items that are not on this list" (some), so an instruction to offer a pending comp again contradicted it. **Measured with the bar set before running (n=10 per arm, synthetic venue, incident history):** a structured comp was re-emitted 0/10 on the old prompt, **6/10 with the instruction and the denial present** (missing the ≥7 bar), and 10/10 with the perks block removed. Under the conflict the model wrote long two-topic replies: **7/10 kept an em dash**, and **3/10 self-rated voice fidelity 0.00**, which `generateStage` refuses, leaving the guest with no reply. An informational re-run after rewording gave 9/10 re-emitted and 2/10 at 0.00. Em dashes appeared in 6/10, and in 5/10 with the perks block removed, so the dashes came with the two-topic reply, not with the conflict. **The ruling dropped the instruction rather than touching the denial**: post-incident safety wording is not edited to move a metric. Scoping it ("do not originate a comp" rather than "do not repeat one the venue drafted") needs its own ruling and ticket. **Markers-only re-run (prediction posted before generating, n=20 per arm):**
  - Refusals and dashes: neither baseline nor markers-only had a generation below the 0.4 floor or any em dash (0/20 each), and all 40 replies answered the hours question.
  - Fidelity: markers-only ran 0.72–0.85 (median 0.82), baseline 0.75–0.85.
  - Comp: neither arm re-emitted a structured comp or offered one in prose.

  Observed but not pre-registered: **17/20 markers-only replies acknowledged the cortado complaint**, where baseline never did. **6/20 said some form of "we'll make it right"**, which v1.23.0 counts as a resource commitment. **Measured afterwards whether the gate holds them** (n=60; pattern and reading posted before generating; real grounding check and gate; pending-draft detection off):
  - **Held, 20/20 matching replies; none would auto-send.** The hold came from the grounding verifier (`knowledge_gap_backstop`, 20/20), which read the promise as contradicting the no-comps denial in the runtime context.
  - **The control v1.23.0 relies on barely fired:** the model's self-flag caught 3/20, and the comp regex 0/20.
  - **So the hold was fragile when measured.** It rested on a check that failed open on transient faults, did not run on followups at the time (`verifyGroundingStage` skipped without an inbound), and cited a denial that renders only for a guest with no eligible perks. Two of those three have since been closed — TAC-376 made it run on followups and the holding message, and TAC-424 made a transient fault hold rather than pass through — so re-measure before repeating the fragility claim.
  - **Under option B's decision 1 as planned** (send beside a protected obligation card when nothing else holds the reply, otherwise drop), all 20 of those turns would be DROPPED, and 29 of the 60 overall. The guest asking the hours would get no reply about half the time on this turn shape. Option F, which shipped instead, does not drop them: a held reply with no structured obligation takes the conversation slot beside the comp card (see *Two pending slots per guest* under the single-pending-draft invariant).
  - **The grounding verifier also reads the markers**, because it is handed the generator's own prompt. It flagged "sorry again" because the earlier apology was never sent.
  **Known residue, not fixed:** a regenerated row keeps its original `created_at` (TAC-264 kept queue position deliberately), so a draft rewritten and then approved still sorts ABOVE the question it answers, and the next turn's history reads the answer before the question. The operator thread endpoints (`lib/operator/thread.ts`) run their own history query; TAC-395 filters them to messages that reached the guest rather than marking delivery (see *Full-thread fetch*).
  **Also not fixed:** a pending draft more than 14 days old, or behind 30 later responses, falls out of history entirely and is still regenerated over, unmarked. And three delivery edge cases read wrong. (1) An operator dispatch whose Sendblue send succeeded but whose status write failed stays `pending_review`/`approved` and reads `never_sent` though the guest received it. (2) An ERROR callback arriving after DELIVERED sets `failed`, so that row reads `never_sent` too. (3) An operator dispatch in flight: `dispatchOperatorOutbound` flips `review_state` from pending to approved BEFORE calling Sendblue and writes `status='sent'` only after, so a guest inbound in those seconds reads the line as `NEVER SENT: it failed to send`. With the row no longer pending, `previous_pending_held` no longer holds the reply either, so the reply can repeat what the guest is receiving.
- **Today's date in context:** `RuntimeContext.todayInVenueTimezone` is set from `new Date()` at runtime, formatted in the venue's timezone. THE-174 added this so the agent answers "are you open today?" correctly.
- **Venue capability is a venue fact, and `hold` is conditional on it (TAC-301 part 2, v1.46.0):** the prompt carried THREE statements about holding that could not all be true — `# Hard rules` ("no promises about staff or stock"), `# Resource commitment self-flag` (holding is permitted but gated), and `# Commitments` (`hold` as a first-class type with a worked example) — and R34, four commits earlier, carved holding OUT of its own prohibition and reaffirmed it. At a counter-only walk-in venue the prompt was **instructing** the behavior the ticket was filed about. **`# Commitments` is now the single source of truth**: `hold` is available ONLY when the venue-services block says so, and the rule closes the workaround ("anything that amounts to the same thing") rather than just the word. `# Hard rules` no longer re-legislates, but note it still **scopes** reservations and stock rather than dropping them — a first version deleted both outright and code review caught that nothing else covered reservations at any venue. R34's carve-out points at `# Commitments` (wording narrowed, id untouched, `UNIVERSAL_RULES_DISPLAY` in lockstep). **`# Resource commitment self-flag` is deliberately UNCHANGED** — it governs whether a commitment needs approval, never whether the service exists; don't sweep it up in a future tidy. **Worked examples were the highest-leverage half and the easiest to half-fix**: the `# Commitments` heads-up example taught holding by demonstration, and an IDENTICAL readiness demonstration survived 31 lines later in `# Arrival capture` past a test keyed on the deleted noun ("almond croissant") rather than the behavior. Both are gone and the guard now asserts the shapes. `comp-complaint.ts`'s "have it ready for them" remedy is capability-scoped for the same reason — it renders LAST and would otherwise win. Verified behaviourally against Le Mil's live config: `holds:false` declines, `holds:true` permits, unconfigured declines.
- **Open/closed status line (TAC-301, v1.45.0):** the `## Right now` block carries a fourth line stating whether the venue is OPEN (with its closing time) or CLOSED (with the next opening), resolved in code by `resolveOpenState` (`lib/schemas/venue-hours.ts`) and threaded onto `today.openState` by `buildAiRuntime`. **Why in code rather than left to the model:** both inputs were already in the prompt — the weekly hours table via `venueInfoToProse` (system prompt) and the venue-local clock via `formatRightNow` (user prompt) — and at ~7:57pm, five hours after close, the agent still answered "omw can you have my usual ready?" with "Got it, see you soon." Nothing in the twelve-trigger `APPROVAL_TRIGGERS` set keys on time, so that reply auto-sent with no operator in the loop. The model was being asked to join a free-text en-dashed range against a 24h clock across two prompt sections, unprompted, mid-commitment. **`buildAiRuntime` is the only place that holds both halves** (`ctx.venue.venueInfo.hours` + the validated timezone) — `venueInfoToProse` sees the hours but not the clock, `runtimeToProse` sees the clock but not the hours — which is why the join lives there and not in a serializer. The CLOSED line carries its own instruction ("do not tell the guest to come by, and do not confirm anything for right now") rather than stating the fact alone: a bare fact is something the venue persona can talk past, and the failure being fixed is specifically a confirmation. `unknown` renders NOTHING — see the governing rule under `lib/schemas/`, including the three cases a code-review pass had to correct (ambiguous shorthand, absence-as-closure, substituted timezone), each of which would have produced a confident WRONG verdict rather than silence. One `now` is taken per `buildAiRuntime` call so the rendered clock and the verdict can't straddle a minute boundary. The regen path inherits this free (`regenerate-with-critique.ts` imports `buildAiRuntime` rather than mirroring it). **Deliberately no "closing soon" threshold** — the block states the closing time and the current time, and a threshold constant would need its own calibration.
- **Resource commitments are VALUE TRANSFER, not money (v1.23.0):** the `# Resource commitment self-flag` block and the `# Commitments` comp type both test "does the guest end up with product, service, or money they did not pay for" rather than enumerating monetary instruments. A remake, replacement, redo, "another one," or a vague "I'll make it right" is a resource commitment exactly as much as a comp or refund. **This is written from a production incident**: on 2026-08-07 the agent auto-sent "Come by and I'll have another made for you" in direct response to a refund request, `review_reason` NULL, no operator in the loop. The prior wording enumerated "comp, discount, refund, or any monetary credit," and the model's trace reasoning followed it exactly: *"a redo/remake … is standard recovery, not a perk … isn't a 'comp' in the structured sense … I'll leave commitment empty and not flag operator approval since I'm not promising a monetary credit."* All three gates (self-flag, commitment type, comp regex) shared the monetary blind spot. The self-flag carries an explicit carve-out so information promises ("let me find out") don't over-fire — that over-fire direction is a worse bug than the one being fixed, because it stalls complaint threads on turns that commit nothing. `COMP_COMPLAINT_INSTRUCTIONS` states its prohibition flatly and first: the previous "do not promise X **unless** Y" was inverted by the model into standing permission, which it then self-authorized against an empty mechanics list.
- **Warm-but-gated complaint handling (v1.24.0; qualified by TAC-307):** a guest reporting a bad experience gets ONE clarifying question that auto-sends, then a warm, apologetic, comp-forward draft that QUEUES for operator approval and pushes. **The auto-sending clarifying question is conditional as of TAC-307** — it survives only when the `comp_complaint` hold came from the fleet-wide code default. At a venue that explicitly holds `comp_complaint` (or holds everything) from Command Center, the clarifying question queues too. See trigger 8 under *Approval policy gates*. The agent proposes generosity; the human authorizes it. Three parts: (1) `venue_configs.approval_policy` routes `comp_complaint` to `operator_approval` — a column seeded fleet-wide on 2026-04-27 that had **zero readers until v1.24.0**; the code-level `APPROVAL_POLICY_DEFAULT` is the base and stored `perCategory` entries merge ON TOP, so the empty `{}` every venue carries can't erase the route and no data migration was needed. (2) `GeneratedMessageSchema.complaintIntent` (`clarifying | resolving | none`, REQUIRED so it costs zero against the TAC-300 optional budget) drives the only exemption, gated behind four checks in `lib/agent/complaint-routing.ts` that ALL fail toward queue. (3) `AiRuntimeContext.willBeReviewed` conditions the `## What this guest can access` block: when a human is guaranteed to see the draft it invites a proposal, otherwise the v1.23.0 denial stands **verbatim**. **The safety property: warmth is unlocked by the gate, never by loosening the brake.** `willBeReviewed` is FALSE for demo guests even on a routed category, because TAC-284's bypass returns `action:'send'` unconditionally and would ship a comp-forward draft to a real phone. Written after v1.23.0 fixed an unauthorized comp and, forty minutes later in UAT, produced "Sour matcha's usually a sign something was off with the prep. Noted." on a guest complaining about a bad drink — warmth on complaints had **never** been instructed in any prompt version, so this is authored behavior, not a restoration.
- **Universal voice rules R1-R36:** live in `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE` (the count grows — check the file, don't trust a number quoted elsewhere, including this one; a prior version of this line said R1-R15 while the file held 16). R11 landed with TAC-305; R12 (message splitting, TAC-313) is **RETIRED as of TAC-319 v1.31.0** — splitting moved out of the prompt into deterministic dispatch code (see "Message splitting" below) and the id is never reused; R13-R16 are the undisplayed guidance bullets (greeting / operator-instruction / Last-Visit / Unanswered-question — the last added by TAC-308), R17-R20 landed with TAC-314 (price scoping, nearby places, register mirroring, ## Length authority), and R21 landed with TAC-334 (don't volunteer advice the guest didn't ask for). **Numbering is positional, APPEND-ONLY (TAC-314), and retired ids are never reused (TAC-319)** — never insert mid-list; renumbering or recycling live rule IDs stales every external reference (this file, tickets, tests, anti-pattern prose). Apply to every agent on every venue. Don't reference actions the guest didn't take, give today's specific answer, no em dashes, don't reference physical artifacts the agent doesn't have, don't redirect to alt channels for things the venue can answer, yes/no questions get yes/no answers, don't restate context already in the conversation. **TAC-324 (v1.32.0) edits two rules' WORDING without touching numbering or R11/R12.** R1 gains a narrow exception: when the runtime context confirms a `qr_scan` guest's first-ever inbound inside a freshness window, the model may greet them as present (not narrate the scan itself) — see "First-touch intentions" below. R15 (Last-Visit, undisplayed) is scoped rather than reworded: its one-item cap was always about backward references to past visits; a forward recommendation is now explicitly carved out as a separate act that doesn't count against it. `UNIVERSAL_RULES_DISPLAY`'s R1 entry moves in lockstep (its `summary` text); R15 isn't displayed, so no other registry entry changes. **TAC-329 (v1.34.0) rewords R1's carve-out RATIONALE, not its gate.** The TAC-324 physical-presence justification ("greet them as present... the way you'd greet a person standing in front of you") licensed present-tense location assumptions and was observed producing "Password's on the board when you get here" sent to a guest who'd left the venue twenty minutes earlier. Replaced with channel-context framing: the guest knows which number they just texted and why, regardless of where they physically are. `firstTouchAfterQrScan` (the condition that fires the exception) is unchanged; only the prose teaching the model what the exception means moved. `UNIVERSAL_RULES_DISPLAY`'s R1 summary moves in lockstep again. **R21 (v1.37.0, TAC-334) closes a gap R11 does not cover.** R11 governs how a delivered recommendation, description, or fact ENDS; it never fires on a turn that isn't delivering one in the first place. Found in UAT: a guest reported an order already placed ("I got a cortado") and Sana evaluated the choice and proposed a different one for next time, unprompted — the assistant reflex of holding knowledge and therefore deploying it. R21's trigger is scoped to a guest statement containing no question, so a recommendation request ("what should I get") or opinion request ("is the cortado good") never reaches the prohibition at all — the boundary lives in the trigger clause, not in an exception bolted onto an absolute ban, deliberately avoiding the TAC-330 v1.35.0 self-contradicting-qualifier failure mode. `UNIVERSAL_RULES_DISPLAY` gains R21, displayed alongside its closest siblings R10/R11 (both also govern when a recommendation or opinion is permitted). Flagged during TAC-334 UAT (see the ticket for the fifth, reported-not-resolved UAT case); adjacent to TAC-318 (ledger hygiene) and TAC-331 (extraction mood), neither of which this ticket touches. **R22 (v1.38.0, TAC-314 second round) is undisplayed, appended after R21.** Promoted from the jurisdictional carve-out sentence TAC-330 (case 2) added locally to `acknowledgment.ts` — a category's register guidance is never authority over whether the model acts on an open goal from the intentions block. That principle is general, not `acknowledgment`-specific, so it moved to the universal layer where it protects every category from the same silent-veto failure class instead of requiring the same audit-and-patch cycle per category. The local sentence was deleted from `acknowledgment.ts` as a paired move in the same PR — same treatment R17 got. See "Category instruction layer carries NO form authority (TAC-314)" below for the full second-round accounting, including the sibling candidate that was evaluated and deliberately NOT promoted. **R23-R28 (v1.42.0, TAC-348) promote six cross-venue rules mined from Mock Sextant's manual venue-rule history, displayed alongside R17/R18/R21.** R23: no visit-count or tracking language, scoped explicitly against R15 so the two don't collide (R15 permits WHAT the guest had; R23 bans HOW OFTEN); promoted out of `follow-up.ts`, where the equivalent line was removed in the same PR. R24 + R25 + R26 are a deliberately coherent set on menu-item description: don't over-explain familiar drinks, no bare comma-list of ingredients, cap recommendations at two with varied phrasing — R25's content used to live inside the now-retired R12 and was lost when TAC-319 deleted that bullet wholesale. R27: never refer to yourself in the third person when speaking as a named person — TAC-338 explicitly deferred this exact prohibition pending "UAT evidence [that] a symptom survives," which it did (`owner` persona: "lemme check with Himanshu"); scoped to SELF-reference only, since TAC-338 already rejected a broader "them" ban for misfiring on ordinary correct staff speech. R28: never blame or criticize a staff member to a guest. Two candidates from the original nine-item audit were dropped in plan review rather than promoted: a universal "don't push a return visit" ban would contradict `comp-complaint.ts`'s own approved remedy design (a return-visit invitation IS the default comp), and a universal "don't ask curiosity questions" ban would silently outrank the first-touch intentions block's conditional restraint with no carve-out — the same silent-veto class TAC-327/TAC-330 already closed once. **R8 and R11 were reworded, not renumbered, in the same PR** — both gaps are narrow extensions of an existing rule's own stated purpose. R8 now also bans claiming to have personally witnessed the guest ("I saw you earlier") even when the guest's own message confirms the underlying fact (distinct from R1, which is about unconfirmed actions — here the action WAS confirmed, only the sensory-witness claim was invented). R11 now covers the whole description, not just the closing sentence — the original UAT gap was a closer, but the same flourish moved earlier in the sentence wasn't covered by wording that only named "a closing sentence." **R29-R31 (v1.43.0, TAC-356) promote three more rules mined the same way, displayed alongside R17/R18/R21/R23-R28.** R29 permits a sentence fragment when it reads naturally ("Open until 3" beats "We are open until 3pm today"), written as permission rather than a mandate and self-contained (it states its own deference to a full-sentence venue voice rather than relying solely on `# Voice imperative` three sections later). R30 says to ask what a guest means rather than guess when their message is unclear, with an explicit carve-out against the `unknown` category's own classifier-driven holding response (TAC-240's low-confidence routing is a system-decided outcome, a different kind of "unclear" than content ambiguity within an otherwise-confidently-categorized message) — the same scoping technique R23 used against R15. R31 bans naming a specific product in reply to a greeting or any content-less message, the fix for a real production incident at Le Mil's (a guest's "hey" got "come try Indian coffee sometime" back); the category a bare guest greeting actually classifies to is `casual_chatter`, whose only instruction was "stay in voice" with nothing stopping this. All three were audited against the first-touch intentions opener (TAC-324/329) and found compatible: the opener only ever asks a question, never names a product, so R31 doesn't conflict, and R30's trigger is a structural flag unrelated to message clarity. No conflicts required dropping a candidate this round. **R32-R34 (v1.44.0, TAC-359) promote a third round of three more rules mined the same way, from a second Le Mil's owner-review run, displayed alongside R17/R18/R21/R23-R31.** R32: never tell the guest to send a message, reach out, or get in touch as if that's a separate, future action, since they're already texting. Checked against `invite_contact_save` (`lib/agent/intentions/definitions.ts`), which legitimately invites a guest to save the number and text again later — the rule scopes to same-turn redundancy and carries an explicit carve-out for future contact, plus a boundary note against R5 (alt-channels is a different axis: routing elsewhere vs. treating the current channel as a future action) so the two don't sit unacknowledged near each other. R33: when retrieved venue knowledge narrates a first-visit order as a multi-step sequence, recommend only the first step. This is the first universal rule of this promotion pattern that DIRECTS rather than prohibits — a straight ban on sequences would be outranked by the venue's own knowledge_corpus content, which renders later in the prompt than this section (`compose-prompt.ts`: template → persona → venue_info → voice corpus → knowledge corpus → category instructions), the same most-proximate-wins failure class as TAC-314/329/330/338. venue_info itself was audited and found clean (not a repeat of TAC-330's "Maiden Voyage" defect); the contributor was an accurate, correctly-attributed knowledge_corpus chunk. Carries a boundary against R26 (item count vs. framing). R34: the agent cannot place, confirm, or take an order — acknowledge what the guest wants and defer to how that specific venue actually takes orders, never asserting a channel (an early draft said "at the counter," which would misinstruct any venue without counter service). Two carve-outs: `# Commitments` holds are scoped to items that already exist AND (TAC-301 part 2) to venues whose services block says they hold at all (a made-to-order drink is not held, it is made, so prep instructions stay on the order-taking side), and a guest reporting an order already placed points at R21 rather than restating it, so TAC-323's `extract-reported-order.ts` (past-tense reports) isn't touched. A redundancy pass against all 30 pre-existing bullets found none fully subsumed by R32-R34; the two boundary notes above (R32→R5, R34→R21) were the actionable output instead of a removal. An early R34 draft also leaked a venue-specific drink name and a venue-specific ingredient verbatim from the motivating case; the first no-venue-names pass had only checked for em/en dashes, not actual names, so a lowercase, uncapitalized brand name survived a "verified clean" claim. Fixed by genericizing the example and adding a real name-blocklist check before landing. **TAC-495 (v1.54.0): R1, R5 and R32 have Instagram variants**, made by phrase substitution on the unedited template; see "Channel copy" below. The Voices rail names the Instagram wording on exactly those three rules, and a test holds it there. **R35 (v1.59.0, TAC-484) is displayed, appended after R34, and is the first universal rule about the agent's own prior message rather than about the guest's.** When a guest questions or pushes back on something the agent said, say plainly what is actually true. It has TWO branches and the second one is the point: if the earlier message was wrong, say so and stop; if it was RIGHT, restate the fact plainly without defending or elaborating. A rule that assumed the challenge was always correct would teach the model to apologise for true facts and withdraw them, which the 2026-09-21 ruling rejected explicitly after the plan proposed the one-branch version. Both branches share the prohibitions, and those are the incident verbatim: never invent a reason for what was said (turns 2 and 3 each supplied one), and never tell the guest to disregard it, ignore you, or that everything is fine (turn 4 said "ignore me, we're good"). Scoped in its own prose to the agent's OWN prior message, which is what separates it from R1, the same technique R23 uses against R15. Every prompt-content assertion for it pins a contiguous clause rather than separate fragments, because a mutant that swaps the two branches survives disjoint `toContain` calls. **It also carries a boundary against the CATEGORY layer** (ruled 2026-09-22, after code review found the rule could be outranked on exactly the turns it targets): a category's register guidance, whether it frames the turn as a close or as a holding response, is never authority over whether the record gets corrected, and the rest of the message then follows that category's guidance. Category instructions render LAST, and two of them plausibly select a challenge turn: `unknown` ("a warm holding response... will be followed up on") and `acknowledgment` ("a close, not an opening... do not turn the closer into a fresh exchange", which is what "ignore me, we're good" is). **`unknown` is reachable by construction**, since TAC-240 reroutes anything below 0.3 classifier confidence there and "you're confusing me" is that shape. Every sibling rule in this series already carried such a boundary (R23 to R15, R30 to the `unknown` holding response, R32 to R5, R33 to R26, R34 to R21); R35 shipped without one for a day. `compose-prompt.test.ts` composes the real prompt for both categories and pins that R35, the clause and the prohibitions all render, and that the category block really does come after R35 — **it cannot show the model OBEYS R35 over the category block, and says so; that is the QA: Device half**. **R36 (v1.61.0, TAC-520) is displayed, appended after R35, and it SHIPPED NARROWER THAN IT WAS WRITTEN because the wide version was measured and made things worse.** The rule as it ships has exactly two clauses: don't name the year unless leaving it out would genuinely be ambiguous, and when the venue's notes give a month with no actual day, say the date is not set rather than naming the month as if it were the plan. It comes from a live Le Mil's draft, held for approval so no guest read it, that answered "did masala mixer start" with "planned for September 2026" about something days away, copied verbatim out of a `currentContext` entry. **The audit is what chose a rule over a serializer**: every date the code formats ITSELF is already person-shaped (`formatTimeDelta` gives "yesterday" and "3 days ago", and `## Visit history`, `## Recent conversation` and `## Active commitments` all use it; a commitment's `expires_at` is not rendered at all), while every absolute date that can reach a guest is venue FREE TEXT passed through verbatim, at **AT LEAST EIGHT** sites — `currentContext` (the incident, and the only block with no framing sentence at all), `hours` and `hours.notes`, knowledge chunks, `menu.notes`/`highlights`, `eventBeingInvited.date` (under a literal `Date:` label), `perkBeingUnlocked.rewardDescription`, the operator instruction (already governed by R14), and `life_context` notes, whose `expires_at` is filtered on but never printed, so "in Tokyo until the 30th" arrives with no anchor. That enumeration is a floor, not a census: `formatMechanicEligibility`'s `rewardDescription` renders for every eligible mechanic on most turns, and the two most on-point omissions are the **voice corpus exemplars** (`ragChunksToProse`) and the **recent-conversation bodies** — the incident reply itself re-renders verbatim on the guest's next turn, which is the echo path this defect lives on. A serializer fix is eight-plus edits and a standing obligation to remember the next one, and it still cannot do the work. **The load-bearing clause is the one saying that restating a documented date invents nothing**, and it exists because R8 (never invent) names `current_context` as a source of truth: the observed failure was FAITHFUL REPETITION, not invention, so without that clause R8 is what the model obeys when it repeats the date verbatim. R14's "the operator's wording is intent, not output" is the precedent. **What was cut, and why it matters more than what shipped:** the first version also prescribed the FORM — "today"/"tomorrow" one day out, the weekday inside the coming week, "later this month" beyond that, and an instruction to work out where a stored date falls against today. Measured at 5 generations per arm per case against Le Mil's live config, that half FAILED: on an event dated three days out the model prefixed a weekday to the date and **got the weekday wrong 3 times out of 3** ("This Thursday, September 25th"; 2026-09-25 was a Friday), and **the grounding backstop held none of them**, so all three would have auto-sent a guest the wrong day — strictly worse than the robotic but correct reply they replaced. On the incident turn the year did drop 4/5 → 1/5, but two replacements were false ("sometime next fall", "sometime next month", when the note said September and it WAS September) and the backstop held 4 of 5, **the one it let through being the only correct reply**. **THE PRIMARY PRE-REGISTERED METRIC IS NULL, AND THE RULE SHIPPED ANYWAY — read that before reading anything else here.** Against the incident note as the ticket actually quotes it, year stated came out **20/20 with the narrowed rule against 18/20 without it (Fisher two-tailed p = 0.487)**, and the not-set clause fired once in twenty against zero. **On its own evidence this rule is close to inert on the turn it was written for**, and saying so plainly is the point of this paragraph. An earlier figure of 17/20 against 12/20 (p = 0.155) is SUPERSEDED and must not be quoted: it was measured against a fixture that appended "Exact date not confirmed yet." to the stored note, a sentence not in the real entry, which let BOTH arms reach "the date isn't set" by plain restatement and measured the not-set clause on a case that did not need it (caught in code review). It shipped on a decision (2026-09-22) that the deliverable is the canaries plus the REMOVAL of the wrong-weekday clause, both of which stand on their own evidence, and that a rule costing nothing measurable is worth keeping as the place the working version will go. **TAC-522 is where the fix actually lives**: the model cannot place a date it cannot look up, and until `## Right now` carries a calendar, no wording of this rule has been shown to move the incident turn. Every other number in this entry is a supporting detail; this is the headline, and an entry that buried it would read as measurement-supported when it is not. **A second finding transfers past this ticket: n=5 IS FAR TOO SMALL FOR A GENERATION ARM.** Two runs of byte-identical code produced 4/5 and 1/5 on this same metric, so the control arm alone reproduced the entire spread of the effect being looked for, and an earlier report of "the wide rule improved the year 4/5 → 1/5" was reading noise as signal. Generation runs at temperature 0.7; the TAC-409 single-verdict lesson applies at least as hard here as it does to a verifier. The diagnosis is that placing a stored date against today is ARITHMETIC and a prompt rule cannot make a model count days — it was off by one. So only the two clauses needing no arithmetic remain; the year clause still consults `## Right now`, but only to judge whether something is a year or more out, a coarse comparison that measured clean 5/5 on both arms. **TAC-522 is the other half and must land first**: give `## Right now` a calendar so a weekday is a LOOKUP rather than a calculation, then restore the cut clauses and re-measure. `system-template.test.ts` carries CANARIES on both deleted clauses (and on "today"/"tomorrow", cut for the same reason — an off-by-one is exactly what makes a model say "today" about tomorrow), so they cannot slip back without deliberately deleting a test that says why not. **The year stays PERMITTED, not banned** — an event dated 2027 was answered "July 19, 2027" correctly on both arms, and AC3 needs it. Clock time was considered and left out: no instance of the agent saying "19:00" has been observed, R2 already models "10pm tonight", and an unmeasured clause attached to a measured change muddies the result. **TAC-522 (v1.63.0) gave `## Right now` a CALENDAR and restored R36's cut clauses against it.** `- Calendar: Tue Sep 22 (today), Wed Sep 23, …` renders the next 10 days as weekday/month-day pairs, always, for a measured **+60 input tokens (0.44%)** of a real Le Mil's prompt. Month-day words rather than ISO because the calendar exists to remove a conversion step and operators write "September 25, 2026" in their notes. **The restored clauses are NOT the old text**: "work out where that falls against today" is gone and the floor "Never work a weekday out for yourself" stands in its place, with "say the date the way the notes wrote it" as the out-of-window branch, because a prohibition with no alternative is how R33 would have lost to the venue's own content. **Measured, n=20 per arm: correct weekday 0/20 → 20/20, numeric dates 19/20 → 0/20, holds 4 → 0**, and the weekday REPLACES the date ("This Friday at 7pm") rather than prefixing it. **Three things this cost, all worth knowing.** (1) **A DST bug in the calendar itself, and the comment asserted a safety the code did not have, in the function that cited the existing DST lesson** — the first `computeCalendar` added 24h to the instant and formatted in the venue's zone, which SKIPS A DAY across spring-forward: at 23:30 the evening before, Los Angeles gave "Sat Mar 13, Mon Mar 15, …" with Sunday the 14th absent. It now resolves the venue-local date once and does pure `Date.UTC` calendar arithmetic formatted in UTC; the skipped day is a named regression test. Same family as `venueLocalInstant`'s two-pass bug. (2) **The calendar landed with 5701 tests green and nothing asserting it**, because every `## Right now` assertion was a substring or an ordering and `computeToday` had no tests at all — a whole new line entered the block and nothing failed. The block is now pinned WHOLE, and it caught a wrong expectation on its first run. Substring assertions answer "is this fact present"; only an exact block answers "is this block what we think it is". (3) **The calendar creates one failure of its own: it is a source of plausible dates to reach for.** Against a note dated months back, one reply came back "should be in by Sunday the 27th", a date lifted straight out of the window. R36 gained "do not take a different date from the calendar in its place" — **and that closed the hole while the model went around it**, inventing "next year" (4 of 20) and "next month" (2 of 20) instead, neither of which is in the calendar. A narrow prohibition moved the fabrication rather than stopping it; that is TAC-525, and it is the transferable lesson. **The calendar solves LOOKUP and does nothing for STALENESS**, which is a comparison between two dates where the window holds only one, so widening the window backwards is not the fix either.
- **Channel copy (TAC-495, v1.54.0).** An Instagram conversation gets its own wording wherever the prompt made a claim about the channel; the SMS copy is untouched. **Branch by channel, never converge (ruled 2026-09-19):** the SMS copy is correct for a guest who texted a phone number, and the mock venues and any future venue on a number need it to keep saying "number" and "texting". Neutralising both into something true but vaguer was rejected. What varies, and nothing else:
  - **R1:** the base rule's "an inbound text" becomes "an inbound message"; the exception's rationale "they know which number they just texted and why" becomes "they know who they just messaged and why". Swapped, never cut: it is the only concrete content after the colon.
  - **R5:** "email, call, DM Instagram, or" becomes "email, call, text, or". Each side names the OTHER channel.
  - **R32**, on every turn: "They are already texting you" becomes "messaging"; "inviting them to save this number or text again" becomes "inviting them to message again".
  - **The first-visit opener:** "first message on this number" loses "on this number", and "who they're texting" becomes "who they're messaging".
  - **The system prompt's opening line**, which frames the whole conversation: "You communicate with its guests via iMessage" becomes "through Instagram messages". It names the platform, not its vocabulary: left unnamed, the model falls back on its default picture of a café messaging a guest, which is texting, and R5's Instagram list only reads right if the model knows where it is. The cost, that naming it may invite Instagram idioms ("DM us", "check our stories"), is what TAC-469's behavioural check looks for.
  - **The register line** "Sound like whichever of those would actually text" becomes "would actually message": it put texting in the frame one line from the opening.
  - **The plain-text rule** "Plain text suitable for iMessage." becomes just "Plain text.": the constraint is the same on both channels (neither renders markdown), and the opening line already says where the guest is.
  - **The heads-up examples in `# Commitments`:** "text me when you're close" becomes "message me", and "text me a heads-up" becomes "send me a heads-up". The em dash that used to sit in that second example, on both channels, is TAC-498's fix (v1.65.0) — replaced with a period, R3's own pattern; the substituted substring is untouched.
  - **The named-speaker persona line** (`serializers.ts`, `speakerFramingProse`): "texting as yourself" becomes "messaging as yourself"; TAC-338's "as yourself" framing is kept. `personaToProse` takes the channel as a required argument: `composePrompt` passes the conversation's, and the classifier passes `'text'`, because its prompt is not guest-facing and stays as it was (its "inbound text messages" line was left alone for the same reason).
  - **The `unknown` category's close** (`categories/index.ts`, `categoryInstructionsFor`): "a real busy person texting back" becomes "messaging back". It renders on every `unknown` turn, including every classifier reroute below 0.3 confidence. It's the one category with a channel variant.
  - **The casual formality line** (`FORMALITY_GUIDANCE.casual` in `serializers.ts`, through `personaToProse`): "write the way you would text a friend" becomes "message a friend". **This swap costs something:** the phrase is a register yardstick as much as a channel claim, and "texting a friend" is the sharper anchor for how casual to be. It was taken because the bigger risk is the model echoing "text" to a guest who isn't texting. **If TAC-469's behavioural check shows the Instagram voice reading more formal than Sendblue's, this line is the first place to look.**
  - **Left alone, deliberately:** R3's rationale "Em dashes read as AI writing in casual texts" (it explains a rule; it doesn't instruct), and every "text" that means a message body ("plain text", "reply text").
  - **Not the first-touch signal line** ("This is the guest's first message, sent after they scanned your venue's QR sign."): it claims no number and no texting, so it is one line on both channels.

  The Instagram copy says "message", never "DM": it has to stop asserting a phone number, not adopt Instagram's vocabulary. **Presence language is shared by ruling** (scanned, at pickup, already ordered, in hand, coming in, what they got): the shared-link false positive it would guard against is hypothetical while the counter QR is the only ig.me link. Revisit when Phase 2's per-placement refs can tell a counter QR from a shared link.

  **Mechanism** (`lib/ai/prompts/channel-variants.ts`). The SMS text is written out in full where it always lived (`SYSTEM_TEMPLATE`, `FIRST_TOUCH_OPENER` in `serializers.ts`) and takes no substitutions, so it is byte-identical by construction. The Instagram variant is that text with a per-channel table of phrase swaps (`satisfies Record<MessageChannel, …>`), and each `from` must occur exactly once or the module **throws at load**. That is deliberate and safe: the inputs are string constants, identical in CI and production, so a miss fails every test file that imports the module and cannot ship, and editing an SMS phrase that has an Instagram twin breaks at the exact phrase instead of letting the channels drift. `systemTemplateFor(channel)`, `categoryInstructionsFor(category, channel)`, `firstTouchOpenerFor(channel)` and the tables behind the named-speaker and casual formality lines read the variants. Every generation prompt reaches them through `composePrompt`, which passes the channel to `systemTemplateFor`, to `categoryInstructionsFor`, to `personaToProse` (the named-speaker and formality lines) and to `runtimeToProse` (the opener, via `formatOpenIntentions`). The one other caller is the classifier, which passes `'text'` to `personaToProse` because its prompt is not guest-facing. `runtimeToProse`'s new `channel` parameter defaults to null only because composePrompt is its sole production caller and importer, which a test pins. **TAC-423 is reopened and will rewrite the opener**: whichever lands second fails loudly, not silently. Rewording or removing a substituted phrase breaks the import at that phrase; a rewrite that keeps the phrases fails the transcribed-literal tests instead.

  **Where the channel comes from** (`lib/agent/conversation-channel.ts`, `resolveConversationChannel`): the conversation, never a venue setting. A config field can say anything; the guest row (a phone number, an Instagram-scoped ID, or both) and the inbound message's `messages.channel` can only say what happened. With an inbound message, the message decides, provided the guest has the identifier that channel needs; a text from a guest with no phone number is migration 048's `'text'`-default signature, so it resolves to **null (unknown)**, as does its mirror image. With no inbound message (followups, holding message, decline), a phone number decides, **including for a guest with both identifiers**, because every such send goes to a phone number today; TAC-469 must revisit that when it routes proactive sends. Neither identifier cannot happen (`guests_must_have_identity`) and also resolves to null. **Null gets the Instagram copy**, because that copy is false on neither channel (a text is also a message); it is a property of the copy, not a claim the guest is on Instagram, so `RuntimeContext.conversationChannel` is for choosing prompt copy only and nothing may route a send on it. `GenerateMessageInput.channel` is a required key, and `generateMessage` rejects anything that is not a channel or null as `invalid_input`, so a cast-smuggled undefined never quietly becomes the SMS copy. **`buildRuntimeContext` requires the venue's `messaging_phone_number` only when the channel isn't Instagram** (`venueMessagingNumberRequired`, ruled 2026-09-19): Le Mil's number is to be deleted once Instagram works, making it the first Instagram-only venue, and before this every Instagram guest there would have failed at context build with an error naming the number rather than the deletion. Nothing reads `VenueContext.sendblueNumber` (now `string | null`), so this changes no send path; every Sendblue send still looks the number up in `lib/messaging/venue-lookup.ts` and fails closed, which is TAC-469's to route around. An unknown channel still requires it. It lives here rather than in TAC-469 because it is a context-build precondition, not routing, and it needs the channel this ticket resolves at that point in the function.

  **The scope guard is the brake.** Once the composer can vary by channel, every line in the prompt is a candidate. `system-template.test.ts` pins the set of template lines allowed to differ, `categories/index.test.ts` that only `unknown` differs, `serializers.test.ts` the opener's phrases and the persona's two phrases, and `compose-prompt.test.ts` that swapping the Instagram strings back yields the SMS prompts exactly. Widening any of them is a deliberate change in its own ticket.

  **R1's exception and the signal line are coupled by prose only.** R1 applies "when the context says this is the guest's first message after they scanned a sign at the venue"; the signal line (and, where it renders, the opener's first sentence) is what says so. Nothing structural links them: the model matches them. The trigger clause and the signal line are identical on both channels, and `compose-prompt.test.ts` holds the pair together per channel. On opt_out, comp_complaint and empty-intention turns the signal line is the ONLY trigger, so rewording it alone would silently switch R1's exception off there.

  **Not covered here:**
  - On Instagram, "first message" means first in our database, and a returning guest's DM history from before the integration is invisible (TAC-497, on TAC-469's pre-flight list).
  - The test harness has no Instagram synthetic guests. Its synthetic guests all have phone numbers, so every scenario resolves to `text`; once Le Mil's number is deleted, every scenario there will throw at context build for want of it (on TAC-469's pre-flight list).
  - Prompts that are not guest-facing keep their SMS wording: the classifier's "inbound text messages" line and its persona section, `extract-reported-order.ts`'s "a text message a guest sent", and `classify-intention-prompts.ts`'s "a text message a cafe … sent".
  - **An unresolved channel only logs a `console.warn`.** That's fine while the agent gate is shut. Once TAC-469 lifts it, a null resolution means a real guest gets copy chosen without knowing their channel, and a log line nobody watches doesn't surface that. A real signal is on TAC-469's pre-flight list, not built here (ruled 2026-09-19).
  - `compose-prompt.test.ts` scans every category, formality and framing, and no line in any Instagram prompt may match its channel-claim patterns (iMessage, SMS, phone, "this number", texting, texted, texts, "a text", "text me/us/them/back/a friend", "would text"). R3's rationale phrase is the one ruled exemption. The scan is only as good as that pattern: a claim worded some other way passes it.
- **Identity framing (Core principles, TAC-338, v1.39.0):** `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE`'s opening line and the fourth `# Core principles` bullet establish that the agent works at the venue — never phrased as representing it "on the venue's behalf." That phrasing is now a banned framing repo-wide for this identity fact (grep before reintroducing it in prompt text describing who is speaking); it read as third-party, agent-for-hire framing and was the root cause of a voice defect where the agent referred to venue staff as "them" and to itself in the third person ("tell them Sana said..."). Two legitimate `speakerFraming: 'named_person'` deployments exist — a real staff member replying as themselves, and a persona standing in for a real role that isn't a specific individual (a maître d', for instance) — and neither `BrandPersonaSchema` nor the prompt distinguishes them with a dedicated field; the identity text is written to hold for either. `voiceName` (`BrandPersonaSchema`, Command-Center display label) is confirmed NEVER rendered into the prompt — the name the model actually knows itself by is `speakerName`, rendered in `speakerFramingProse`'s `named_person` branch (`lib/ai/prompts/serializers.ts`). Deliberately no symptom-level ban (no "never refer to yourself in third person," no "them" prohibition) — plan review rejected that as the same technique that hit its ceiling with R21 (TAC-334: naming "good pick" / "the right call" didn't stop "good call"), and a "them" ban would misfire on ordinary correct staff speech ("Kinani will have it ready, ask him at the counter"). Fix the misstatement, verify via UAT, add a prohibition later only with evidence a symptom survives. **TAC-348 (v1.42.0) removes the same branch's signing instruction.** `named_person` previously told the model "Sign messages as {speakerName}." — real iMessage/SMS threads don't carry signatures, and at least one venue needed a manual anti-pattern rule to undo it. Removed outright, not reworded; the sentence had no other job. The rest of the branch (staff-identity framing, the "not an outside service" line) is unchanged.
- **Mechanic eligibility (THE-170):** mechanics with `min_state` set are filtered out of `RuntimeContext.mechanics` when the guest's recognition state is below the gate. Mechanics with active redemptions are also filtered (`one_time` policy blocks forever after any `mechanic_redeemed` event; `renewable` blocks within `redemption_window_days`). Helpers: `isStateAtLeast` and `filterEligibleMechanics` in `lib/recognition/`. The filter runs at load time in `build-runtime-context.ts` after `recognition.state` is computed, sharing `computedAt` so the filter timestamp matches the recognition snapshot. Empty list is meaningful — the serializer renders an explicit "do not offer perks of any kind" instruction when `mechanics: []`. Empty-list framing is load-bearing for closing the eligibility-leak failure case where Sonnet would otherwise improvise mechanic offers from voice corpus matches.
- **Voice vs knowledge retrieval:** the agent retrieves from two corpora. `voice_corpus` (always-on, fail-closed) supplies HOW the venue speaks — style exemplars rendered as `## Examples of how the venue actually communicates`. `knowledge_corpus` (gated by `shouldRetrieveKnowledge`, fail-graceful) supplies WHAT IS TRUE about the venue — narrative content (sourcing stories, staff personalities, mechanic explanations, philosophy) rendered as `## Venue knowledge` with `[primary: ...]` and `[secondary: ...]` lines per chunk. Knowledge fires for every inbound and for followup triggers `event` / `manual`; skips `day_*` cron triggers. Failure asymmetry is intentional — voice failure breaks voice fidelity (the whole point of the message), knowledge failure just means a less specific reply, still in the venue's voice.
