PostHog: `captureGroundingVerifierUnavailable`, ONE event with an `outcome: 'truncated' | 'degraded'` discriminator, an explicit `failedClosed` boolean and (TAC-424) a `retried` boolean, **Slack-relaying BOTH**. `failedClosed` is `true` on both outcomes now, so `failedClosed=false` selects exactly the rows written before TAC-424 — the turns that shipped with no grounding verdict. It stays as its own field rather than being dropped, so that query keeps working and so a third outcome has to STATE its consequence rather than have it inferred. Its Slack headline read "reply proceeded ungated" on the degraded branch, which stopped being true the moment that outcome started queueing; corrected under SR-2 in the same change. Known cost: a sustained provider outage relays once per inbound; the lever if that proves unworkable is a PostHog-side filter on `outcome`, not deleting the emit.

12b. `grounding_check_degraded` (TAC-424) — **not a reason to hold, a record of WHICH of trigger 12's two causes fired.** Rulings 1 C and 2 B together forced this shape: degraded, truncated and clean must be three-way distinguishable by SQL alone, with no migration on `messages` and without touching `ungrounded_claims`. `messages.review_triggers` is the only existing per-message field that can carry it — `response_review` cannot take agent output at all (`MessageReviewSchema` requires a `reviewedBy` uuid, and migration 039's own header already rejected that column for the neighbouring case), and `pending_commitment` / `rendered_intentions` are narrow carriers for other mechanisms. So this code rides ALONGSIDE `grounding_check_failed` on a degraded turn and **never fires alone**, which is what keeps the hold and the operator's primary copy exactly as they were. **Ranked directly BELOW its partner in `PRIMARY_TRIGGER_PRIORITY`** so it can never win `review_reason` off a trigger it always co-fires with; the test that pins this co-fires `hold_all_outbound` deliberately, because without a third trigger present it would pass against both "ranked above" and "partner deleted from the priority list" (the `triggers[0]` fallback trap TAC-367 recorded). Its `PUSH_POLICY` entry is `'push'` and **inert by construction** — that map is consulted with the primary trigger only — and says so at the entry rather than leaving the next reader to derive it.

13. `prose_promise_backstop` (TAC-401) — **the primary control for a promise made in PROSE with no structured commitment behind it**, fired from `prosePromiseBackstop.status === 'flagged'` (a new fifth parameter to the gate). Ruled 2026-09-15 (question 1, option c): an independent check becomes the control and **nothing may depend on the v1.23.0 self-flag**, which stays only as a secondary signal. Both controls that were supposed to cover this measured near zero on the same 220 replies at Le Mil's — the model's own `requiresOperatorApproval` fired **0 times** and caught **0 of the 4** genuine uncarried promises, and the comp regex fired 5 times and caught **0 of them** (3 apology idioms, 1 fabricated comp). What held the promises that were held was the grounding check and the mechanic-offer check, neither of them a commitment control and both firing for unrelated reasons. At the time of that measurement grounding was also fail-open on paths this one covers; TAC-424 closed that, which strengthens the backstop behind this check without changing why this check exists. `verifyProsePromiseStage` (`lib/agent/stages.ts`) runs a third independent Haiku call (`lib/ai/verify-prose-promise.ts`) against the drafted body **and nothing else** — not the prompt, not the retrieved knowledge, not the mechanics list. That narrow input is what makes the check replayable against fixed bodies and robust to venue persona rather than tuned to one venue's voice (TAC-415: the same code and prompt produced 27/60 on a synthetic persona reading "quick to make things right" and 4/220 at a venue whose persona says the opposite). Skips (no model call) for a demo guest, when `isCommitmentTypeGated` already applies (the draft carries an obligation carrier, so the card is already right), and on an empty body. **It deliberately does NOT skip on `isModelFlagged`** — that would be depending on the self-flag, and a model-flagged draft still carries no carrier. **Unlike every other backstop in this file it PRODUCES the carrier**: the check names the commitment type and description, which ride the queue decision onto `messages.pending_commitment`, so an operator approving the card creates a real `guest_commitments` row through `createCommitmentFromPending` and the promise enters the lifecycle — expiry, heads-up surfacing, dedup. That is the difference between a caught promise and a tracked one. **An OBLIGATION the check finds REPLACES a recommendation generation carried, and the check never mints a second obligation when generation already carried one** (ruled 2026-09-21, ruling 3 as narrowed the same day). The narrowing is the TAC-380 distinction: a recommendation is an INTENTION, not an obligation — it costs the venue nothing, never gates, and carries no verification code — so it must never be the reason a comp the venue now owes goes untracked. The first version kept the recommendation, which caught the promise and then recorded the wrong thing: an operator approved a card for a comp and the `guest_commitments` row created was a drink suggestion. The half that did NOT move is the obligation case — the model's own structured comp is a better record of what it promised than a second reading of its prose, and the stage skips on `isCommitmentTypeGated` anyway. `resolveDraftCarrier` / `resolveDraftCarrierIdentity` (`lib/agent/pending-slots.ts`) are the single precedence, called by the gate, both persist writes and race recovery, so the three sites cannot drift, and `captureProsePromiseCaught` carries `replacedRecommendation` so that case is countable. A flagged draft's carrier is a comp — including one that displaced a recommendation — so it lands in the OBLIGATION slot and can be dropped by `decideSlotAction` when that slot holds a different commitment, the same treatment a real comp already gets. `blankBody` still nulls it (TAC-309). PostHog: `captureProsePromiseCaught`, Slack-relayed. **The operator app needs both codes added to `analog-operator/lib/review-bucket.ts`'s `BUCKET_BY_CODE`**, which is a hand-kept mirror: until then these cards render the correct sentence (the label ships from this server) but sit on the mid-thread ground with a generic strip, exactly as `unverified_url` does.

14. `prose_promise_check_failed` (TAC-401) — the prose-promise check produced no readable verdict. **FAILS CLOSED, and unlike `grounding_check_failed` that is true of EVERY failure mode, not only truncation.** The reasoning is the one thing to understand before changing it. Grounding USED to fail open on a transient fault because it degrades to a defensible prior, the model's own `knowledgeGap` self-report, which that check is a second opinion on; TAC-424 closed that anyway, so the two now agree. **This check still has no prior to degrade to** — the self-flag caught 0 of 220 and the ruling forbids depending on it — so failing open here would return to nothing at all, which is why this one must never be loosened even if grounding's posture is revisited again. **A transient fault is retried ONCE, immediately** (ruled 2026-09-21, ruling 1), which is what pays for the closed posture on a check this broad: the flood case narrows from "any hiccup" to "a fault that survives two immediate attempts", which is an outage rather than a blip. **Truncation is NOT retried** — retrying a cap that was already hit spends a second call to hit it again, and the fix is the cap. A DISTINCT trigger rather than folding into trigger 13, for the reason TAC-367 split `grounding_check_failed` out: telling an operator a promise was caught on a turn where nothing was caught is the wrong-reason-copy problem TAC-364 exists for, and it makes a sustained outage countable in SQL separately from a wave of real catches. **Carries NO carrier, deliberately** — we do not know what was promised, so nothing is recorded and approving that card creates no commitment; the alternative is inventing a description that would land in `guest_commitments.description` and render as a fact nobody wrote. PostHog: `captureProsePromiseCheckUnavailable`, Slack-relayed. **Known and accepted cost:** this check runs on nearly every generation, so a sustained Haiku outage queues nearly every reply where grounding would degrade quietly in the same outage. Both triggers PUSH (ruling 1), and during an outage that push volume is what makes it legible as an outage while it is happening. **If it bites, the lever is to narrow the population, never to flip to open.**

**One more residual, inherited rather than introduced.** The check still runs when `generation.knowledgeGap === true` (it skips only on demo, an obligation carrier, and an empty body), so a self-reported gap turn that also promises something takes `prose_promise_backstop` as its `review_reason` — and once the holding timer clears `pending_until`, `isKnowledgeGapCard` and `findPendingQuestion` stop recognising that card. This is the same residual `commitment_type_gated` already has (see the `isKnowledgeGapCard` gotcha), now reachable through one more trigger. Closing it needs a column, which is a migration on `messages`. It also spends a Haiku call judging a body that is about to be blanked.

**Measured catch rate (TAC-401, replay 2026-09-21).** 220 labelled synthetic bodies from the 2026-09-15 measurement, 5 repeats each, 1100 calls, via `npm run measure-prose-promise`. **Reported as four cases, not a rate** (ruling 4) — at n=4 an aggregate would read as a precision the measurement does not have:

| body | held | named a carrier | before this check |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A2 #40 "I want to make that right for you" | **5/5** | 5/5 comp | nothing held it; **auto-sent live and fleet** |
| A2 #41 "we'll make it up to you" | 5/5 | 5/5 comp | held only by the mechanic-offer check |
| A2 #35 "I'll make sure your next cortado is right" | **4/5** | 4/5 comp | held only by the grounding check |
| A4 #34 "we still owe you a good cortado" (followup) | 5/5 | 5/5 comp | fleet default **sent** it |

**Both fail-open paths the ruling named are covered by the positives themselves**, not by a separate arm: three are on the eligible-perks path (A2, where the no-comps line does not render) and one is on an engine followup (A4). **False positives, per category, never as one number: 0/20 apology idioms, 0/30 offers-nothing, 0/25 do-better borderline, 0/1005 clean.** The four apology idioms are exactly what the comp regex caught instead of the promises, and this check flags none of them. **0 failed and 0 truncated calls in 1100**, so the 1000-token cap has headroom. A2 #35 at 4/5 is the one non-deterministic case and is why the harness repeats: at temperature 0.2 a single verdict is a draw, not a property of the body.

13. `commitment_cancellation_gated` (TAC-513) — the draft carries a structured cancellation, resolved against this guest's own open + pending_ack list. **ALWAYS queues, whatever else is true**: taking back something a guest was promised is an operator decision, and there is no fidelity score and no venue policy that makes one auto-sendable. The carrier reaches `messages.pending_cancellation` (migration 052) and `dispatchOperatorOutbound`'s step 7b cancels the commitment at the moment the guest is told it is cancelled. **Skip needs no code** — a skipped draft never reaches that path, so "on skip, nothing changes" holds by construction. The ONE path that reaches a send with a cancellation on it is the TAC-284 demo bypass, which overrides every trigger by design; `applyInlineCancellation` in `schedule-and-send.ts` applies it there instead, so a demo guest's ledger still follows their words rather than carving a hole in a bypass CLAUDE.md calls total.

14. `prose_cancellation_backstop` (TAC-513) — the reply TELLS the guest a promise is cancelled and nothing carries it. The 2026-09-21 incident exactly: comp `GWPZ` stayed `open` while the guest was told it was gone. Fires on **two shapes folded into one trigger**, because the operator's decision is identical and the copy is true of both: the independent check (`verify-cancellation-claim.ts`) read a cancellation in the body with no carrier, OR the model emitted an id that did not resolve against this guest's own commitments. The PostHog event (`captureCancellationClaimUnbacked`) carries the unresolved id and the open-commitment count, which is where the two are told apart — "the model invented a cancellation" and "the block was empty and it invented one anyway" have different fixes. **NEVER carries a carrier and never mints one**, the one place in the gate where a flagged check does not: see the asymmetry above.

15. `prose_cancellation_check_failed` (TAC-513) — the cancellation-claim check produced no readable verdict. **Fails CLOSED on every failure mode**, like `prose_promise_check_failed` and for the same reason: there is no prior to degrade to. A DISTINCT trigger per TAC-367 and TAC-364 — telling an operator a cancellation was caught on a turn where nothing was caught is the wrong-reason-copy problem.

16. `unresolved_cancellation_id` (TAC-513, split out of trigger 14 on the 2026-09-22 ruling) — the model emitted a commitment id that resolves to NOTHING for this guest, while the body does not read as claiming a cancellation. **The hold is the same one trigger 14 always applied; only the sentence the operator reads is new.** It shipped folded into `prose_cancellation_backstop`, and the fold was wrong in the one way that matters on a card: that trigger's copy says *"This tells the guest a promise is cancelled"*, which is simply FALSE of a reply whose text says nothing of the kind, and sends the operator hunting for a sentence that is not in the draft. Same wrong-reason-copy problem TAC-364 exists for, and the same one `prose_cancellation_check_failed` was kept separate to avoid. Copy: **"This reply points at a promise that doesn't exist. Check it before sending."** **Mutually exclusive with trigger 14 BY CONSTRUCTION** — the condition is `claim !== 'flagged' && resolution.status === 'unresolved'`, so when both shapes are true at once (the incident's own shape: the body claims it AND the id is unresolved) exactly trigger 14 fires and the stronger sentence wins. Two tests pin each direction with `not.toContain`, because "both shapes queue" is true under every arrangement of the two conditions and proves nothing about which card the operator gets; a mutant swapping the two pushes kills six tests. **It DOES co-fire with trigger 15** (an unreadable check does not make an unresolved id any less unresolved) and ranks above it, per the same rule `grounding_check_failed` follows: a finding about this draft beats an absence of one. Pushes. Carries no carrier, like trigger 14.

17. `closed_venue_arrival_emitted` (TAC-363) — **the venue is CLOSED and the generation emitted an `imminent` arrival.** Deterministic and structural: it reads the emission and the venue's own hours, and no model judgement enters. That independence is the entire point. TAC-301 part 1 put a `- Status: CLOSED` line in the user prompt, as proximate to generation as a prompt instruction can be, and on 2026-09-14 the model read it and replied "See you soon" to a guest six hours after close; on 2026-09-21 the prose held and **arrival capture moved the comp anyway**. The relationship this has to that status line is the one `comp_regex_backstop` has to `model_flagged`. **Scoped to `imminent` (ruled 2026-09-22), narrowing the ticket's literal `closed && (commitment || arrivalCapture)` proposal.** A `scheduled` capture while closed is a guest at 11pm arranging 8am tomorrow, which is correct behaviour and the most common out-of-hours arrival conversation; holding it would be noise protecting nobody, since nobody sets off on it. The `commitment` half was dropped for a different reason: comp, hold and discount already queue on every turn via `commitment_type_gated` regardless of hours, so its only net-new coverage was a `recommendation`, which ruling 4(a) has just removed from the arrival path entirely. **`unknown` hours do NOT fire it** — the condition is `isVenueClosed`, true only for a positive closed verdict, which is ruling 2(a) reached through the type rather than through each caller remembering. Uses the same `now` as the recognition snapshot, so the gate and the arrival dispatch cannot disagree about the clock inside one turn. PostHog: `captureClosedVenueArrivalCaught` with `source: 'structured'`, Slack-relayed.

18. `closed_venue_arrival_backstop` (TAC-363) — **independent text check for the same failure, covering the shape trigger 17 cannot see.** A reply that reads as a same-moment confirmation while emitting NO structured field — "see you soon" with nothing attached — passes every other trigger by construction and auto-sends, and the 2026-09-15 ruling added a text check for exactly that gap. `verifyClosedVenueArrivalStage` runs a fifth independent Haiku call (`lib/ai/verify-closed-venue-arrival.ts`) on the drafted body **and nothing else**, the same narrow input discipline TAC-415 paid for. **It is NOT TAC-401's check**: `verify-prose-promise` is scoped to value transfer and its own do-not-flag list names "something the guest has already paid for or already ordered", so "see you soon" transfers nothing and would not flag there. Skips with no model call when the venue is not positively closed (so it costs nothing during service, which is most traffic), when trigger 17 already fired, on a demo guest, and on an empty body. **FAILS CLOSED on every failure mode**, with one immediate retry on a transient fault and none on truncation. **`flagged` and `check_failed` ride ONE trigger**, following `mechanic_offer_backstop` rather than the grounding and prose splits: those exist so an operator is never told "a claim was caught" on a turn where nothing was caught, and here the operator's decision is identical either way, which is the test that precedent turns on. Runs on followups too. PostHog: same event with `source: 'text_backstop'` — the discriminator is what keeps the two halves countable apart, and if the backstop ever dominates, trigger 17's condition is missing the real shape of the failure.

`primaryTrigger` is **not** `triggers[0]`. It's picked via `PRIMARY_TRIGGER_PRIORITY` (severity-of-signal order): `commitment_type_gated` > `commitment_cancellation_gated` > `mechanic_offer_backstop` > `prose_promise_backstop` > `prose_cancellation_backstop` > `unresolved_cancellation_id` > `knowledge_gap_backstop` > `knowledge_gap` > `comp_regex_backstop` > `model_flagged` > `closed_venue_arrival_emitted` > `closed_venue_arrival_backstop` > `unverified_url` > `self_talk_detected` > `complaint_commitment_floor` > `previous_pending_held` > `fidelity_below_auto_send_floor` > `grounding_check_failed` > `grounding_check_degraded` > `prose_promise_check_failed` > `prose_cancellation_check_failed` > `category_requires_approval` > `hold_all_outbound`. (This list read seventeen entries and omitted `unverified_url` and `grounding_check_degraded` until TAC-363 reconciled it against the array; check it against `PRIMARY_TRIGGER_PRIORITY`, not against this sentence.) **The two closed-venue triggers rank below every money and fabrication signal and above the two deterministic text backstops** — no money and no invented fact is at stake, but both they and `unverified_url` are "the guest acts on this" failures, and a wasted trip to a locked door costs the guest more than a dead link. Structural above model judgement mirrors `commitment_type_gated` above `prose_promise_backstop`; the two are mutually exclusive by construction (the backstop skips when the structural condition fired), so that half is documentation rather than a live tie-break. **`grounding_check_failed` ranks below every trigger that names something about this draft** — it is the only trigger reporting an ABSENCE of signal, so any concrete co-firing finding is the more useful operator label — and above the two venue-wide policy signals, because it is at least specific to this message. **`knowledge_gap_backstop` ranks just above `knowledge_gap`**, mirroring `comp_regex_backstop`'s rank above `model_flagged` — a caught claim is a more specific operator label than an honest self-report. Since the two never co-fire on the same turn, this ordering is documentation today rather than a live tie-break. **`category_requires_approval` ranks second-to-last** because it is a policy signal, not a claim about this draft — every trigger above names a concrete risk in the specific message and carries a more useful operator label. It sits BELOW `previous_pending_held` so a regenerated complaint turn doesn't re-push at an operator already holding the card. `primaryTrigger` lands on `messages.review_reason` (the field the operator queue UI surfaces first), so the most-severe signal is what gets shown. **Commitment_type_gated tops the priority** because it carries explicit type information (the operator queue UI sees "hold" / "comp" / "discount" directly rather than just "regex matched some comp prose"). **`mechanic_offer_backstop` ranks directly below it, at parity rather than beneath the other backstops** — TAC-355's audit found it's the PRIMARY defense for the mechanic-grant failure mode, not a secondary layer, so an unauthorized-perk signal carries the same operator-facing priority as an unauthorized comp/hold/discount. **`commitment_cancellation_gated` ranks SECOND, directly below the offer, and that ordering is a judgement rather than a derivation** — on a reply that both offers and cancels, the operator should read the label about money going OUT first, because an unnoticed new comp costs the venue where an unnoticed cancellation costs a card they were going to read anyway. **`hold_all_outbound` is ranked last** because it's a venue-wide policy rather than a per-message signal — any concrete co-firing trigger carries more operator-actionable information. **`knowledge_gap` ranks below the two structural/backstop triggers above it, deliberately not first.** TAC-308 originally asked for top, but that request was reasoning about the timer — and the timer anchors on `pending_until`, not on `review_reason`, so rank decides only the operator-facing label. It sits below `commitment_type_gated` and `mechanic_offer_backstop` because either losing its label is the worse failure (this repo has bled from an unlabelled comp signal twice) and above everything else because a knowledge-gap card is the only card with a running clock and a guest sitting in silence. **`self_talk_detected` ranks below `model_flagged`, above the softer signals** — a hard, deterministic catch once it fires (the text is confirmed broken), but a voice-quality/product-premise failure rather than a money-or-perk exposure, so it sits below every resource-commitment-class trigger. Confirmed via the operator card (`analog-operator/components/queue/queue-card.tsx`) already rendering the full draft body regardless of which trigger wins the primary label, so this ranking only affects the displayed reason string, never visibility of the actual self-talk text.

**Every trigger except `previous_pending_held` fires an APNs push.** The fire/skip decision is a TOTAL map in `lib/notifications/push-policy.ts` (`satisfies Record<ApprovalTrigger, PushDecision>`) — adding a trigger above without a decision there fails `tsc`. See "Common gotchas → sets keyed on approval triggers must be TOTAL maps" for why this is load-bearing.

**Manual followups never regenerate over a pending card (TAC-307; enforced end to end by TAC-394).** `previous_pending_held` never fires when `ctx.followupTrigger?.reason === 'manual'`. Since TAC-394 a manual followup that would queue into an occupied slot is REFUSED (`slot_occupied`, the `never_regen` policy), including when only a unique violation reveals the card; before that, the race path regenerated the card anyway. The old bypass was doing two unrelated jobs and only one was meant to go: left in, a Follow Up click on a guest who already has a pending card would fire `previous_pending_held`, route to `persistOrRegenQueuedDraft`'s UPDATE-in-place branch, and overwrite the draft the operator was about to approve — body, `review_reason` and `pending_commitment` replaced, `created_at` preserved so the card looks untouched in the queue. That is data loss on a human's work and a different axis from "does approval policy apply". Caught in code review.

**Follow Up button bypass — REMOVED (TAC-307).** `handle-followup.ts` used to skip `applyApprovalPolicyStage` entirely when `input.trigger.reason === 'manual'`, on the reasoning that the operator had already approved by clicking. **It now runs the gate on every followup path.** Clicking Follow Up authorises THE ACT OF REACHING OUT, not the text — the body is model-generated and nobody reads it before it ships — so the old bypass let a button click auto-send past a hold a venue had deliberately switched on. Consequence to know before debugging it: at a venue with an approval hold configured, the Follow Up button now produces a QUEUED CARD rather than a sent message. That is the intended meaning of the switch. Manual followups still bypass Gate 1 (`canSendFollowup` lives in the engine, not the orchestrator) and still don't write `followup_log` rows or count toward `weekly_cap`. `skipHumanFeelDelay` still keys on `reason === 'manual'` — that heuristic is untouched.

**Generation schema fields:** `GeneratedMessageSchema` (`lib/ai/generate-message.ts`) rigidly requires `requiresOperatorApproval: boolean` and `approvalReason: string` — no `.optional()` because the Anthropic structured-output validator is more reliable with explicit presence. `approvalReason` defaults to `""` when `requiresOperatorApproval=false`. Both are threaded onto `GenerateMessageAttempt` and `GenerateMessageResult` for trace observability.

**Per-mechanic flag (`mechanics.requires_operator_approval`):** added in migration 019, defaults `false`. The eligible-mechanics serializer (`formatMechanicEligibility` in `lib/ai/prompts/serializers.ts`) annotates flagged mechanic bullets with `[operator approval required: …]` so the model knows committing this mechanic should set `requiresOperatorApproval=true`. Loaded by `build-runtime-context.ts` through `EligibilityCandidate` → `EligibleMechanic`. SQL UPDATE template for toggling per-venue is in Common gotchas.

**PostHog events:** `captureDraftQueued` (`lib/analytics/posthog.ts`) fires whenever the gate queues a NEW pending draft (INSERT path), with `triggers` + `primaryTrigger` + `voiceFidelity` + `modelRequiresApproval` + `modelApprovalReason` + `compRegexMatchedPattern` + `hasPreviousPending` + `kind` ('inbound' | 'followup') + `category` + bodies. `captureDraftRegenerated` (TAC-264) fires when the gate queues a REGENERATION of an existing pending row (UPDATE path), with the same shape plus `originalDraftId` (the `messages.id` that was updated in place) and `priorReviewReason` (the row's `review_reason` BEFORE overwrite — captured pre-UPDATE so analytics can surface trigger evolution across regens). Both Slack relay on (pilot ops needs visibility into both paths). Mirrors the `voice_fidelity_low` / `dash_violation_persisted` shape.

**Demo guest bypass (TAC-284).** When `ctx.guest.isDemo === true` (the `guests.is_demo` flag, migration 022), `applyApprovalPolicyStage` still evaluates every trigger (thirteen, see above) — so the would-have-queued set is accurate, except that `knowledge_gap_backstop`, `grounding_check_failed` and `mechanic_offer_backstop` can never appear in it, because `verifyGroundingStage` and `verifyMechanicOfferStage` return `skipped` for a demo guest — then **short-circuits to `{ action: 'send', reason: 'demo_bypass' }` regardless of trigger outcome.** The bypass is total: every trigger, **including the comp regex backstop**, is overridden. The comp backstop is therefore **not a guarantee for demo guests** — a demo guest who is committed a comp gets the comp auto-sent with no operator review. This is intentional (demo guests are teammates' own phones, not real customers); the visibility guarantee is the `demo_bypassed_approval_gate` PostHog event, which fires whenever the would-have-queued trigger set is non-empty and **Slack-relays only when `comp_regex_backstop` is among those triggers** (the irreversible-financial-commitment case). The bypass is **fail-closed**: only the literal boolean `true` bypasses — `undefined` / `null` / a missing column flow through the normal policy. Both orchestrators also pass `skipHumanFeelDelay: ctx.guest.isDemo` to `scheduleAndSend`, and the demo send is stamped `messages.review_reason='demo_bypass'` (the auto-send path otherwise leaves `review_reason` null) so the row is self-describing without a PostHog cross-reference. Manual followups (`reason='manual'`) have run the gate like every other followup since TAC-307, so this short-circuit applies to them too: a demo guest's manual followup sends, and `handle-followup.ts` passes `approval.reason` into `scheduleAndSend`, so that send is stamped `review_reason='demo_bypass'` like any other. Flip a guest's flag via the SQL template in Common gotchas; the flag is read fresh every agent run (no runtime caching).

### Single pending draft per guest invariant (TAC-264, v1.14.0)

**The invariant:** at most one row with `review_state='pending'` per `(venue_id, guest_id)` **per slot** since TAC-394 (see *Two pending slots per guest* below). Enforced at the storage layer by migration 041's two partial unique indexes, which replaced migration 020's single `idx_messages_one_pending_per_guest`; enforced at the application layer by `persistOrRegenQueuedDraft` (`lib/agent/schedule-and-send.ts`) which branches on `existingPendingDraftId` to UPDATE in place vs INSERT.

**Two persist modes via `persistOrRegenQueuedDraft(ctx, generation, primaryTrigger, existingPendingDraftId, options)`** — returns `{ outboundMessageId, action: 'inserted' | 'updated', priorReviewReason }`. Two outcomes write nothing and carry a null `outboundMessageId`: `action: 'dropped'` (TAC-394: race recovery found a card this draft must not overwrite; it carries the drop `reason`, the protected card and both commitments) and `action: 'skipped'` (TAC-308: an `updateOnly` caller whose row is already gone):

1. **INSERT** — `existingPendingDraftId === null` AND the partial unique index doesn't fire. Status quo INSERT via `buildOutboundInsert` with the queue-path overrides. `priorReviewReason` is always `null` on this path.
2. **UPDATE in place (regenerate)** — `existingPendingDraftId !== null`. Conditional UPDATE gated on `id = existingPendingDraftId AND review_state = 'pending'` so a TOCTOU race vs. `dispatchOperatorOutbound` produces rowcount=0 rather than corrupting the operator's just-dispatched body. Captures `priorReviewReason` via a SELECT before the UPDATE so analytics can observe trigger evolution.

**Columns UPDATED on regen** (the "current state of the draft" subset): `body`, `voice_fidelity`, `prompt_version`, `category`, `reply_to_message_id`, `langfuse_trace_id`, `review_reason`. `updated_at` is auto-bumped by `trg_messages_updated_at`.

**Columns PRESERVED on regen** (operator-visible history + queue ordering): `status='pending_review'`, `review_state='pending'` (unchanged — **no demotion to send across regen**), `created_at` (FIFO queue position — operator's "this guest has been waiting since X" mental model), `last_operator_action_at`, `last_operator_id`, `previous_review_state`, `id`, `venue_id`, `guest_id`, `direction`, `generated_by`, `response_review`.

**Race recovery (bounded loop, `RACE_RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`)**:
- INSERT path: a concurrent inbound for the same (venue, guest) wins the unique-index race; the losing INSERT receives `code='23505'`. Recovery re-reads both slots (`loadPendingRowsBySlot`, TAC-394) and runs `decideSlotAction` with the caller's policy: regenerate the card in this draft's own slot on the next loop tick, or return `action: 'dropped'` when that card must not be overwritten. If the racing row vanished between violation and read (operator immediately dispatched), the loop retries INSERT.
- UPDATE path: a TOCTOU race vs. `dispatchOperatorOutbound` clears the pending slot between our slot read and our UPDATE. Either the prior-reason SELECT returns no row OR the conditional UPDATE returns rowcount=0 — either way we drop `existingPendingDraftId` and recurse into a fresh INSERT. A `23505` on the UPDATE itself (moving a row into an occupied slot, which only old code can do, during migration 041's deploy window) is a distinct red alert (`uniqueViolation: true`) and a throw.
- Sustained ping-pong (3 ticks without convergence) fires a red alert (`stage='persist'`) and throws. Caller maps to `AgentResult.failed`.

**No-demotion invariant**: structurally enforced by the `previous_pending_held` trigger inside `applyApprovalPolicyStage`. When the slot read finds a card in this draft's own slot, the trigger fires unconditionally; `triggers.length > 0`; the gate returns `action='queue'`. A high-fidelity untriggered regenerated draft on a guest with an existing pending row still queues — never sends out from under the operator. The fail-open path (`loadPendingRowsBySlot` errors → returns null → trigger doesn't fire → action might be 'send') is the only loophole; migration 041's partial unique indexes close it at the storage layer.

**TAC-308 narrows the no-demotion invariant, and adds `AgentResult.dropped`.** A pending row that is a *knowledge-gap card* is treated differently from every other pending draft, in exactly three ways. (1) If the new turn is independently sendable (no trigger fires at all), it SENDS — `previous_pending_held` no longer forces queue. What TAC-264 actually guards is a regenerated version of THE SAME draft going out from under an operator; a reply to a different question is not that, and the old behavior both silenced the guest AND overwrote the card. The coexistence is permitted because the send writes `review_state='auto_sent'`, outside the pending indexes (migration 020's, and since TAC-394 migration 041's two). (2) If the new turn also gaps, it UPDATEs in place and PRESERVES the original `pending_until`, so a chatty guest can't push the deadline out. (3) If the new turn would queue for any OTHER reason, the gate returns `action:'drop'` and the draft is discarded — not sent, not persisted. The guest is silent on that turn; that is the accepted cost of not losing the operator's question, and `captureDraftDropped` Slack-relays it precisely because it's the one path where a guest says something and receives nothing. **Every other pending row keeps pre-TAC-308 behavior exactly.**

**TAC-394: the regeneration's precondition was never built.** TAC-264's AC is "Regenerated pending draft reflects full conversation context, not just the latest message", and the regen path depends on it: a replacement that answers only the newest message silently drops whatever the pending draft said. Nothing ever told the model the pending draft was unsent, because the history projection rendered it like a sent message. v1.50.0 marks it (see *Recent conversation block* in the runtime contract) and deliberately does not tell the model to carry the draft forward. **Marking it does not stop the overwrite; PR 2's two slots do.** With v1.50.0 alone, a reply to the guest's next question still queues behind `previous_pending_held` and regenerates over a pending comp. Option B (refuse the overwrite, then send beside the card or drop the reply) was measured and would have dropped 29 of 60 replies on the incident's turn shape (see *Recent conversation block*); option F shipped instead, as the two pending slots below. A queued reply is always one unit: the gate judges the whole generated body, and only an auto-sent reply is split into bubbles, after the gate.

**A guest's second message: its own card, nothing, or a rewrite (TAC-397, migration 054).** Supersedes the paragraph below wherever they conflict. The conversation slot is now ONE CARD PER INBOUND, not one per guest; the obligation slot is untouched throughout.

Three cases, decided in the gate by `resolveConversationDisposition` (`lib/agent/pending-slots.ts`) from the classifier's new `correctsPendingReply` plus the category, with `looksLikeQuestion` (TAC-484, reused not rewritten) as a second deterministic condition:

| disposition | what happens |
|---|---|
| `own_card` | a question or request gets its OWN card; the pending one is untouched. Also what happens when nothing is pending. |
| `no_answer` | acknowledgement or chatter: NOTHING is generated into a row, nothing regenerated, nothing sent. The gate returns `{action:'silence'}` and the run is `AgentResult` status `'silenced'`. |
| `correction` | it amends the pending question: that card is regenerated in place and KEEPS the text it replaced, in migration 054's two columns, surfaced as `QueueDraft.replacedDraft`. |

**`no_answer` is UNREACHABLE when nothing is pending**, and that is the safety bound on the whole mechanism: a misjudged disposition can never be why a guest gets no reply at all, only why they get no EXTRA reply while an operator already holds a card for them. Before TAC-397 that same message *overwrote* the card, so even a wrong silence is strictly better than the old behaviour.

**`looksLikeQuestion` is used here in the UNSAFE direction, and the AND is what makes it safe.** TAC-484 uses it where a `false` return costs a nudge; here a `false` return argues for SILENCE, and the function is deliberately precision-biased — its own test pins `looksLikeQuestion('tell me the wifi password') === false`. An imperative request would also have to classify as `acknowledgment` or `casual_chatter` before anything is silenced. Do not drop the category half.

**`'silence'` is its own `ApprovalDecision` and `AgentResult` variant, not a `SlotDropReason`** (ruled 2026-09-22): a drop means a draft competed for a slot and lost, and `captureDraftDropped` Slack-relays on exactly that basis. Nothing competed here, so folding the two together would fire an incident alert on the single most common turn shape there is. **No telemetry on a silenced turn today** — recorded as a candidate if TAC-519 shows the absence of a record is itself the problem; the hook is the `'no_answer'` return.

**Ruling Q3 removed TAC-308's protected-card drop from the `regen` path.** That drop existed only to stop an unrelated turn overwriting a knowledge-gap card; an unrelated turn now opens its own card, so nothing is overwritten and nothing needs protecting. A CORRECTION reaching a gap card still regenerates it — it amends the very question the card is stuck on. `knowledge_gap_card_protected` is NOT dead: it still applies to the obligation slot, where a backstop-flagged card can carry a commitment and a clock at once.

**Ruling Q2: a correction is only ever matched against the most recently opened conversation card**, `mostRecentlyOpenedConversationCard`, the single implementation. The three non-`regen` caller policies (`regen_always`, `regen_gap_card_only`, `never_regen`) read it as "the occupant" and are otherwise unchanged — they have no guest message to judge.

**The read moved to the DESC-window pattern**, and the ordering is load-bearing rather than a preference: `loadPendingRowsBySlot` orders `created_at DESC`, takes `PENDING_ROWS_READ_LIMIT` (25, raised from 3) and reverses in JS. With `ascending: true` a guest over the limit loses their NEWEST cards — precisely the one a correction must match against and the one the gate decides against. That is the TAC-316 truncation bug verbatim. Hitting the limit is REPORTED, not silently truncated.

**A 23505 on the conversation slot now means only one thing**: the SAME inbound already has a card, because the index is keyed on `reply_to_message_id` — a duplicate delivery, never two different messages. Race recovery checks that BEFORE `decideSlotAction` and reports the existing card, **scoped to the `regen` policy** so the decline, the crash card and a manual followup keep their own meanings for an occupied slot. Without that branch the loop retries the INSERT, collides again, exhausts `RACE_RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` and fires a red alert on every duplicated webhook delivery.

**Two other `REVIEW_REASON_LABELS` entries were false in the same way and were corrected here** (the ticket's step-5 audit; both approved verbatim 2026-09-22). `commitment_type_gated` said *"This offers something free"* while firing on `comp`, `hold` AND `discount` — a hold is an item set aside that the guest still pays for and a discount is cheaper, not free — and the card carries no type, so one sentence has to be true of all three: it now says the venue is committed to something. `category_requires_approval` said *"You chose to review these yourself"* while also firing on `source: 'code_default'`, the fleet-wide `comp_complaint` route nobody picked per venue; it now names the KIND of message rather than claiming a choice. A source-aware pair of strings is possible (`policyHoldWasExplicit` already makes the distinction for the demo-bypass event) but needs the source on the wire, which is a Contract change. **`knowledge_gap`'s label is the third of this family and was deliberately LEFT** — *"A guest asked something I don't have an answer for"* can render on a turn where nothing was asked, because the trigger is not gated on `looksLikeQuestion` the way TAC-484 gated the clock; the fix may be the trigger rather than the copy, and guessing wrong adds a third false label.

**Contract (TAC-402 is the client half):** `QueueDraft.replacedDraft: { body, replacedAt } | null`, always present; and `otherPendingDraftsForGuest` **may now exceed 1** — it never had a bound in code, but the note saying the server produces 0 or 1 did.


**Two pending slots per guest (TAC-394 PR 2, option F, migrations 041 and 042).** The invariant above is now ONE PENDING ROW PER SLOT. The obligation slot holds a draft whose structured carrier (`pending_commitment.type`) is `comp`, `hold` or `discount`; the conversation slot holds everything else, including a blank knowledge-gap card (TAC-309 nulls its carrier). A comp promised in prose without a carrier sits in the conversation slot (TAC-401). "Same commitment" means the same type AND the same `commitmentDedupKey` (trim plus lowercase). `decideSlotAction` (`lib/agent/pending-slots.ts`) is the ONE decision table, used by the gate, by `persistOrRegenQueuedDraft`'s 23505 recovery, by the crash card and by the decline, in this order:
  1. The draft's slot is empty: insert.
  2. The obligation slot holds a DIFFERENT commitment: drop, `obligation_slot_taken`, whatever the caller. No path overwrites one obligation with another.
  3. `never_regen` (manual followups): drop, `slot_occupied`. The Command Center route returns 409 with a plain-words detail.
  4. `regen_always` (operator decline): regenerate the card in the draft's own slot.
  5. `regen_gap_card_only` (crash card): regenerate a knowledge-gap card; drop `slot_occupied` over anything else.
  6. `regen` (inbound and engine followups): TAC-308's protected gap card still wins over a non-gap turn (`knowledge_gap_card_protected`); otherwise regenerate.

`previous_pending_held` fires only for a card in the SAME slot, so a reply beside a pending comp card sends when nothing else holds it, or queues as a second card when something does. **The knowledge-gap clock is decided per guest, not per slot:** a gap turn arms `pending_until` only when NEITHER slot already holds a knowledge-gap card (`anyKnowledgeGapCard`), at the gate, on the crash card and in race recovery, because the timeout scan fires once per card and a second clock would send the guest a second holding message. **TAC-484 narrows the gate's half further** (a self-reported gap on an inbound that reads as a question, never a backstop catch) and leaves the crash card's half at the `anyKnowledgeGapCard` check alone, so the two are no longer the same rule; the whole thing is inert while the holding message is disabled. The realistic pair is a self-reported gap card in the conversation slot and a backstop-flagged comp in the obligation slot; code review caught it before merge. **What that guarantees, and what it does not.** A guest gets one holding message per wait whenever each gap turn can read the card the other wrote. Inside race recovery, each write decides the clock from the last successful slot read, less any card since found gone, so a card an operator handles mid-write takes with it the reason recovery had to withhold the clock. That restores only a clock race recovery withheld. When the GATE withheld it (its own read saw a gap card in the draft's own slot) and that card is handled before the regenerate lands, the card written in its place has no clock: it never sends a holding message, and its label keeps it protected. The crash card has the same gap. Both predate TAC-394 and are recorded under TAC-404. **Two gap turns seconds apart can still send two holding messages:** both reads find no gap card, one draft lands in each slot, the inserts never collide, and each card arms a clock. That needs a grounding-flagged comp and a knowledge gap for one guest within seconds. Migration 020 prevented it only by overwriting one of the two cards, the defect TAC-394 fixed, so it is accepted; a per-guest check in the timeout processor is TAC-404, which also covers the reverse case (an operator handles the card holding the clock before it fires, and a gap card created meanwhile has no clock of its own). **A residual, recorded and not fixed:** a comp the grounding backstop flags, created beside an existing gap card, arms no clock (the other card holds the guest's), and its `review_reason` is `commitment_type_gated`, which outranks the backstop label. `isKnowledgeGapCard` therefore never recognizes it: a same-commitment non-gap turn regenerates it without TAC-308's protection, and it never counts toward the per-guest clock. That is the gap-card predicate's accepted residual (see the `isKnowledgeGapCard` gotcha), reached at creation rather than after the clock fires. The gate reads both slots with `loadPendingRowsBySlot`, which fails OPEN to two empty slots; a card it missed surfaces as a 23505, and race recovery decides with the caller's own policy. A drop found there returns `action: 'dropped'` and is reported exactly like a gate-time drop. `captureDraftDropped` names both commitments and the guest (first name, last four digits of the phone), because the one production instance of two overlapping obligations (2026-08-07) happened mid-incident; the full number never leaves `lib/analytics/posthog.ts`. `draft_queued` gains `slot` and `otherSlotOccupied`. The operator queue gains `QueueDraft.otherPendingDraftsForGuest`, and each card's `recentContext` excludes every pending row (migration 042); the client half is TAC-402, blocked on TAC-395. Until TAC-403 ships in the operator app, a draft push tap opens the guest's oldest pending card rather than the one the push is about (the client matches drafts by `guestId` and ignores the payload's `draftId`); it is a normal build, independent of TAC-395, and does not gate migration 041. `lib/agent/two-pending-slots.test.ts` runs the real gate and persist layer against `lib/agent/testing/pending-rows-fake.ts`, an in-memory `messages` table that returns rows in insertion order (a read that forgot to order or to name its slot is handed the wrong card) and enforces migration 020 or 041.

**Manual followup interaction**: TAC-307 removed the gate bypass, so a manual followup now runs `applyApprovalPolicyStage` like any other and CAN queue. When it does, it takes its slot but never overwrites a card there: `previous_pending_held` does not fire for it, and when its slot is already occupied the gate, and persist race recovery through the `never_regen` policy, refuse it with `slot_occupied` instead of regenerating, and the Command Center route answers 409 with a plain-words detail (TAC-394). When the gate returns `send` — the common case at a venue with no hold configured — behaviour is unchanged from before: `review_state='auto_sent'`, no partial-unique-index conflict, and it can coexist with pending cards on the same guest.

### Follow-up engine (TAC-123, v1.21.0)

Daily per-venue scan that detects which enrolled guests are due for an unprompted touch (post-visit day_N, cold_lapsed re-engagement, perk_unlock), runs Gate 1 (`canSendFollowup`) + the claim-before-dispatch idempotency machinery, and hands off to the existing `handleFollowup` → `applyApprovalPolicyStage` (Gate 2) → dispatch tail. **No fork** of the outbound path. Concrete sibling to TAC-297's commitments processor; both live in their own folders (`lib/followups/` / `lib/guests/commitments-due.ts`) and the shared seam extraction is deferred per design call #3.

**Cron + trigger.** An hourly external cron on cron-job.org hits `/api/cron/followups-due` (TAC-428); the GH Actions workflow `.github/workflows/followups-due-cron.yml` still fires as a redundant net. The route delegates to `processDueFollowups(now)` in `lib/followups/engine.ts`. The per-venue filter (against `followup_rules.cron_hour_local`, default 10) lives in the processor and is **`hour >= cron_hour_local`, not `===`** — any tick from that hour to local midnight dispatches, which is the same-day catch-up. Vercel Hobby still blocks sub-daily Vercel cron. **What makes repeated ticks safe is `weekly_cap`, not the dedup key** — `dedupKeyForReason` embeds the post-visit TIER, which flips at the visit's own 24-hour anniversary, so two ticks either side of it claim two different keys; at a venue with `weekly_cap` above 1 an anniversary day can produce two post-visit follow-ups, which `===` made impossible. Found in code review after the first version of the engine's own comment claimed the dedup key covered it.

**Detectors → reasons[] aggregation.** Three pure detectors in `lib/followups/detectors.ts`:
- `detectPostVisitReason(lastVisitAt, messagingCadence, now)` — highest ENABLED day_N tier the guest has crossed since their last visit. "Highest only" — skipped tiers don't backfill (sending day_1 + day_3 + day_7 at once reads as spam).
- `detectColdLapsedReason(lastVisitAt, currentState, rules, now)` — last visit older than `absence_window_days` AND current state in `lapsed_eligible_states` (default `['regular','raving_fan']` — we don't try to re-engage guests who never engaged).
- `detectPerkUnlockReason({currentState, eligibleMechanics, announcedMechanicIds, rules})` — first eligible mechanic the guest can now unlock that hasn't been announced yet (`announcedMechanicIds` parsed from `followup_log.dedup_key` rows with `perk:` prefix).
The engine aggregates hits into a `FollowupReason[]`, picks the primary via `PRIMARY_REASON_PRIORITY` (`perk_unlock > cold_lapsed > post_visit_day_14 > … > post_visit_day_1`), maps the primary to `FollowupTrigger.reason` (renaming `post_visit_day_N` → `day_N`; `cold_lapsed` / `perk_unlock` pass through), and puts the rest in `trigger.additionalReasons`. For perk_unlock, the chosen mechanic also rides as `trigger.perkMechanic` — `buildAiRuntime` reads it and populates `perkBeingUnlocked` on the AI runtime (first production caller of that AI-runtime field).

**A self-reported visit sets `last_visit_at`, gated by time precision (TAC-377).** Until this ticket `guests.last_visit_at` was written in exactly two places, both Square (`lib/pos/reconcile.ts`, `lib/pos/reconcile-tap.ts`). Le Mil's transactions are `manual` and `guest_reported`, so all six of its guests had `last_visit_at = null` — and since `detectPostVisitReason` and `detectColdLapsedReason` both key on that field, **the engine could only ever fire `perk_unlock` there.** The cron ran hourly, the scan reported success, and no `follow_up` message had ever been sent at that venue. The decision is that a self-report counts: `load-signals.ts` already consumes `guest_reported` transactions for recognition scoring, so excluding them from visit recency alone was an inconsistency, not a policy. TAC-323's write path (`lib/agent/extract-reported-order.ts`) now advances `last_visit_at` after its INSERT succeeds, guarded on the value being newer and mirroring `reconcile.ts`'s log-and-continue on failure.

**Precision is a three-state field and `null` is PERMISSIVE — do not "tidy" that into a stricter default.** `post_visit_day_*` requires the visit to be pinned to a real moment, because a "how was it?" scheduled a day after a visit nobody can place reads as the system inventing the visit. But only an explicit `'approximate'` blocks it:
- `pinned` — a present-tense report (`ReportTiming` from the Haiku extractor) sent while the venue was open. The message IS the receipt.
- `approximate` — any past-tense report, or a present-tense one sent after close. Written to `last_visit_at` all the same, so the guest profile stays honest; it just schedules no post-visit touch.
- `null` — nobody ever recorded a precision. Every row predating migration 036, and every Square write until that path opts in, where the timestamp is a receipt and is as pinned as it gets. Blocking on null would silently switch those off. (Forward-looking rather than a live regression: as of 2026-09-13 only four guests fleet-wide have a non-null `last_visit_at`, all at mock venues.)

`detectColdLapsedReason` deliberately takes NO precision parameter — it fires at 21+ days of silence, where a few hours of drift is noise. The precision value rides on `guests.last_visit_precision`, denormalized alongside `last_visit_at` and written in the SAME UPDATE so the two can never describe different visits; the engine reads it directly in its per-venue guest scan. **That invariant binds ALL THREE writers of `last_visit_at`, and the two Square ones were nearly missed** — `lib/pos/reconcile.ts` and `lib/pos/reconcile-tap.ts` both stamp `'pinned'` (a POS receipt is the most pinned evidence there is). A first version of TAC-377 changed only the `guest_reported` writer while asserting the invariant in three places, which would have left a guest who self-reports once ('approximate') and then becomes a POS regular permanently blocked from `post_visit_*`: the Square path would advance the timestamp past a stale precision, and `extractReportedOrder` disarms after one row so nothing would ever rewrite it. **Any future writer of `last_visit_at` must write the precision in the same statement.** An engine-side join back to `transactions` was rejected — a `cold_lapsed` candidate's anchoring row is 21+ days old, so there is no usable `occurred_at` cutoff to bound the scan.

**Two consequences worth knowing before reading follow-up volume as a bug.** (1) **The ladder fires once per guest, ever.** `extractReportedOrder`'s gate 2 permanently disarms after the first `guest_reported` row for a guest, so `last_visit_at` is written once on this path and then frozen — `post_visit_day_N` runs its course once, and `cold_lapsed` evaluates a date that never advances, so a weekly regular who reported once eventually reads as lapsed. TAC-325 is the fix. (2) **`manual` transactions still write nothing** — they are the bulk of the fleet's rows, and only `guest_reported` got this fix.

**Gate 1 — `canSendFollowup` (`lib/agent/followup-rules.ts`).** Pure function. Suppression order: opt-out → quiet hours (venue-local with midnight-crossing handled; default 21:00–08:00) → recent conversation (`recent_conversation_hours`, default 48) → weekly cap (rolling 7d, default 1; counts engine-initiated only — manual sends from TAC-249 don't count) → time-bound per-reason dedup (`cold_lapsed` only — `cold_dedup_days`, default 30). Intent-bound dedup (don't re-fire post_visit_day_7 for the same `last_visit_at`; don't re-fire perk_unlock for the same mechanic) is NOT here — that's the claim layer's job via the `followup_log.dedup_key` UNIQUE constraint.

**The recent-conversation rule's input is DERIVED, not stored (TAC-476).** `FollowupGuestSnapshot.lastInboundAt` comes from the `venue_guest_activity` RPC, loaded once per venue in the engine's existing `Promise.all` — never from `guests.last_inbound_at`, which records first contact and is dead (see the gotcha). **`canSendFollowup` itself was not touched**: same signature, same logic, same field; only the source moved, which is what kept the fix off both webhook handlers. Two consequences to know. The activity load **fails the venue's scan** rather than degrading, matching the guests and mechanics loads beside it — degrading would treat every guest as never having messaged, which is the failed-open behaviour the ticket replaced, restored silently; no scan means no sends, the safe direction. And **`last_inbound_at` on that RPC is genuinely nullable** (a guest with only outbound rows), while `db/types.ts` types every RPC return column non-null, so the runtime null check in the engine is the only guard and must not be tidied away.

**Suppression DROPS a post-visit follow-up past a tier boundary rather than deferring it (TAC-504, open).** The gate runs before the claim, so no `followup_log` row burns and the reason re-arms next tick — but `detectPostVisitReason` returns only the highest tier crossed, so a guest suppressed on days 1 and 2 gets `day_3` on day 3 and never `day_1`. Latent until TAC-476, because the gate was failing open and suppressing almost nothing.

**Gate 2 — `applyApprovalPolicyStage` (existing, TAC-212).** Engine sends are subject to all the same triggers — voice fidelity floor, model self-flag, comp regex backstop, sticky pending, commitment-type gate. A perk-bearing followup that requires operator approval queues normally; the operator queue UI surfaces it with whatever `primaryTrigger` the gate picked.

**Idempotency — claim-before-side-effect (TAC-123 plan-review).** Beats double-send under overlapping cron runs. Per guest, per run:
1. Engine builds `FollowupClaimRow[]` from detected reasons + their dedup_keys (`day_N:<last_visit_at_iso>` / `cold:<last_visit_at_iso>` / `perk:<mechanic_id>` per `dedupKeyForReason`).
2. `claimFollowupLogRows` atomically INSERTs all rows. UNIQUE conflict on `(venue_id, guest_id, dedup_key)` → entire INSERT rolls back (atomic), helper returns `{conflict: true}`, engine skips this guest.
3. `handleFollowup` dispatches. AgentResult `sent` / `queued` → `finalizeFollowupLogClaim` stamps `message_id`. `refused` / `failed` → `releaseFollowupLogClaim` DELETEs the claim so dedup isn't burned (next morning tick can re-attempt).

**Manual followups bypass the ENGINE entirely, but no longer the GATE.** TAC-249's Command Center button calls `handleFollowup` with `trigger.reason='manual'`; that path skips Gate 1 (`canSendFollowup` lives in the engine, not the orchestrator), doesn't write `followup_log` rows, and doesn't count toward `weekly_cap`. **It DOES run Gate 2 (`applyApprovalPolicyStage`) as of TAC-307** — see "Follow Up button bypass — REMOVED" under *Approval policy gates*.

**`messages.category` on engine sends.** All engine sends persist as `category='follow_up'` regardless of which reasons fire (TAC-123 plan-review call). The perk-weaving clause lives in `lib/ai/prompts/categories/follow-up.ts` and only fires when category is `follow_up`; routing perk-bearing engine runs to `category='perk_unlock'` would mean the clause never applied. The existing `perk_unlock` MessageCategory remains for the inbound / standalone perk moment (different tuning, untouched). `triggerToCategory` in `lib/agent/handle-followup.ts` maps both day_* and `perk_unlock` and `cold_lapsed` to `'follow_up'`.

**Per-venue config — `venue_configs.followup_rules` (migration 028).** Zod schema in `lib/schemas/followup-rules.ts`; default in `FOLLOWUP_RULES_DEFAULT`. Fields: per-reason `enabled` toggles, `absence_window_days`, `lapsed_eligible_states`, `cold_dedup_days`, `weekly_cap`, `recent_conversation_hours`, `quiet_hours_start_local` / `quiet_hours_end_local`, `cron_hour_local`. `parseFollowupRules` is fail-OPEN — null/missing/malformed jsonb returns defaults with a `console.warn` (same posture as `filterActiveContext`). The pre-existing `messaging_cadence` column stays the pure day-schedule (`{day_1, day_3, day_7, day_14}`); the engine reads both.

**Observability.** Two PostHog events in `lib/analytics/posthog.ts`: `followup_suppressed` (per-guest, fires from canSendFollowup blocks; PostHog + Slack relay so pilot ops can chart unexpected spikes) and `followup_scan_complete` (once per processor run, PostHog only; aggregated summary + per-venue breakdown). Both events are leaf — failures swallowed via `capturePostHogEvent`.

**Tunables** are surfaced read-only at `/admin/tunables` via `lib/tunables/manifest.ts` — five `agent_runtime`-category entries (`followup_absence_window_days`, `followup_cold_dedup_days`, `followup_lapsed_eligible_states`, `followup_weekly_cap`, `followup_recent_conversation_hours`) and three `timing`-category entries (`followup_quiet_hours_start_local`, `followup_quiet_hours_end_local`, `followup_cron_hour_local`). All sourced from `FOLLOWUP_RULES_DEFAULT` — runtime reads `venue_configs.followup_rules` per venue and the viewer shows the canonical default.

## Auth boundary (bearer-token path for analog-operator)

The venue-operator path is bearer-token authenticated via `verifyOperatorRequest` (or its `getCurrentOperator` wrapper, or the `withOperatorAuth(handler)` HOF for route handlers). The helper resolves the Supabase auth JWT to our internal `operatorId` plus an `allowedVenueIds` array. Route handlers do venue-mismatch checks themselves (`allowedVenueIds.includes(targetVenueId)`) and choose their response code — by convention `app/api/operator/*` returns 404 (not 403) for out-of-allowlist messages so existence isn't leaked; the helper itself only ever produces 401. RLS is the longer-term defense; the helpers are the v1 enforcement point.

**Status today:** the bearer path is live as of TAC-258 — five route handlers under `app/api/operator/*` (queue / approve / edit / skip / undo) consume `withOperatorAuth`. The `verifyAnalogAdminRequest` variant (bearer + `is_analog_admin = true`) remains forward-scaffolding for the future `analog-operator` admin-only surface. Active admin auth for `app/admin/(authed)/*` uses the cookie-session path via `verifyAnalogAdminAccess(authUserId)`, documented in "Admin scaffold" below. Don't conflate the two — the cookie path is for Analog staff in the Command Center; the bearer path is for venue operators in the mobile app + future dashboard.

### Multi-method auth + linking (TAC-272)

**Schema:** `operators` carries two nullable UUID columns — `auth_user_id_phone` and `auth_user_id_email` — each UNIQUE and FK-by-convention to `auth.users.id`. A CHECK enforces at least one is populated. `phone_number` is NOT NULL going forward. Both the bearer-token path (`verifyOperatorRequest`) and the cookie-session path (`verifyAnalogAdminAccess`) resolve the operator with the same OR-match: `auth_user_id_phone.eq.X OR auth_user_id_email.eq.X` where `X` is the just-verified `auth.uid()`. The RLS policy `operators_select_own` mirrors the OR clause with explicit `IS NOT NULL` guards on each side.

**Linking:** `linkOperatorByAuthUser(authUserId)` in `lib/auth/link-operator.ts` is the single point where an `auth.users` row gets bound to an `operators` row. Flow: `supabase.auth.admin.getUserById` → probe phone-vs-email identity → fast-path OR lookup → match against `operators` by `phone_number = authUserPhoneToE164(auth.users.phone)` OR `email = auth.users.email` → idempotent UPDATE of the appropriate column. Errors-as-values per the `RAGResult` / `AIResult` convention — six failure modes (`auth_user_not_found`, `auth_user_has_no_identity`, `no_matching_operator`, `multiple_matching_operators`, `already_claimed_by_different_user`, `db_error`). Never throws.

**Three call sites for linking:**
- `app/admin/auth/callback/route.ts` (eager) — right after `exchangeCodeForSession`, before the redirect to `/admin`. `no_matching_operator` → redirect with `?error=no_access`; other link failures → `?error=link_failed`.
- `lib/auth/verify-jwt.ts` (lazy) — when the OR-lookup misses, call `linkOperatorByAuthUser` and retry. Self-heals any auth user that authenticated before the callback was wired (and any future "auth-but-no-link" case).
- `lib/auth/verify-analog-admin.ts` (lazy, cookie-session) — same pattern, plus a follow-up `select is_analog_admin where id = operatorId` because the link helper doesn't return the admin flag.

**Phone normalization:** Supabase stores `auth.users.phone` WITHOUT the leading `+` (e.g. `"18777804236"`); `operators.phone_number` stores E.164 WITH `+` (e.g. `"+18777804236"`). `authUserPhoneToE164` in `lib/auth/normalize-phone.ts` bridges them at match time — Supabase manages `auth.users`, so we don't normalize at storage. Idempotent (an input already with `+` returns unchanged), null-safe, whitespace-trimming.

**Studio-only RPC drop (021):** A `link_operator_auth(text, text)` RPC existed in Studio (created during TAC-206) but had zero call sites in app code — orphaned linking infrastructure that never landed a caller. Migration 021 drops it. The TS-side `linkOperatorByAuthUser` is the canonical replacement. **Lesson worth remembering:** when CLAUDE.md flags "some policies may have been added directly in Studio, not via migrations" for RLS, the same risk applies to SQL functions. Audit Studio for both before any migration that touches `operators` (or any other table that's been long-lived enough to accumulate Studio-only objects). **Update (023, TAC-285):** the RPC is re-introduced under the same signature because `analog-operator/lib/auth/operator.ts` calls it post-OTP / magic-link to link the auth user to the operators row. The TS-side helper remains canonical for analog-guest's own surfaces; the RPC is the operator-app surface only. Now versioned via migration 023, not Studio-only.

## Admin scaffold

The Command Center lives at `app/admin/*` inside this repo and is served via a separate Vercel project (`analog-admin`) on `admin.theanalog.company`. Production middleware at `middleware.ts` (root) host-gates: admin host serves only `/admin/*`; guest host 404s `/admin/*`. Local dev (`localhost`/`127.0.0.1`) and `*.vercel.app` previews allow everything for QA.

**Admin API routes live under `/admin/{surface}/api/{thing}`, not `/api/admin/...`.** The host gate above 404s anything not starting with `/admin` on the admin apex. Routes placed at `/api/admin/...` work locally and on `*.vercel.app` previews (which bypass the gate for QA) but 404 in production. Existing pattern to match: `/admin/conversations/api/trace/[traceId]`. Failure signature: route works locally, deploys cleanly, prod fetches return 404 with the correct request URL — first thing to check is whether the path starts with `/admin/`. (THE-203 hotfix #29.)

Auth is magic-link via Supabase (`signInWithOtp`). The protected tree lives under `app/admin/(authed)/` — its layout reads the cookie session via `createServerClient` and calls `verifyAnalogAdminAccess(session.user.id)`. Sign-in (`/admin/sign-in`) and the OAuth callback (`/admin/auth/callback`) are siblings outside the route group so they bypass the gate without redirect loops.

Three states at the gate:
- No session → redirect to `/admin/sign-in`.
- Session, not analog admin → render `<NotAuthorized>` in place (don't redirect; the user has identity, just not authorization).
- Session + analog admin → render `<AdminShell>` (sidebar + topbar + content).

To grant admin access: SQL template under "Common gotchas" (the THE-199 entry).

Brand language is canonical at `docs/brand/style-guide-v01.html`. Fonts load via `next/font/google` in `app/layout.tsx` (Fraunces with `opsz/SOFT/WONK` axes + Inter Tight). Tokens live in `app/globals.css` under `@theme inline` — Tailwind v4, no separate config file. Copy register: **Direct** per the style guide. No emoji, no checkmarks; status indicators use `<StatusDot>`.

**Per-surface palette overrides (TAC-237).** Admin renders on white, not the canonical cream — implemented as a `[data-surface="admin"]` block in `app/globals.css` that re-binds `--paper`, `--parchment`, `--highlight`, and `--stone-light` to a neutral grayscale, scoped via `app/admin/layout.tsx` setting `data-surface="admin"` on its root div. The cascade lets every admin component keep its existing `bg-paper` / `bg-parchment` / `bg-highlight` Tailwind classes unchanged. **Don't mutate `:root` tokens for surface-specific tweaks** — scope them via `[data-surface="..."]` so canonical brand stays canonical and other surfaces (operator dashboard, future repos) can opt into their own palette without drift.

**shadcn/ui component layer (TAC-306).** CC's shared component set is shadcn/ui (Radix + Tailwind, copy-in source we own under `components/ui/*`), themed to the brand — NOT a second palette. The bridge lives in `app/globals.css`:
- **Token bridge.** shadcn's semantic tokens (`--color-background`, `--color-primary`, `--color-muted-foreground`, `--color-border`, `--color-ring`, the `--color-sidebar-*` set, …) are registered in the `@theme inline` block mapped **directly onto the brand source vars** (`var(--paper)`, `var(--clay)`, `var(--ink)`, `var(--stone-light)`, …). Because `@theme inline` inlines the source var into each utility, and the brand vars are re-bound under `[data-surface="admin"]` (TAC-237 above), the shadcn tokens inherit the admin grayscale automatically at every use site in CC. **Keep the mapping aliased to brand vars, not literals** — a literal would freeze the token to cream and break the admin override. The only non-brand literals are `--destructive` (`#DC2626`, matched to `StatusDot` `bad`) and `--radius`, both on `:root`.
- **Named radius scale is intentionally NOT remapped.** Standard shadcn derives `--radius-sm/md/lg/xl` from `--radius` in `@theme`; we omit that so existing surfaces' `rounded-md`/`rounded-lg` don't shift. Vendored components render with Tailwind's default radius scale (acceptable for an internal surface); a future surface PR can revisit if spec-accurate radii are wanted.
- **Admin-scoped border default.** A `@layer base` block pins `border-color: var(--stone-light)` for `[data-surface="admin"] *` because Tailwind v4's bare `border` utility defaults to `currentColor`; shadcn components rely on a `--border` default. Scoped to admin so guest surfaces keep Tailwind's default; every existing CC border already sets an explicit color, so only the new shadcn components are affected.
- **Card.** Exactly one Card component (`@/components/ui/card`). The old `lib/ui/card.tsx` `default` / `trace` variants are reproduced at call sites via className overrides (`block gap-0 rounded-[2px] border-stone-light/60 bg-paper py-0 shadow-none` for default; `rounded-md border-stone-light/60 bg-parchment shadow-none` prefix for trace).
- **Token-resolution guard.** `lib/ui/token-bridge.test.ts` statically parses `globals.css` and fails if any required shadcn token is unbridged or points at an undefined var. Adding a component that references a new token means adding the bridge entry AND the token name to `REQUIRED_SHADCN_TOKENS`.
- **Shell (TAC-306 PR #2).** The CC shell (`app/admin/_components/*`) runs on the shadcn `Sidebar` family (`SidebarProvider` + `Sidebar` `collapsible="icon"` + `SidebarInset`, wired in `admin-shell.tsx`). `app/admin/_components/nav-items.ts` is the **single source of nav truth** (pure data + `isNavItemActive`) consumed by BOTH the sidebar and the ⌘K command palette so they can't drift — add a surface there, not inline. Nav icons live in `sidebar.tsx`'s `NAV_ICONS` (keyed by href) to keep `nav-items.ts` pure/unit-testable (`nav-items.test.ts`). The ⌘K palette is `command-palette.tsx`: a client `CommandPaletteProvider` (owns open state + the global `⌘K`/`Ctrl+K` listener + renders `CommandDialog` once) with a `useCommandPalette()` hook and a `CommandPaletteTrigger` for the top bar; `SidebarProvider` owns the separate `⌘B` collapse. The chrome wraps but never touches the auth gate in `(authed)/layout.tsx`.
- Per the ticket, the foundation (init + token bridge + Card reconcile) ships first; per-surface reskins (shell + ⌘K ✓, conversations, health, tunables, venue-config viewer, voices) are follow-up PRs that wire the installed components.

Magic-link callback URL is constructed from `NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_URL` (per environment) plus a fallback to `NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_URL` so preview deploys self-resolve. Supabase project's "Site URL" + "Redirect URLs" allowlist must include all three: localhost, `*.vercel.app`, and `admin.theanalog.company`. Configure in Supabase Studio.

### Conversations viewer (THE-201)

`/admin/conversations` is the headline debugging surface — single-conversation focus, iMessage-style bubble thread, inline Langfuse trace render. Filters live in the URL (`?venue=&guest=`); reload preserves view, links are shareable.

- **Routing:** server-component page (`page.tsx`) does all initial fetches in one render path. Client component (`conversations-client.tsx`) owns selection, trace cache, Realtime. Pre-filter / venue-only paths render `<EmptyState>` with a 5-row recent-activity list scoped to the operator's `allowedVenueIds`.
- **Bubble palette:** real iMessage colors (#007AFF outbound / #E5E5EA inbound) on a paper-toned background. Inter Tight inside bubbles. Brand discipline yields to fitness-for-purpose on internal surfaces — same logic as health-page status colors.
- **Trace fetch:** server prefetches the last 5 outbound messages' traces in parallel via `lib/observability/fetchTrace`; on-demand fetch for older messages via `app/admin/(authed)/conversations/api/trace/[traceId]/route.ts` (cookie-session auth, never exposes the Langfuse secret key client-side). `Promise.allSettled` so a Langfuse outage doesn't 500 the page.
- **Trace panel shape:** linear stage stack matching the agent pipeline order (`context_build` → `classify` → `retrieve` → `generate` → `send`, with `generate.attempt_N` nested). `lib/select-trace-stages.ts` is the pure projection; unknown observations bucket into "Other" so future stages don't silently disappear before this code is updated.
- **Realtime:** subscribes to `messages` filtered by `venue_id` (single-column server filter), refines by `guest_id` client-side. Uses `lib/db/browser.ts` (browser-side anon Supabase client). Subscribe on mount; tear down on unmount or filter change (filter changes navigate via `router.replace`, which remounts the client component cleanly).
- **Recognition state:** read latest `guest_states` row directly. **Don't** call `computeGuestState` from the page — it's expensive and writes audit rows on transitions.
- **StatusDot mapping for guest state:** `neutral` for `new`, `good` for `returning|regular|raving_fan`. `bad` is reserved for actually-wrong states (failed sends, errors), not "this guest is new."
- **Message window (TAC-316):** newest-200 rows per conversation load — `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 200`, reversed via the projection. Was ASC until TAC-316, which kept the OLDEST 200 and silently hid everything newer once Mock Sextant crossed the cap (the ticket's headline truncation). Older history reachable via TAC-202 (guest detail page) once that ships.
- **Show-everything contract (TAC-316):** the conversation query has NO filter on `status`, `review_state`, or body content — never-sent superseded drafts, pending cards, failed sends, blank knowledge-gap cards, reaction rows, and media rows all render. `app/admin/(authed)/conversations/lib/project-thread.ts` is the pure projection: groups raw rows into RESPONSES by `generation_id ?? id` (keyed-not-adjacent, migration 032 identity — sibling of `lib/agent/group-responses.ts` but viewer-shaped, and unlike the sibling it sorts internally so input order can't silently break it), resolves blank-body placeholders per kind, and derives delivery-state labels via `deriveResponseState` — known combos get friendly labels ("never sent — superseded", "pending review", "failed to send"), **unknown enum values render as literal text** (`status=X · review_state=Y`), never an exhaustive switch. Split responses render as separate chained bubbles sharing ONE selection/trace/review identity keyed on the first bubble's row id. Response-rate stats count dispatched RESPONSES only (`wasDispatched` — consistent with `count_outbound_responses`); never-sent/pending/failed/unknown rows are visible but excluded from stats. Client state is raw rows; the thread derives via `useMemo(projectThread)` so Realtime handlers stay row-grained.
- **Full-width frame (TAC-316):** the admin shell's content frame is `ContentFrame` (`app/admin/_components/content-frame.tsx`) — left-pinned `max-w-5xl` by default, with an explicit `FULL_WIDTH_ROUTES` list (currently `/admin/conversations` only) that drops the cap so the detail panel and context cards flex into the full viewport. Deliberately NOT centered (TAC-316 layout ruling); the thread column stays 400px. New full-width surfaces opt in by adding their route prefix there.
- **Routes:**
  - `GET /admin/conversations/api/trace/[traceId]` — on-demand Langfuse trace fetch (cookie-session auth, server-side secret).
  - `POST /admin/conversations/api/follow-up` — operator-initiated manual outbound. Calls `handleFollowup` with `reason='manual'`; the operator's note becomes a top-level block in the system prompt (THE-232).
  - `PUT /admin/conversations/api/review/[messageId]` — captures per-message review (THE-235); writes `messages.response_review` and mirrors the 08-flow destinations (`voice_corpus` row keyed on `cc-review:{message_id}`, anti-pattern dedupe-append).
  - `DELETE /admin/conversations/api/transactions/[transactionId]` (TAC-323) — the recovery path for a false-positive self-reported order: deletes a `transactions` row, restricted server-side to `source='guest_reported'` (400 for any other source; no editing of items or amounts, delete only). Auth/venue-allowlist pattern mirrors the `review/[messageId]` route above exactly. Deletion needs no separate re-arm flag — `lib/agent/extract-reported-order.ts`'s gate reads the transactions table directly, so the row's absence IS the re-arm.

### Voices command center (THE-237 + THE-238)

`/admin/voices` (list) and `/admin/voices/[slug]` (per-voice workbench) are the surface for refining a venue's agent voice — direct edits to rules, corpus, and persona; threads list + bubble thread + live regen playground; pattern-detection banner in the Rules tab. The flow is: click flagged outbound → type why it's bad → regen → pick the best attempt → commit. Pattern detection surfaces a banner when ≥3 similar edit_only critiques accumulate without promotion.

**Routes** (under `/admin/voices/api/...` per the host-gating convention):
- `PATCH /admin/voices/api/persona/[venueId]` — single writer for all `BrandPersona` fields (voiceName, tone, formality, lengthGuide, emojiPolicy, signaturePhrases, bannedTopics, voiceTouchstones, speakerFraming, speakerName). Anti-patterns are excluded; they have their own endpoints.
- `POST /admin/voices/api/venues/[venueId]/corpus` — ad-hoc corpus add (uses `addCorpusEntry`).
- `PATCH /admin/voices/api/corpus/[entryId]` — content/tags update; re-embeds only on content change.
- `DELETE /admin/voices/api/corpus/[entryId]` — delete + FK-cascade voice_embeddings.
